title: Gate layer encodes known defects as invariants — rebase off derived facts, not hardcoded bounds
description:
WHAT: Sweep the gate layer for assertions that encode a KNOWN DEFECT as an
invariant, so that fixing the defect fails the gate. Rebase each off derived
facts instead of hardcoded bounds. Add a meta-test per gate proving the gate
still trips on the real bad input after the rebase.

WHY: Found 2026-08-14 while teaching module 15 (C5). Module 15 was assessed but
never taught — the fairness defect C5 closed. THREE independent gates had, over
time, written that defect down as a rule:

  - smoke_learn.py          asserted the hub MUST NOT link to module 15
  - smoke_feedback_links.py skipped module > 14 as "no Learn page required"
  - smoke_weak_links.py     REJECTED module 15 keys as "unexpected"

So the correct fix FAILED THREE GATES FOR BEING CORRECT. An agent without the
context to recognise this would read three red gates as three reasons the fix is
wrong, revert, and leave the defect in place with more evidence behind it than
before. That is worse than an ungated defect: the gate layer has become an
immune system attacking the repair.

THE CLASS, which is the point of this bead: a gate written by observing what the
tree currently does will encode the tree's current defects as requirements. The
defect is not "someone hardcoded 14". It is that the assertion was derived from
OBSERVED STATE rather than from a stated contract. Two sibling instances found
the same day, same root cause, unrelated subsystems:

  - smoke_diagrams.py hardcoded PRESENT to the three P0 diagrams, so it reported
    green without looking at four new P1 diagrams. FIXED (derives from
    docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md), 3 -> 7.
  - The migration epic enumerated "17 Python gates" from a remembered count;
    smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py were on the check.sh path and in no
    port bead. FIXED (.19/.20 filed).

Known remaining instances (C5 finding 3), both currently satisfied BY LUCK and
not by gate:
  - scripts/verify_coverage.py  range(1,15)  exempts module 15 from the coverage floor
  - scripts/build_units.py      <= 14        exempts module 15 from the micro-check floor

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify_coverage and build_units derive their module set from the same source
  the bank and Learn index use, not from a literal bound. Module 15 is subject to
  the coverage and micro-check floors, or its exemption is a RECORDED row with a
  reason, never a range literal.
- Each rebased gate ships a known-bad injection proving it still trips, AND a
  known-GOOD leg proving it does not refuse legitimate work.
- A grep for numeric module bounds (14, 15, range(1,15), <= 14) across scripts/
  and crates/ returns either zero hits or hits that are each justified in place.
- Anti-vacuous: zero modules discovered is an ERROR in every rebased gate.
- Meta-test per gate: delete the assertion -> selftest non-zero; restore -> 0.
  True exit codes recorded, never read through a pipe.
close_reason: Closed — open instances 5 -> 0, and the sweep is now COMPILED. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs scans scripts/** and crates/** for hardcoded module bounds and requires every hit to carry a verdict row; 23 inventoried, count pinned so it shrinks deliberately and never grows silently. It caught the controller mid-reconciliation, refusing to record '0 open' while a sixth prose line was uninventoried. domains_listed < 14 was removed with an argument rather than renumbered: once the module set derives from domains.toml the check compares the registry against ITSELF. KNOWN LIMIT, filed as bd-ggs7: the detector keys on NUMERIC bounds, so a hand-frozen module TABLE in smoke_weak_links is invisible to it — '0 open' means 'no numeric bound outside the inventory', not 'nothing hand-frozen'.

title: regen_goldens_after_bank.py manufactures the divergence it is checked against
description:

retired. Today it re-pins every derived digest around FROZEN item_ids.

WHY: Its stated behavior — "does NOT reshuffle mock40 item_ids" — is the exact
mechanism that produced bd-golden-sampler-divergence-09q. Measured 2026-08-14:
goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json could not be reproduced by its own

23/40 different ids, because the bank drifted (fixture bank_fingerprint
0557953e8a49a3cf vs live 5ff22c310349b2bd) while this script froze item_ids and
re-pinned the digests around them. NEITHER implementation reproduced the
committed fixture: it was an orphaned artifact, not a reference.

Post-fix the hazard inverts and gets sharper. cdcp_cli now asserts the fixture
equals cdcp_assemble's output for seed 42. Running this script after a bank edit
re-pins the digests while leaving item_ids stale, which turns that assertion RED
— so the script now MANUFACTURES the divergence its own output is checked
against. A repair tool that reintroduces the fault is worse than no tool,
because it is reached for precisely when someone is trying to fix things.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either: the script regenerates item_ids via `cdcp goldens fixture` (which calls
  cdcp_assemble) before re-pinning any derived digest; or it is deleted and its
  substrate_allowlist row is deleted in the same commit.
- If retained: running it after a bank edit leaves `cargo test -p cdcp_cli`
  GREEN. Prove it — edit a bank item, run the script, run the test, record the
  true exit code.
- Anti-vacuous: a run that regenerates zero goldens is an ERROR, not a pass.
- goldens/PROVENANCE.md states which command is authoritative and which is not.
close_reason: Closed by DELETION, with the argument. It was not a stale-item_ids bug in a working tool: measured on a PRISTINE bank with zero edits it exited 0 printing 'ok' while writing bank_hash af6f14fa… against the Rust law's e8281757…. Three divergent re-implementations of three shipped algorithms, all drifted. grep -c status = 0 — it never read the C1 approved-only field, so 804 items / 0 approved would still have printed ok. Its allowlist reason claimed 'its output is gated by the Rust goldens check' while it wrote both the digests AND the pin that check compares against: it graded its own homework, and the exemption's stated reason was the cover. Repair was rejected because it meant shelling out to three cargo commands — a fourth name for a procedure that already has one, in the substrate we are migrating off. Script and allowlist row deleted together; the guard verified the coupling by erroring on the orphaned row.

title: Flip ported gates from oracle exit codes to cdcp_gate 0/2/3/4 — one commit, after the oracles die
description:
WHAT: After every port lands and the Python oracles are deleted, flip all ported
gates from the oracle's exit codes to cdcp_gate's convention in ONE commit:
0 ok / 2 violation / 3 usage / 4 error. Update crate::exit's doc, check.sh, and
every selftest that asserts a specific code.

WHY: A real fork, raised by the verify_orphans port agent 2026-08-14 rather than
resolved silently — which is why this bead exists instead of a surprise.

crate::exit states "every ported gate returns these and only these" (0/2/3/4).
scripts/verify_orphans.py exits 1 on failure and writes nothing to stderr. Those
cannot both hold. Routing a port through GateError changes the exit code AND adds
a stderr line on every RED, so the differential test — the only mechanism that
can tell a port BUG from an intended FIX — would fail on every red case for
reasons that have nothing to do with the port's correctness.

DECISION (controller, 2026-08-14): byte-exactness wins DURING the migration.
Ported gates reproduce the oracle's exit code, including `std::process::exit(1)`,
and document the departure in the module header. This is safe downstream because
check.sh invokes every gate as `cmd || fail "..."`, which distinguishes only zero
from non-zero; no caller reads the specific code today. Verified before deciding.

The convention is not being abandoned, it is being SEQUENCED. Once an oracle is
deleted there is nothing left to be byte-exact against, and the code becomes free.
Doing it per-gate as each port lands would leave the crate in a mixed state where
a reader cannot tell which convention a given gate follows — worse than either
convention consistently applied.

RISK IF THIS BEAD IS LOST: the crate ships with cdcp_gate's own guard on 0/2/4
and its ported gates on 0/1, with a doc comment asserting a uniformity that does
not hold. That is a false statement in the substrate, and the kind a reader stops
checking. This bead is the reason the departure is temporary rather than a lie.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Blocked until every bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.N port is closed AND its
  oracle .py is deleted with its allowlist row.
- One commit flips all gates; no mixed state is ever committed.
- crate::exit's doc comment matches reality at every commit in between — if the
  mixed state persists, the doc says so explicitly with a pointer to this bead.
- Every selftest asserting a numeric exit code is updated in the same commit.
- Anti-vacuous: a gate returning 0 on an input it could not evaluate is an ERROR
  (4), never a pass, under the new convention.
- Meta-test: a gate forced to violate returns exactly 2; forced to error, 4.

    elif "id" in data: ...
    else: errors.append(f"{path.name}: no id or items[]")

The `elif` never runs for an empty list, so the else-branch that would have
caught it never runs either. Verified empirically: dropping `items = []` into the
specimen bank leaves BOTH implementations at PASS, items=804, rc=0, byte-identical.

This is decalogue rule 3 — "an empty input set is an ERROR, never a pass" —
violated at FILE granularity while the script's own docstring asserts it at
WHOLE-BANK granularity. That gap is the whole defect: a file that was never
really checked reports exactly like one that passed, and the aggregate count
still looks healthy because 804 other items carried it.

Fixed in the Python FIRST, not the Rust, so the differential test keeps working:
change the oracle, watch diff_verify_orphans.rs go RED, then change the port to
match. Fixing the Rust first would make the port non-byte-exact and the test
would flag the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A bank file yielding zero items is reported by name and is non-zero exit.
- Known-bad: `items = []` planted in the live bank -> RED, names the file.
- Known-GOOD: a legitimate single-item file (`id = ...` form, no `items` key)
  still passes — the elif branch must not be broken by the fix.
- diff_verify_orphans.rs updated in the SAME commit; its KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT
  comment is deleted, not amended, because the defect is gone.
- Meta-test: delete the new assertion -> non-zero; restore -> 0. True exit codes.
close_reason: Fixed for verify_orphans, Python first, Rust matched, byte-identical. Controller-verified: a planted 'items = []' beside an 804-item bank is now named and RED in both implementations; before, both reported PASS / items=804 with zero mentions of the file. The KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT pin was DELETED, not amended. NOTE: this closed ONE of FOUR instances — verify_coverage, verify_bank and verify_objectives carried it identically and were closed under bd-0czh, which also added a scan test that parses branches rather than grepping messages.

comments.author: josh

Measured after the close: verify_coverage.py, verify_bank.py and verify_objectives.py carry the byte-identical  fail-open. Only verify_orphans.py (this bead) is fixed. Filed as a class sweep with the ordering and message-text reuse specified.

title: Drift guard has three holes — word-spelled counts invisible, wrong file reported, --require double-counts
description:
WHAT: Close three holes in verify_injection_count.py — the DRIFT GUARD itself.
Found 2026-08-14 by its port agent, reproduced faithfully rather than fixed.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this gate is what stops the L4
"gates proven to trip" claim from decaying. It sums the known-bad injections
actually executed and compares them against the number the README advertises.
A hole in the drift guard is a hole in the mechanism that detects every other
hole — the top of the certificate chain.

HOLE 1 — a count spelled in WORDS is invisible.
`_SUITE_COUNT` understands "one".."twelve"; the injection-count regex requires
`\d+`. Rewrite the README badge as "thirty-six known-bad injections" and that
check silently stops covering it. Note the shape carefully: if EVERY digit form
disappears you get "advertises no count at all" -> ERROR, so it fails closed at
the extreme. THE DANGEROUS CASE IS THE MIDDLE — a README where one of the four
advertisement sites is prose. That site just stops being checked, and the gate
stays green because the other three still parse. A partial loss of coverage that
reports identically to full coverage is the exact fooled-certificate shape.

HOLE 2 — findings hardcode `README.md:<lineno>` regardless of `--readme`.
Inside selftest_injection_count.sh this prints `README.md:3` while the file
actually under test is README_off.md. A gate that misreports WHERE the defect is
sends the next reader to an innocent file.

HOLE 3 — a suite named twice in `--require` double-counts.
`total = sum(counts.get(s, 0) for s in required)` iterates `required`, which is
`args.require.split(",")` with no dedup. `--require alpha,alpha` where alpha
reports 3 yields measured_total=6 and registered_suites=2, and prints the suite
row twice. NOT reachable from check.sh (its default roster has no duplicates) but
reachable by any other caller — and inflating measured_total is the direction
that turns a real drift GREEN. A repeated identical receipt LINE does not
double-count (dict assignment overwrites); that asymmetry is pinned by a test.

RELATED, do not fix here but read together: the README "36 injections" badge
counts shell-selftest receipts only. The Rust known-bad legs added 2026-08-14
(6 in cdcp_gate, more per port) are not in that ledger by design. So the
advertised number is drifting from the real injection count for a reason the
gate cannot see. Deciding what the badge is supposed to count is a prerequisite
to fixing hole 1 — otherwise you harden the parser around a number that is
already wrong.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_injection_count.rs go RED, then change the
port to match. Fixing the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the
differential test flags the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide and RECORD what the injections badge counts (shell receipts only, or
  shell + Rust known-bad legs). The number is regenerated, never hand-maintained.
- Word-spelled counts either parse, or a non-digit count at any advertisement
  site is itself an ERROR. Silent non-coverage is not an option.
- Findings report the file actually scanned, not a hardcoded README.md.
- `--require` dedups, or a duplicate entry is a usage ERROR.
- Known-bad per hole: badge in words -> RED; `--readme X` reporting a path other
  than X -> RED; `--require a,a` -> RED or usage error.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all three fixes.
- Meta-test, stated correctly: MUTATE the gate, confirm the diff test trips, then
  delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm it passes.
  Deleting an assertion on an unmutated tree proves nothing.
close_reason: All three holes closed. Word-spelled counts now parse, plus MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES catches a site dropping out any other way; findings name the file actually scanned; a suite named twice in --require is an ERROR rather than a silent double-count. The agent REJECTED the controller's proposed 'non-digit count is an ERROR' rule after measuring it against the live README, where it fires on innocent prose and would be edited away — an over-strict gate gets routed around, a slower death than no gate. Badge decision recorded: shell receipts only, because Rust legs emit no receipt and hand-typing the number is the defect this gate removes. Advertised total is now REGENERATED (36 -> 47) and the per-suite counts are COMPUTED, not literals.

comments.author: bd-wf2 agent
comments.text:
DECISION (prerequisite) — what the injections badge counts.

The badge counts SHELL-SELFTEST RECEIPTS ONLY: the sum of `INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>`
lines emitted by the registered scripts/selftest_*.sh suites during a real check.sh run.
The Rust known-bad legs (cdcp_gate #[cfg(test)] cases, and the per-port ones landing this
wave) are NOT in the total.

Reasoning:
1. They emit no receipt. cargo test reports pass/fail, not a count, so there is nothing for
   check.sh to tee into INJ_LOG and nothing for this gate to sum. Including them means
   hand-typing a number somewhere — which is the exact defect this gate exists to remove.
2. Their count is internal to a test binary's own accounting, which the gate cannot observe.
   A Rust leg that silently stopped asserting would be invisible here WHILE inflating the
   advertised number: a fooled certificate on the certificate-checker.
3. Consequence stated honestly rather than hidden: the advertised number is a FLOOR on the
   repo's known-bad population, not its total. README now names the population on the two
   sites that explain it ("shell suites only; the Rust ports' own known-bad cases emit no
   INJECTIONS= receipt, so they are not in this total").
4. Folding them in later is a MECHANISM change, not a number change: the Rust legs must first
   emit receipts that check.sh aggregates and be registered in REGISTERED_SUITES. Until then,
   counting them would be a claim with no receipt behind it.

Recorded in scripts/verify_injection_count.py (module docstring, "WHAT THE ADVERTISED NUMBER
COUNTS"), crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_injection_count.rs (module header), and the two
README advertisement lines.

The number is now REGENERATED, not hand-typed: `--write-readme` rewrites every advertisement
site from the receipts actually collected, and refuses to write when the receipts are unsound
(missing/zero/unregistered suite, empty or missing log), so a bogus log cannot launder a wrong
number into README. Verified idempotent on the live tree: "5 site(s) already advertise 36",
README md5 unchanged.

comments.author: bd-wf2 agent
comments.text:
FIXES + EVIDENCE (ordering honoured: Python first, differential RED, then Rust).

HOLE 1 — word-spelled counts invisible. FIXED by parsing, not by erroring.
  The count token in both scanners is now `(\d+|\b(?:<english cardinal zero..ninety-nine>))`,
  hyphen and space compounds included, alternation ordered longest-first then lexicographic so
  the Rust port can rebuild the identical leftmost-first order. The `\b` guards the WORD branch
  only, so "v1.7 injections" still reads 7 while "eight" inside "freighter" does not.
  Erroring on any non-digit count was REJECTED after measurement: the live README contains
  "the known-bad injection alongside the feature" and "injections it *observed* go RED", so an
  error-on-prose rule fires on innocent lines and the gate would be edited to shut it up.
  SECOND DEFENCE for the dangerous middle case the bead names: MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES = 5 is a
  floor on how many sites must parse. The live README advertises at exactly 5 sites, and the

title: Three gates print PASS then crash — verdict emitted before a path that can still raise
description:
WHAT: Three gates print PASS (or most of a PASS report) to stdout and THEN die
with an uncaught exception. Make each fail closed BEFORE emitting a verdict.

WHY: A verdict followed by a crash is the worst possible output shape. A reader
skimming stdout sees PASS; CI sees non-zero; the two disagree, and which one wins
depends on whether anyone looked. Worse, any consumer that greps stdout for PASS
— including a human — gets the wrong answer from a gate that actually failed.
All three found 2026-08-14 by port agents, reproduced faithfully rather than
fixed, and pinned in the differential tests.

1. verify_doc_consistency.py — RAGGED ROW. `parse_doc` falls back to the
   heading's status when a data row has fewer cells than the Status column. If
   the heading is not itself a status word the fallback is None, the row is
   recorded with status=None and NO error, and main() then hits
       seen = ",".join(sorted({r["status"] for r in rows}))
   -> TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, NoneType found
   AFTER printing PASS and most of the summary. Trigger: `| M2 | ragged row |`
   under a non-status heading such as `## Notes on the waves`.
   OPEN DECISION for whoever fixes it: status=None should almost certainly be
   fail-closed ("row is shorter than its Status column") rather than rendered as
   the string None. That is a behaviour change, which is why it was not made.

2. verify_bank.py — ZERO EXAM SIZE. `exam_n_items = 0` silently falls back to 40
   because `or` treats 0 as falsy. `exam_n_items = "0"` instead reaches n/exam_n
   and raises ZeroDivisionError after printing three lines of a PASS report. Two
   spellings of the same value, two different wrong behaviours, neither an error.

3. verify_content_lock.py — two uncaught paths: the bank-hash subprocess exits 0
   with output that strips empty, so the oracle does [][-1] -> IndexError; and
   subprocess timeout=300 -> TimeoutExpired.

ALSO IN verify_bank.py, a latent nondeterminism worth fixing in the same pass:
`ALLOWED_CORRECT` is a frozenset and the diversity loop iterates it, so emission
order is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent. Harmless TODAY only because two letters cannot
both exceed 70% (they would sum past 140%), so at most one line is ever emitted.
Lower that threshold below 50% and the gate's output becomes nondeterministic
run to run — which would silently break every byte-exact differential test built
against it. The Rust ports iterate A-D and document why that is currently
equivalent.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch the corresponding
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs go RED, then change the port to match. Fixing
the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the differential test flags the
FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No gate emits PASS on stdout before a path that can still raise. Verdict is the
  LAST thing written, or it is not written.
- Known-bad per defect: ragged row -> RED naming the row; exam_n_items = "0" and
  = 0 -> both RED or both defaulted, consistently and stated; empty subprocess
  output -> ERROR not IndexError.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all fixes.
- ALLOWED_CORRECT iterated in a fixed order; a test pins the order.
- The diff_*.rs tests pinning each defect are DELETED (not amended) as each is
  fixed — the pin exists to make the repair deliberate, not permanent.
- Meta-test as the CHARTER now defines it: MUTATE the gate, confirm the suite
  trips, then delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm
  it passes. True exit codes, never read through a pipe.
close_reason: All three shares fixed, each Python-first with the port matched byte-identically. verify_doc_consistency: the fix separates a TABLE-level status declaration (heading-supplied, legitimate) from a ROW-level shortfall, and Row::status is now &'static str so an absent status is structurally inexpressible. Second defect inside the first: milestone_rows fell 6 -> 3 because unread rows had been counting toward the anti-vacuous counter — the gate reported having read rows it could not read. verify_bank: policy_positive_int, both zero spellings fail closed. verify_content_lock: empty subprocess output and timeout are typed errors.

title: content.lock gate has no tree-side walk — deleting a row silently stops checking that file
description:
WHAT: verify_content_lock.py has NO tree-side walk. It enumerates only rows
already in content.lock, so a file that is never listed is never checked, and
DELETING a row silently stops checking that file. Add a tree-side sweep, or
state the hole in the gate's own output rather than only in a header comment.

WHY: Confirmed empirically 2026-08-14 by the port agent, both directions:
  - Planted knowledge/smuggled_policy.toml and modules/99-smuggled.md. Both
    implementations exit 0 with `knowledge=9 modules=31` UNCHANGED.
  - Deleted the content.lock row for knowledge/claims.toml, then CORRUPTED that
    file. Both sides stayed GREEN. The only tell was the count moving to
    `knowledge=8` — a number nobody is asserting against anything.

The second direction is the dangerous one and it is the exact fooled-certificate
shape: the gate's coverage is defined by the artifact the gate is checking, so an
attacker (or an ordinary careless commit) removes coverage and the removal looks
identical to a pass. This is L7's content lock — the constellation.lock pattern —
whose entire purpose is "the pinned content still matches". A pin you can delete
without the gate noticing is not a pin.

Note the count IS emitted (`knowledge=9 modules=31`), so the information needed
to catch this is already on stdout. Nothing asserts against it. That is the
cheapest possible first fix: pin the expected counts, so a row deletion is RED.
The fuller fix is a tree-side walk with an explicit ignore list.

RELATED, same class, found the same day: scripts/verify_bank.py and
scripts/verify_knowledge_paths.py both have vacuity holes where zero-checked
reports identically to all-checked (see bd-...-jhd.5's report: a registry whose
every row is a licensed empty prints PASS / primary_notes_checked=0).

ACCEPTANCE:
- A file present under a locked root but absent from content.lock is RED, or the
  gate's OUTPUT states which roots it does not cover. A header comment is not
  sufficient — the reader of a green verdict must be told what it does not mean.
- Deleting a content.lock row is RED. Known-bad: delete the claims.toml row ->
  non-zero.
- Anti-vacuous: zero rows, or zero files discovered under a locked root, is an
  ERROR, never a pass.
- The two tests currently pinning these holes as agreed behaviour
  (`an_unlisted_file_slips_past_both_implementations`,
  `deleting_a_row_silently_stops_checking_that_file_in_both`) are DELETED in the
  same commit, because the behaviour they pin will no longer exist.
- Python first, then the port — the differential test must flag the port, not the fix.
close_reason: Fixed. content.lock now walks the three roots gen_content_lock.py writes rows from, so a regenerated lock is green by construction and any divergence is a real unpinned file. Both directions verified: a planted unlisted file is RED, and DELETING a row no longer silently stops checking that file. GREEN output now states its own scope on stdout — covered roots with counts, and an explicit NOT-covered list — so a green verdict tells the reader what it does not mean. Also wired CDCP_CONTENT_LOCK_SELFTEST, an L4 gate-proven-to-trip leg that existed fully implemented on both sides and that nothing ran. Stated limit, not closed: the walk is one level deep, so knowledge/corpus/x.toml is invisible to both generator and gate — tracked in bd-zhnd.

title: cargo fmt cannot see src/gates/*.rs — audit which other tools stop at the #[path] boundary
description:
WHAT: `cargo fmt --check` cannot see crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs. Decide
whether the glob-based gate registration keeps its `#[path]` indirection (and
check.sh keeps the compensating per-file rustfmt leg added 2026-08-14), or
whether registration changes shape so cargo's own tooling reaches the files.

WHY: The gate modules are pulled in by `#[path = ...]` from a build.rs-generated
OUT_DIR file. `cargo fmt` walks the module tree from src/lib.rs and never
resolves that indirection, so it silently formats and checks NOTHING under
src/gates/.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, not inferred:
  - substrate_guard.rs deliberately misformatted -> `cargo fmt --check` exit 0,
    zero output. `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` on the same file -> exit 1,
    47-line diff.
  - Sweeping all nine gate files with rustfmt found THREE genuinely unformatted:
    install_hooks.rs, substrate_guard.rs, verify_orphans.rs. Two of those were
    already committed in 27a0c2d. They had never been checked by anything.
  - The five port agents that used per-file `rustfmt --check` were clean. The
    ones that relied on `cargo fmt` were not. The tool was the difference.

THIS IS THE COST OF THE PARALLELISM, AND THAT TRADE SHOULD BE MADE DELIBERATELY.
The glob registration is what lets N port agents each add exactly one file with
zero shared-file collisions — verified working under SIX concurrent agents, and
it is the reason 19 ports are parallelisable at all. It is worth keeping. But it
created an unchecked surface, and a green fmt leg over files it never opened is
the same vacuous-scan pattern check.sh hard-fails on everywhere else. The bug is
not that cargo fmt is wrong; it is that we adopted an indirection without
auditing which tools stop working across it.

MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED: check.sh now runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` per
file over the glob, with an anti-vacuous floor (zero gate files scanned = ERROR).
Proven to trip: misformatted gate -> exit 2 naming the file; empty glob -> exit 2.
That closes fmt specifically. This bead exists because fmt is unlikely to be the
only tool that cannot cross a `#[path]`/OUT_DIR boundary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Enumerate every tool in the chain that walks the module tree rather than the
  filesystem, and state for each whether it reaches src/gates/*.rs. At minimum:
  cargo fmt, clippy, rustdoc, cargo-mutants, tarpaulin/llvm-cov, cargo-udeps.
  `clippy --all-targets` is believed to reach them because it compiles; CONFIRM
  that by misformatting-equivalent injection, do not assume it.
- For each tool that does NOT reach them, either a compensating per-file leg with
  an anti-vacuous floor, or a recorded decision that the tool is not required.
- A meta-test per compensating leg: it trips on a known-bad file AND errors on an
  empty glob.
- If the decision is to change registration shape instead, the six-way-concurrent
  no-collision property must be preserved and re-demonstrated, not assumed.

title: SEV-0: guard reads paths from the index but the allowlist from the worktree — a commit is approved against a tree that never exists
description:
WHAT: The commit-time leg reads candidate paths from the git INDEX but reads
registries/substrate_allowlist.toml from the WORKING TREE. Read the allowlist
from the index too (`git show :registries/substrate_allowlist.toml`) whenever the
paths came from the index, so a commit is judged against the tree it creates.

WHY: CONFIRMED BY INJECTION 2026-08-14 (adversarial review, then reproduced by
the controller against a throwaway index):

    printf 'print("payload")\n' > scripts/payload.py
    git add scripts/payload.py
    # append a valid [[allow]] row for it, and do NOT git add the allowlist
    cdcp_gate substrate-guard            -> EXIT 0
    cdcp_gate substrate-guard --staged   -> EXIT 0

The resulting commit contains scripts/payload.py and does NOT contain the row
that authorised it. The guard approved a tree that has never existed and will
never exist. The next run on a clean checkout would flag the file — but the
commit is already in history, and in a public repo that is the part that matters.

The general shape, which is worth stating because it will recur: a gate that
mixes two sources of truth (index for the subject, worktree for the policy) is
judging a hybrid state that no commit ever has. Both halves must come from the
same snapshot.

RELATED, same root cause, same fix: the hook likewise evaluates the WORKTREE
copies of scripts/check.sh and the gate sources while committing possibly
neutered STAGED versions of them. So the BUILT != WIRED detector can read a
correctly-wired check.sh while the commit removes the wiring.

ACCEPTANCE:
- When candidates come from the index, the allowlist and check.sh are read from
  the index at the same revision. If a file is absent from the index, that is an
  ERROR (the commit deletes the policy), never a pass.
- Known-bad: the exact reproduction above -> exit 2 naming scripts/payload.py.
- Known-bad: stage a check.sh with the substrate-guard step deleted while the
  worktree copy still has it -> RED.
- Known-GOOD: staging the file AND its row together -> 0. This is the normal
  workflow and must not become harder.
- Anti-vacuous: an index with zero entries is an ERROR.
- Meta-test: mutate the index-reading path, confirm the suite trips; then delete
  the assertion with the mutation in place and confirm it passes.
close_reason: Closed in tick 5 (ef83759), re-verified by the controller before closing. ONE SNAPSHOT PER VERDICT: the guard read candidate paths from the git INDEX and the allowlist from the WORKING TREE, so a staged .py with an unstaged [[allow]] row returned 0 on both legs — approving a tree that had never existed. Re-verified 2026-08-14 against a throwaway index: same injection now exits 2 with 'staged snapshot (the tree this commit creates) — scripts/payload.py'. Both snapshots are read and both must be clean, each internally consistent, so staging a script WITH its row passes and deleting a script WITH its row passes — proven again during the regen_goldens deletion, where the exemption count read 42 from the index until both halves were staged together, then 41. A policy file missing from the index is an ERROR. Graded: acceptance met.

title: SEV-0: wiring detector accepts inert shell — ': "cargo run ..."' and '|| true' both certify wired=yes
description:
WHAT: `check_sh_wires_guard()` decides "wired" by looking for a line containing
both "cdcp_gate" and the gate NAME, excluding comment/echo/ok lines. That admits
inert shell. Require evidence the step actually EXECUTES and that its failure
propagates.

WHY: CONFIRMED BY INJECTION 2026-08-14. Replacing the real call in check.sh with

    : "cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard"   # inert no-op

leaves the guard reporting `wired=yes` at exit 0. The `:` builtin does nothing.
These also certify:

    true # cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard || true      # failure swallowed

The last one is the nastiest: the gate genuinely runs, and its verdict is
discarded. "Wired" currently means "a string appears", not "a failure stops the
build" — which is the only property anyone cares about.

Two more holes in the same block:
- `[wiring].status` may be set back to "pending" after having been "wired". A
  gate that can be un-wired by editing one word is not ratcheted.
- `check_sh` is not pinned to scripts/check.sh. Point it at any file containing a
  suitable inert string and wiring is satisfied.

ACKNOWLEDGED DESIGN LIMIT: no substring test can prove a shell line executes.
The honest fix is not a better regex — it is to stop asking check.sh's TEXT and
start asking its BEHAVIOUR. Prefer: a selftest that runs check.sh against a
planted unlisted .py and asserts check.sh itself exits non-zero. That is a
behavioural assertion and it cannot be satisfied by an inert line.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Wiring is established by RUNNING check.sh against a planted known-bad and
  observing a non-zero exit, not by scanning its text.
- Known-bad: each of the three inert forms above -> RED.
- Known-bad: `[wiring].status` moved "wired" -> "pending" while the step is
  absent -> RED (ratchet, not a toggle).
- Known-bad: check_sh pointed at a file other than scripts/check.sh -> ERROR.
- Known-GOOD: the real check.sh -> 0.
- Meta-test: mutate the behavioural assertion, confirm the suite trips.
close_reason: Closed in tick 5 (ef83759), re-verified by the controller before closing. The text leg was a substring test, so ': "cargo run ..."', 'true # ...' and 'cargo run ... || true' all certified wired=yes — the third runs the gate and discards its verdict. No text test can fix this, so the text leg is DEMOTED: it subtracts, reporting ABSENT/INERT/UNPROVEN, and never says wired. Proof lives in --prove-wired, which materialises the INDEX, plants an unlisted .py, runs check.sh for real and requires check.sh ITSELF to exit non-zero. Re-verified 2026-08-14 against a throwaway index: '|| true' -> exit 2 'discards its verdict' (caught by check.sh reporting a later step ok AFTER the guard had failed); ': "..."' -> exit 2 'never invoked'; the real check.sh -> exit 0, child transcript ending in 'check.sh: FAIL: substrate guard'. The architecture is confirmed by its own meta-test: under a mutation restoring substring semantics the behavioural probe STILL PASSED — it does not depend on the text leg. status is now a ratchet and check_sh is pinned. NOTE for the reader: plain 'substrate-guard' exits 0 on an inert form BY DESIGN; that is the demotion working, not a residual bypass. My own first re-verification targeted that leg and misread the 0. Graded: acceptance met.

title: Substrate floor is a filename policy on one commit path — .PY, shebang-only, docs/, merge/rebase/cherry-pick, commit-tree, fresh clones all bypass
description:
WHAT: The substrate floor is a FILENAME policy, not a "non-Rust source" policy,
and pre-commit is not the only way a commit is created. Decide the real scope and
close the gaps, or state the narrowed claim everywhere the broad one is written.

WHY: adversarial review 2026-08-14, every item below confirmed by injection.

SCOPE GAPS (all returned exit 0 while staged):
    scripts/payload.PY          uppercase extension
    scripts/payload             no extension, `#!/usr/bin/env python3`
    scripts/payload.bash        another shell extension
    docs/payload.py             outside scan.roots
Also already outside the floor at 27a0c2d, four real shell files:
    .flywheel/scripts/publishability-bar.sh · .flywheel/watchdog.sh
    tests/publishability-bar.sh · tests/voice-slop.sh
A directory symlink or submodule is opaque the same way — git reports the link,
not the .py files beneath it.

COMMIT-PATH GAPS: only `pre-commit` is installed. Git runs different hooks for
merge (`pre-merge-commit`), rebase (`pre-rebase`), and `git am`
(`pre-applypatch`), and the sequencer does not fire `pre-commit` for ordinary
cherry-pick/rebase commits. Plumbing bypasses hooks entirely:
    git commit-tree $(git write-tree) -p HEAD -m payload
`core.hooksPath=/dev/null` redirects hook lookup away from the installed shim.
And hooks are NEVER CLONED: a fresh clone has no hook at all, the committed shim
is mode 100644, and nothing installs it before the first ordinary commit. The CI
workflow checks out fresh and runs check.sh but never runs install-hooks — so
`install-hooks --check` should be RED in CI today.

IT ALSO DOES NOT FAIL `cargo build`. Neither `cargo build --workspace` nor
`cargo test --workspace` runs the repository presence scan; only check.sh does.
"Fails the build" is therefore true only of one shell orchestrator.

THE HONEST FRAMING, which is the real deliverable here: this gate raises the cost
of CASUALLY adding a .py/.sh through the ordinary `git commit` path in a clone
where the hook is installed. It is not, and given hooks-are-advisory cannot be, a
containment boundary against someone who does not want to be stopped. Server-side
enforcement (a CI job on the pushed ref, or a pre-receive hook) is the only place
a real boundary can live. Say that in the header instead of implying more.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision on scope: extensions case-insensitive? shebang sniffing?
  roots = whole repo minus an ignore list? Each choice recorded with its reason.
- Whatever is decided, a known-bad per bypass class that currently passes.
- CI runs `install-hooks` (or the equivalent) so a fresh clone is guarded, and
  `install-hooks --check` is green in CI rather than vacuously unrun.
- A server-side check on the pushed ref, or a written decision that we accept
  client-side-only and why.
- The gate header and every commit message stop saying "fails the build and is
  refused at commit" and say what is actually enforced, where.
close_reason:
CLOSED for the classes in scope; three deferred with reproductions. Every class was measured against the built binary in a throwaway clone, never the live index.

REAL AND NOW CLOSED (each was exit 0 before, exit 2 after): case-varied extensions (.PY/.Py/.pY); extensionless files carrying a python shebang; the wider shell family (.bash/.zsh/.ksh/.pyw); scripts anywhere outside scripts/ and crates/ (docs/, tests/, .flywheel/, web/); directory symlinks pointing outside the tree with a .py readable through them; submodule gitlinks. Scope is now the whole engine tree, extensions are case-insensitive over the shell+python family, plus a shebang leg and symlink/gitlink identification. Allowlist 41 -> 46 rows, with identified_non_rust == exemptions asserted.

THE BEAD UNDERSTATED ONE THING: four shell files lived outside the floor, and TWO OF THEM ARE INVOKED AS GATES BY check.sh (tests/voice-slop.sh, tests/publishability-bar.sh). The floor did not cover two of the repo's own gates.

THE BEAD OVERSTATED ONE THING, and the agent said so rather than accepting the framing: merge / cherry-pick / rebase / git am / commit-tree / --no-verify / core.hooksPath=/dev/null all bypass the HOOK, but every one was then caught by the presence leg at exit 2. That is delayed detection, not invisibility. Deferred as bd-efm7 with the reproduction, correctly reframed.

DEFERRED WITH REPRODUCTIONS: bd-efm7 (commit paths, no server-side boundary), bd-m67m (P0 — a fresh clone has no hook, CI is a fresh clone, so install-hooks --check was RED on every CI run and green on every developer machine; the install step is now wired ahead of it in check.sh), bd-yp9x (four scripts/*.mjs node gates on the check.sh path; js/mjs deliberately outside the floor).

INCIDENTAL FINDING WORTH KEEPING: the agent's first case-folding mutation returned exit 0, revealing that has_scanned_extension's eq_ignore_ascii_case is redundant defence behind extension_of's lowercasing. Kept, but the meta-test pair was re-aimed at the live mechanism — a mutation that cannot fail proves nothing.

comments.text:

title: smoke_diagrams: a registry row can point at the registry itself — deriving fixed WHICH items, not HOW they are checked
description:
WHAT: smoke_diagrams' registry-derived check selects rows by regex and then
trusts whatever path the row names. Bind the row to the artifact.

WHY: confirmed by injection 2026-08-14, after the derive-from-registry fix that
was itself meant to close a hardcoding hole. Point a row at the registry document
itself:

  | `fire-sequence` | ... | P1 | **present** | `docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md` |

The file exists, and it contains the substrings "not", "certif", and
"fire-sequence" — so every predicate passes and web/diagrams/fire-sequence.html
is never opened. Measured: exit 0, "PASS (7 present diagrams from the registry)".

Three more, same shape:
- Status spelled `shipped` instead of `**present**` silently drops that one row
  while the other six keep the zero-row anti-vacuous error from firing. Partial
  coverage loss reports identically to full coverage.
- Removing the backticks from a row's ID or path makes the regex skip it.
- The whole "diagram" `not certif fire-sequence` passes every content predicate.

THE LESSON, and the reason this bead is worth reading: deriving the list from a
registry fixed WHICH ITEMS get checked and left HOW they are checked untouched.
The registry became a new place to write the same lie. Deriving is necessary and
not sufficient — the derived reference has to be BOUND to the artifact.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A row's path must live under web/diagrams/ and its basename must match its ID.
- The expected count is pinned, so a row silently leaving the PRESENT set is RED
  rather than invisible.
- Content predicates are structural, not substring: parse for the honesty banner
  element and the data-diagram attribute rather than grepping for "not"/"certif".
- Known-bad per bypass above -> RED, including the status-typo case.
- Known-GOOD: the live 7 -> 0.
- Anti-vacuous stays: zero present rows, and an unreadable registry, are ERROR.
close_reason: Fixed. Rows are bound to web/diagrams/<id>.html, the count is pinned, statuses are a closed enum, and content predicates are PARSED (html.parser) rather than grepped — a file whose whole content is 'not certif fire-sequence' no longer passes. All four bypasses reproduced before and RED after. It also found the old gate carried a per-item EXEMPTION for power-path, the one diagram that never conformed; removing the excuse turned it RED on a real defect sitting since P0, fixed with one line of HTML. The exemption had outlived the effort it saved.

title: Hub mastery catalog is pinned at 14 — module 15 is taught and assessed but cannot appear in learner progress
description:
WHAT: web/assets/js/hub_mastery.js MODULE_CATALOG holds 14 slugs, ending at
14-auxiliary. Module 15 is absent, so the hub mastery surface cannot show it.
Derive the catalog from the same registry the Learn index uses, and rebase
scripts/smoke_hub_mastery.mjs off the derived count.

WHY: C5 closed the fairness defect — module 15 was ASSESSED but never TAUGHT —
by shipping web/learn/15-ops-adjacent.html (7,211 words) and 39 approved items.
That part is real and holds. But the PRODUCT-FACING leg was missed: MODULE_CATALOG
drives the mastery/progress surface rendered on web/index.html and web/learn.html,
and it stops at 14. A learner is assessed on module 15, can read module 15, and
cannot see their module-15 progress anywhere.

CONTROLLER ERROR, recorded so it is not repeated: I closed
bd-hardening-c-status-hzs.4 grading it "acceptance fully met", citing the report
line "Learn hub lists 15 modules, not 14". web/learn/ does contain 15 HTML files,
so the sentence was true — but the mastery CATALOG is a different artifact and it
was never checked. This is the second time on this same bead that I measured the
wrong file: I also first counted the Learn page's HTML shell (131 words) instead
of its content markdown (7,211). Verifying a claim means finding the artifact the
claim is about, not the nearest artifact with a matching name.

THIRD INSTANCE TODAY OF THE bd-lt7 PATTERN, and the reason this bead is P1 rather
than P2: scripts/smoke_hub_mastery.mjs:77 asserts
    assert(MODULE_CATALOG.length === 14, "MODULE_CATALOG has 14 modules");
plus two `m <= 14` sweep loops. So ADDING module 15 to the catalog FAILS THE GATE.
The gate layer has written the defect down as a requirement again — after
smoke_learn/smoke_feedback_links/smoke_weak_links did exactly this for the same
module, and after the smoke_diagrams per-item exemption for power-path did it one
layer down. A fixer without this context reads the red gate as a reason to revert.

ACCEPTANCE:
- MODULE_CATALOG is DERIVED from knowledge/domains.toml (or the same
  modules_index.json build_units.py now uses) — not a hand-maintained literal.
- smoke_hub_mastery.mjs asserts the catalog matches the derived registry count,
  never a numeric literal. Its two `m <= 14` sweeps follow the derived length.
- Known-bad: a module declared in the registry but absent from the catalog -> RED
  naming the module. This is the leg that would have caught C5's product side.
- Known-GOOD: the live tree with 15 modules passes; a legitimate 14-module tree
  would also pass, so the fix is not "change 14 to 15".
- Anti-vacuous: an empty catalog, or zero modules discovered, is an ERROR.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER: MUTATE the derivation, confirm the suite trips; then
  with the mutation still in place delete the assertion and confirm it passes.
- crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs open-instance count drops from 5
  as each is closed; it must never grow silently.
close_reason: Fixed and browser-verified. MODULE_CATALOG now derives from web/data/modules_index.json — no filter, no upper bound. Worse than the bead recorded: the n > 14 clamp in normalizeLastWeak DISCARDED a weak module 15 before it could be recommended, so the one place the assessment should change a learner's behaviour was where the bound bit hardest. The recommend card now reads 'Next up · Review M15'. Verified in Chrome against a served build with a seeded learner: 15 mastery rows, zero console errors. Derived, not renumbered — a legitimate 14-module registry still derives a 14-module catalog and invents nothing.

title: The bd-lt7 rebases are unguarded — their known-bad legs exist only in a scratchpad
description:
WHAT: The bd-lt7 rebases of verify_coverage, build_units, verify_bank,
verify_objectives and smoke_feedback_links are proven by evidence that lives in a
scratchpad. Nothing in the repo re-runs any of it. Wire the legs.

WHY: decalogue rule 10 — BUILT != WIRED. Every one of those gates now has a
known-bad leg (a declared module with no items goes RED, an exemption without a
reason is a schema error, drift between registries is caught) and a known-GOOD
leg (a legitimate 14-module tree still passes, so the fix is not "14 -> 15").
Those legs were run by hand, once, against temp fixtures. They are not in
check.sh, not in a selftest, not in a cargo test. The rebase is real; its GUARD
is not. A regression would be silent, and the next reader would see five rebased
gates and reasonably assume they are protected.

This is the same shape the whole bd-lt7 class is about, one level up: the fix was
derived from a contract, and the PROOF of the fix was derived from a session.

Both natural homes are guarded, which is why the agents described rather than did:
- scripts/selftest_l7_objectives.sh — adding cases moves INJECTIONS 4 -> 8, and
  that number is drift-guarded by verify_injection_count against >=5 README
  advertisement sites. It must be regenerated via --write-readme, not typed.
- crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs — already carries the
  verify_coverage and build_units legs; it is the obvious home for the rest.
  smoke_feedback_links needs a tree-copy fixture because the script takes no
  path flags, or it needs --domains/--root arguments added.

The concrete legs are enumerated in the wave reports and are not lost: (e)
declared-module-starved -> RED naming the module; (f) exemption without a reason
-> RED and the module STAYS required; (g) [[domain_min]] for an undeclared
module -> drift; (h) topic in an undeclared domain -> drift; (i) recorded
exemption WITH a reason -> GREEN, a known-good control that must NOT be counted
as an injection.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every known-bad and known-GOOD leg above runs in CI, on every check.sh.
- The 14-module known-GOOD leg is present for each rebased gate. Without it the
  suite ships an over-strict gate, and over-strict gates get routed around.
- Any INJECTIONS bump goes through verify_injection_count --write-readme; the
  advertised number is regenerated, never typed.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER: MUTATE each gate (restore its bound), confirm the
  wired suite trips; then with the mutation still in place delete the assertion
  and confirm it passes.
- Anti-vacuous: a suite that runs zero legs is an ERROR, not a pass.
close_reason: Landed together in dff752b; check.sh TRUE rc=0; advertised total regenerated 36 -> 47 via --write-readme; 5 meta-test pairs green; green controls verified uncounted

title: A third hand-frozen module table survives in smoke_weak_links — and the bound sweep is structurally blind to it
description:
WHAT: scripts/smoke_weak_links.py carries its own hand-written EXPECTED_SLUGS
module->slug table — a third copy of the mapping that verify_objectives.py and
smoke_feedback_links.py just stopped hand-maintaining. Derive it from
knowledge/domains.toml like the others.

WHY, AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TABLE: it is invisible to the sweep
that exists to catch exactly this. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs
detects NUMERIC MODULE BOUNDS — range(1,1X) and comparisons against 13..16. This
table contains no numeric bound at all. It is the same defect class (state
observed once and frozen into a literal, so the gate encodes the tree's current
shape as a requirement) wearing a form the detector cannot see, and it is
therefore in nobody's open count. The sweep reports 0 open instances while this
sits in the tree.

It happens to be CORRECT today, which is precisely why it is dangerous: it will
be correct right up until someone adds module 16, and then it will fail a correct
change for being correct — the bd-lt7 failure mode, from a file the bd-lt7 gate
says is clean.

THE GENERAL LESSON FOR THE SWEEP: a detector keyed on syntax finds instances that
share syntax, not instances that share the defect. "0 open" currently means "no
numeric bound outside the inventory", not "nothing is hand-frozen". Either widen
the detector to hand-maintained module tables, or state the narrowed claim in
rebase_module_bounds.rs so the count is not read as broader than it is. The
second is cheap and honest and should happen regardless.

ACCEPTANCE:
- EXPECTED_SLUGS derives from knowledge/domains.toml; no hand-written mapping
  survives in the file.
- Known-bad: a module declared by the registry with no weak-link surface -> RED
  naming it. Known-GOOD: the live 15-module tree passes AND a legitimate
  14-module tree passes.
- rebase_module_bounds.rs either detects hand-maintained module tables, or its
  header and the open-count assertion state plainly that the count covers
  numeric bounds only.
- Anti-vacuous: zero modules discovered is an ERROR.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER pair.
close_reason: EXPECTED_SLUGS derived from knowledge/domains.toml; rebase_module_bounds.rs widened to Shape::FrozenTable and scan set widened to web/assets/js; 6 new hits adjudicated; open count 0 now covers both shapes; suite 20 -> 36 green; follow-ons bd-we5a and bd-8mjs

title: Four selftest shells owe known-bad cases — coupled through the INJECTIONS drift guard, must land together
description:
WHAT: Four selftest shells each owe new known-bad cases that were specified in
detail by the agents that fixed the underlying gates, and none can land alone —
every one moves an INJECTIONS count that verify_injection_count drift-guards
against the README. Land them as ONE coupled change.

WHY: each fix this wave was proven by hand, once, in a scratchpad. The shells are
where that proof becomes permanent. Every agent described its case rather than
adding it, for the same correct reason: bumping INJECTIONS without regenerating
the advertised total turns the drift guard RED, and the guard is exactly the
mechanism that stops the L4 "gates proven to trip" claim from decaying. Four
separate commits would each break it.

THE CASES, verbatim from the wave reports so nothing is re-derived:

title: The known-bad badge counts shell receipts only, and the Rust migration is shrinking that population
description:
WHAT: Rust known-bad legs emit no INJECTIONS receipt, so the advertised known-bad
count covers shell selftests only. Decide whether to give cargo tests a receipt
mechanism check.sh can aggregate, or to state the narrowed claim permanently.

WHY: the badge decision recorded 2026-08-14 was "shell-selftest receipts only",
with sound reasoning: cargo test reports pass/fail, not a count, so including
Rust legs would mean hand-typing a number — the exact defect the drift guard
exists to remove — and a Rust leg that silently stopped asserting would be
invisible to the gate while inflating the advertised total. A fooled certificate
on the certificate-checker.

That decision is correct AS A STOPGAP and wrong as an end state. The repo is
migrating its gates from Python/shell to Rust (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd).
Every port moves known-bad legs OUT of the counted population and into the
uncounted one. The advertised number therefore describes a shrinking fraction of
the real known-bad population, and at the end of the migration it describes
almost none of it while still reading as the repo's L4 headline.

README now names the population honestly, so nothing is currently false. The risk
is drift-by-success: the number stays green and stays true while becoming
uninformative, which is harder to notice than a number that breaks.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either: cargo test targets emit a receipt check.sh can tee into INJ_LOG and
  verify_injection_count aggregates alongside the shell suites (a libtest
  harness hook, an xtask wrapper, or a per-crate count assertion — evaluate);
- Or: a recorded decision that the badge is permanently shell-only, with README
  and the gate header stating what fraction of the known-bad population it
  covers, and a separate mechanism reporting the Rust legs.
- Whichever: the number stays REGENERATED, never typed.
- Anti-vacuous: zero receipts from a registered source is an ERROR.

title: Prose and generated artifacts asserting contracts the code no longer has (4 sites)
description:
WHAT: Prose and generated artifacts that still assert a contract the code no
longer has. Each is small; together they are the 80%-documents pathology's early
warning, because a reader trusts prose and prose is the least gated surface here.

INSTANCES, all found 2026-08-14, each verified as still present:
1. scripts/check.sh:136-143 — the crosswalk loop enumerates domains 01-14 as a
   literal list. Module 15 exists. Same class as bd-lt7 but in the orchestrator,
   which no gate scans. (Its sibling label at the L6 coverage step was already
   corrected; this one was not.)
2. web/index.html:46 — learner-facing copy reads "14 curriculum modules + ops
   expansions". Semantically defensible (14 EPI domains plus the partner-
   expansion module) and it matches domains.toml's own framing, which is why the
   agent left it rather than editing shipped copy on a hunch. But it is a numeral
   in product copy with no template to derive it from. DECIDE: derive it, or
   record that it is deliberate and why.
3. Four docs still state the golden contract that was REMOVED when the seed-42
   fixture stopped short-circuiting the Rust sampler: web/data/README.md:6,20,23
   · web/README.md:34 · docs/FEATURE_SURFACE.md:13 · docs/PHASE-L6.md:30.
4. web/data/coverage.json — was hand-authored, never generated, and had drifted
   on six numbers (item_count 798 vs 804; m15 40 vs 39) before being regenerated
   2026-08-14. It has NO CONSUMER. Decide: wire it to something, or delete it. An
   artifact nobody reads cannot be wrong in a way anyone notices, which is how it
   drifted six numbers without a single failure.

WHY IT IS ONE BEAD: they share a cause. Each was true when written and became
false when code changed underneath, and nothing mechanically ties any of them to
the artifact they describe. cdcp_registry_check enforces this for CLAIM markers
in README/docs; none of these carry one. The fix is not four edits — it is
deciding, per item, whether it should be derived, gated by a claim marker, or
deleted.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the four resolved by derivation, a claim marker, or deletion — with the
  choice recorded. A plain edit is the weakest option and must be argued.
- The check.sh crosswalk derives from the same registry verify_coverage uses.
- Anti-vacuous: any derived list that comes back empty is an ERROR.
- A known-bad per newly-gated item: change the code, watch the doc gate go RED.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
FIFTH SITE, same class: web/data/coverage.json's own 'note' field says

  Regenerate via: python3 scripts/verify_coverage.py --write-json web/data/coverage.json

As of the check.sh swap on 2026-08-14 that command is no longer the gate — cdcp_gate verify-coverage is. The ledger now instructs a reader to run the oracle rather than the gate.

It could not be fixed in the porting commit and that is not an oversight: the note is part of the byte-exact output the differential test compares, so changing it means changing the Python oracle first, re-running the differential, then changing the port. Exactly the ordering discipline every port in this migration follows.

Note the shape — this is a MACHINE LEDGER carrying a self-referential instruction that went stale the moment its producer changed. It is the same failure as the four prose sites, in a file we generate, which is the category we adopted specifically because prose drifts.

title: Three stated limits with no guard — hand-maintained floor, one-level content.lock walk, build_learn deleting a tracked doc
description:
WHAT: Three residuals the wave-3 agents named honestly inside otherwise-complete
fixes. Each is a stated limit, not a surprise; each is currently unowned.

1. MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES = 5 in verify_injection_count is itself a hand-
   maintained constant. It fails CLOSED (losing an advertisement site is RED and
   forces a deliberate edit) and it is a floor, so adding sites is free — but the
   agent could not derive it and said so. Same class as bd-lt7 in a gate built to
   catch drift. Derive it, or record why a literal is right here.
2. verify_content_lock's tree-side walk is ONE LEVEL DEEP, matching Path.glob.
   A file at knowledge/corpus/x.toml is invisible to both the generator and the
   gate. Closing it requires gen_content_lock.py to change first, which was
   read-only to the agent. Until then the gate's stdout names the roots it does
   and does not cover — the honest form — but the hole is real and reachable.
3. scripts/build_learn.py silently DELETES web/content/modules/README.md on every
   run: its orphan sweep matches any non-module .md. Pre-existing; anyone running
   it has been deleting a tracked doc. It was fixed and the file restored via
   `git show` on 2026-08-14 (DCG correctly blocked `git checkout --`, and the
   agent did not route around it), but the fix has NO REGRESSION TEST — the next
   refactor of that sweep can reintroduce it silently.

WHY ONE BEAD: all three are "the fix landed, the guard did not". Item 3 is the
sharpest — a data-destroying bug was repaired with nothing to stop it returning.

ACCEPTANCE:
- MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES derived, or a recorded argument for the literal.
- content.lock either walks recursively (with gen_content_lock.py updated in the
  same change so a regenerated lock stays green by construction), or the depth
  limit is asserted in a test so it cannot silently deepen or shallow.
- build_learn's orphan sweep gains a known-bad: plant a non-module .md under

title: Does 'offline hub' mean file:// or local server? The hub has never worked over file://
description:
WHAT: The web hub does not work over file://, before or after the 2026-08-14
mastery-catalog fix. Decide whether offline-first means file://-openable, or
means "runs from a local static server with no network".

WHY: Chrome blocks ALL <script type="module"> over file:// by CORS (origin
'null'), so web/assets/js/hub_mastery.js never executes there. Verified by
capturing byte-identical console output on the pre-change and post-change trees —
this is NOT a regression from the catalog work. web/README.md already states a
static server is required, and `cdcp_cli serve` exists and was used to verify the
fix in a real browser.

THE DECISION THIS FORCES, which is why it is a bead and not a note: the CHARTER's
shipped_means opens with "A learner opens the offline hub". If that sentence
means double-clicking an HTML file, the hub is not shipped and never has been for
any module-aware surface. If it means "serve locally, no network", the hub is
fine and the CHARTER sentence should say so. Both readings are defensible; only
one can be the acceptance criterion, and a loop-#3 practitioner signal will be
collected against whichever a real person actually does.

Making file:// work means de-modularizing the whole web/assets/js/ ES-module
graph — a large change with real cost, and it should not be undertaken by
inference from an ambiguous sentence.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The CHARTER's shipped_means states which it is, in words a stranger cannot
  misread.
- If file:// is required: the ES-module graph is bundled or inlined, and a gate
  drives the hub over file:// asserting zero console errors.
- If a local server is required: web/README.md, the learner-facing entry point,
  and any doc saying "offline" say so at first contact, and `cdcp_cli serve` is
  the documented path.
- Either way, a gate exercises whichever contract is chosen. Today nothing does.

title: ESCALATION (Josh): DOE/FEMP guide — accept not-vendored, or authorise a permission request?
description:
WHAT: A decision only Josh can make. The DOE/FEMP data-centre design guide is
"US Government work" but CONTRACTOR-AUTHORED (LBNL) and contains embedded
third-party figures — six attribution lines, some ASHRAE. It is recorded as
capture = "not-vendored", rights = "mixed-us-government-work-with-third-party-
material" (explicitly NOT bare public-domain), ai_ingestion = PROHIBITED.

THE THREE OPTIONS, and why two are already closed:
(a) DO NOT VENDOR — the current state. Costs us the guide's DOE-authored §4-§6
    material, which 25 graph nodes already cite by clause without the body text.
(b) VENDOR A REDACTED EXTRACT — REJECTED FOR AGENTS, and the reasoning is the
    point: producing one requires LOCATING the ASHRAE pages in order to exclude
    them, and that locating act is itself the prohibited ingestion. The exclusion
    list is recorded so a human can execute (b) without re-deriving it.
(c) SEEK PERMISSION from DOE/LBNL (and possibly ASHRAE for the figures).
    External and irreversible — contacting a third party on the project's behalf.
    ESCALATION-ONLY. This bead exists so that escalation is tracked rather than
    living in a session transcript.

WHY IT IS BEADED RATHER THAN DROPPED: it was escalated to Josh on 2026-08-14 and
had no durable record. An escalation with no bead is indistinguishable from a
decision that was never needed — and the next agent to look at the corpus will
re-derive the same analysis and re-escalate, which is exactly the re-litigation
the autonomy grant's "record every fork you resolve" clause exists to prevent.

NOTHING IS BLOCKED ON THIS. The gap it leaves is open and named:
Gap_rci-unusable-without-the-envelope stays open on purpose, and the graph's 25
citing nodes all point at DOE-authored §4.x/§5.x/§6.x — none cites §3.x or
Table 3-1, the third-party sections.

ACCEPTANCE (Josh's, not an agent's):
- A recorded decision: stay at (a), or authorise (c) with a named counterparty.
- If (c) is authorised, the request goes out under Josh's name; an agent drafts
  at most, and never sends.
- If (a) stands, record it as a DECISION with its reason so the analysis is not
  re-derived, and close this bead. Standing still is a legitimate answer; an
  unrecorded standing still is not.
- Under no option does an agent read, quote, summarise, or paraphrase the
  ASHRAE-derived pages. That constraint survives every outcome.

title: The items=[] fail-open bd-2kr closed exists identically in three more bank loaders
description:
WHAT: The `items = []` fail-open bd-2kr closed in verify_orphans.py exists
IDENTICALLY in three more bank loaders. Close them the same way, oracle first.

    if "items" in data and isinstance(data["items"], list):
        for it in data["items"]: ...      # empty list -> adds nothing, no error
    elif "id" in data: ...
    else: errors.append(f"{path.name}: no id or items[]")

The `elif` never runs for an empty list, so the else-branch that would have
caught it never runs either. A bank file whose entire body is `items = []` is
scanned, contributes zero items, and produces NO error and NO mention.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, after bd-2kr closed the first instance:
    scripts/verify_coverage.py    FAIL-OPEN
    scripts/verify_bank.py        FAIL-OPEN
    scripts/verify_objectives.py  FAIL-OPEN
    scripts/verify_orphans.py     fixed (bd-2kr)

WHY IT SURVIVED, and the part worth carrying forward: every one of these files
DOES have an anti-vacuous check — at WHOLE-BANK granularity ("empty bank: zero
items loaded (vacuous coverage is ERROR)"). Grepping any of them for "zero items"
returns a hit and reads as guarded. The controller made exactly that mistake
while auditing this and called verify_coverage.py GUARDED before reading the
actual branch. The aggregate check is real, and it is satisfied by the other 804
items, so it can never fire on this defect. A file that was never really checked
reports exactly like one that passed, and the healthy total is what hides it.

The port agent for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.6 found it, reproduced it
faithfully rather than fixing it (a port that fixes a bug is an unreviewed
behaviour change), and pinned it in tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs with a comment
saying why the port stays quiet too.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix each PYTHON first, watch the corresponding
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs go RED, then change the port to match. Fixing
the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the differential flags the FIX
as the bug. verify_orphans.py shows the shape and its message text
("items[] yielded zero items (vacuous file scan is ERROR)") should be reused so
the three read identically.

Each `KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT` / deliberately-quiet pin in the diff tests is DELETED,
not amended, as its instance is fixed.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A bank file yielding zero items is named and RED in all four loaders.
- Known-GOOD, do not break: a legitimate single-item file (`id = ...` form, no
  `items` key) still passes — the elif branch must survive in each.
- The whole-bank anti-vacuous check stays; this is added granularity, not a
  replacement.
- A scan proves no fourth instance: assert in a test that no bank loader has an
  `items` list branch without a zero-yield guard, so a NEW loader cannot
  reintroduce it. Grep is not sufficient — key on the branch, not on a message.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER pair on at least one instance.
close_reason: done

title: The --prove-wired vacuity check is a substring scan — a comment warning against a row reads as the row
description:
WHAT: The --prove-wired vacuity check is `reg_text.contains(PROBE_PLANT)` — a raw
substring scan of registries/substrate_allowlist.toml (substrate_guard.rs:698).
It must test PARSED ROWS: does any [[allow]] row's `path` equal the plant?

WHY: MEASURED 2026-08-14, it took scripts/check.sh RED with ZERO actual [[allow]]
rows for that path. The only occurrence in the file was a COMMENT — the comment
warning people never to add such a row:

    # NEVER add a row for scripts/__cdcp_probe_unlisted__.py — that is the plant
    # --prove-wired uses, and listing it makes the probe vacuous (the gate ERRORs)

Documenting the rule tripped the rule. A gate that cannot be described in its own
registry without failing is a gate whose documentation is a liability, and the
next person to write that comment will lose the same hour.

THE CLASS, which is why this is worth more than its size: a detector keyed on
TEXT finds matches in scopes it did not mean — comments, prose, error messages,
its own documentation. The same shape appeared five separate times on 2026-08-14
in controller verification alone (a grep for "zero items" matching a whole-bank
message while the file-granular hole sat unguarded; docstrings recording a
removed bound read as live code, twice; a table row appended past the end of the
table). rebase_module_bounds.rs already exists BECAUSE grep cannot tell
documentation from code, and it handles it by inventorying every hit with a
verdict. This check has no such affordance — it just fails.

NOT HOT-PATCHED DELIBERATELY. Changing what a safety gate detects is
escalation-class under the autonomy grant even when the change looks obviously
correct, and a substring scan may be catching a real case a parsed scan would
miss (a malformed row that does not parse, a row with unusual quoting). That
needs deciding, not assuming. The immediate block was cleared the same way the
`dual-path` claims-lint collision was: reword the prose, leave the detector to a
considered change.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The check tests parsed [[allow]] rows for a `path` equal to PROBE_PLANT.
- A row that FAILS TO PARSE is an ERROR, not a silent pass — that is the case
  the substring scan may have been implicitly covering, and it must stay covered.

- BEFORE, clear comment restored: `--prove-wired` exit 4, "lists scripts/__cdcp_probe_unlisted__.py ... vacuous", with ZERO actual [[allow]] rows for that path (grep -c '^path = "scripts/__cdcp_probe_unlisted__.py"' = 0).

(2) Mutation STILL IN PLACE, both assertions deleted: suite exit 0.

SWEEP of every `.contains()` in the shipped part of substrate_guard.rs:
- 324 `has_scanned_extension` `!ext.contains('/')` — KEEP. Guards an artifact of rsplit_once, not a policy decision.
- 361 `validate_rows` `path.contains("..")` — DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE, filed as bd-n1aj. Same substring-for-structure shape `is_in_scope` was fixed for on 2026-08-14, and it contradicts that fix: `scripts/payload..py` is in scope so it REQUIRES a row, and this line rejects every row that could authorise it. - 442 / 931 / 938 / 1040 — BTreeSet membership, not substring. No action.

title: The anti-hallucination gate passes green on an empty corpus — it is greenest when checking nothing
description:
WHAT: scripts/validate_grounding.py reports PASS with nothing to check. Make an
empty item set, an empty corpus, and a missing corpus directory ERRORs.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 by the .9 port agent, three separate vacuous passes:
  empty bank/items (scanned_items=0)        -> exit 0, PASS
  corpus of zero characters (corpus_chars=0)-> exit 0, PASS
  knowledge/corpus/public absent entirely   -> exit 0, PASS
Only a missing bank/items DIRECTORY is caught. The banner in each case reads
"no high-severity hallucination heuristics".

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this is the anti-hallucination gate. Its
whole function is to check bank claims against a grounding corpus. With zero
corpus there is nothing to contradict any claim, so every item trivially scores
clean and the gate emits its most reassuring possible output. It is greenest
exactly when it is checking nothing.

That inverts the value of the signal. Every other gate's green means "I looked and
found nothing wrong." This one's green can mean "I had nothing to look with."
A reader cannot tell those apart from the output, and `corpus_chars=0` is printed
right there next to PASS without anything asserting on it — the same shape as
content.lock printing `knowledge=8` while a deleted row went unnoticed.

LIVE EXPOSURE IS REAL, NOT THEORETICAL. bd-corpus-public-captures-not-licensed-
class-kej tracks NINE captures with redistribution=not-licensed sitting in a
PUBLIC repo. The remediation for those is removal, and validate_grounding
consumes them as its grounding corpus (~659k chars). Removing them without a
replacement source would drop corpus_chars toward zero — and this gate would go
GREEN on the way down instead of RED. The legal fix and the vacuity defect
intersect exactly.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_validate_grounding.rs go RED, then change the port.
Three named tests currently pin the defect deliberately; their failure messages
already say to fix oracle, port and ledger together. DELETE those pins, do not
amend them.

ALSO FOUND, same file, reproduced not fixed — fix in the same pass:
  - topic_labels() splits on "\n[[topic]]\n", so a topics.toml whose FIRST byte
    begins a block never yields that label; the raw id is tokenised instead and
    the score degrades silently. Harmless today (the live registry has a header
    line, 106 labels read).
  - iid = it.get("id", path.name) has no truthiness check, so id = "" produces
    findings prefixed with an empty string instead of the filename.
    verify_orphans already guards this; copy its shape.
  - OK_FAMILY is dead code, compiled and never referenced.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Zero items scanned, zero corpus chars, and a missing/unreadable corpus root are
  each an ERROR naming which one, never a pass.
- A DELIBERATE minimum: state a floor (corpus_chars and scanned_items both above
  a recorded threshold) rather than merely non-zero, so a one-byte corpus cannot
  satisfy it either. Record the threshold and its reason.
- Known-GOOD: the live tree still passes; a small but legitimate corpus passes.
  An over-strict gate gets routed around, which is a slower death than no gate.
- The three deliberate pins in diff_validate_grounding.rs are deleted.
- Byte-exactness restored between oracle and port on every case.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER pair.
close_reason: Anti-vacuous floors landed in oracle + port + ledger; three vacuity cases now RED and named, live tree and a small legitimate tree still green

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: fixed. Oracle first (scripts/validate_grounding.py), differential red, then the port (crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/validate_grounding.rs), then the ledger (tests/diff_validate_grounding.rs).

FLOORS (recorded beside the constants in both files, with reasons):
  MIN_SCANNED_ITEMS = 40  — one full exam form (knowledge/bank_policy.toml exam_n_items = 40); deliberately 1/10 of verify_bank's pool_min_items = 400 so the pool floor stays that gate's. Live: 804 items.
  MIN_CORPUS_CHARS = 20000 — one median module (29 live modules, 749..47651 chars, median 23870). Live: 659149 chars, of which 545885 are OUTSIDE knowledge/corpus/public, so bd-corpus-public-captures-not-licensed-class-kej can delete every capture and this still clears at 27x.
