title: validate_rows rejects every row that could authorise scripts/payload..py — substring-vs-structure, second instance
description:
WHAT: substrate_guard.rs validate_rows() rejects any [[allow]] row whose `path` contains the substring ".." (`path.contains("..")`). is_in_scope() was fixed on 2026-08-14 to test path COMPONENTS, so `scripts/payload..py` IS in scope and DOES require a row — and no row for it can ever be valid.

WHY: found by the bd-ip10 sweep for substring-deciding-structure. REPRODUCED 2026-08-14 in a throwaway repo: scripts/payload..py tracked, a well-formed [[allow]] row present, gate exit 4 with
  ERROR: 1 schema error(s): [[allow]] scripts/payload..py: `path` must be a normalised engine-root-relative path
The file is unfixably RED: it cannot be allowlisted and it cannot be taken out of scope.

NOT FIXED UNDER bd-ip10 DELIBERATELY. It is fail-closed, so a trap rather than a bypass, and the repair WIDENS what the gate permits (a row for a dotted filename becomes valid). Changing what a safety gate permits is a separate, escalation-class decision from bd-ip10's, whose acceptance named only the vacuity check. Recorded in-source as a SWEEP NOTE at the site.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `path` normalisation tests COMPONENTS (reject `.`/`..` as whole components, reject absolute and backslash), matching is_in_scope.
- Known-good: scripts/payload..py with a valid row -> exit 0.
- Known-bad, unchanged: a row whose path is ../escape.py or /etc/x.py -> ERROR.
- The widening is stated explicitly in the commit message and in the gate header.
close_reason: Shared normalisation_defect() predicate: is_in_scope and validate_rows now answer the traversal question from ONE function. scripts/payload..py and scripts/a\b.py with a well-formed row -> exit 0; without a row -> exit 2, named; ../, ./, and absolute rows -> exit 4 as traversal. Agreement asserted over a 24-path corpus. Meta-test pair run: mutation -> 101/101, mutation + assertions deleted -> 0/0.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
CONTROLLER NOTE — this is MY defect, introduced in tick 4 (edc721c), and the record should say so.

I fixed is_in_scope's contains("..") to test path COMPONENTS after codex found that scripts/payload..py fell out of scope entirely. I fixed one instance of the substring bug in that file and did not look for its twin. validate_rows:361 carries the identical bug, and my fix is what put the two halves into contradiction: after tick 4 the path is IN SCOPE so it requires a row, while validate_rows rejects every row that could authorise it. Before tick 4 both halves were consistently wrong, which is why nothing tripped.

Raised to P1 from P2. Not because the exposure is worse — it is fail-closed, a trap and not a bypass — but because an unfixably-RED path is the shape that gets a gate ROUTED AROUND, and a routed-around gate is a slower death than no gate. Someone hitting this cannot comply: adding a correct row does not help.

The repair WIDENS what the gate permits, which is why the bd-ip10 agent filed it instead of shipping it inside a bead authorised only to narrow a detector. That judgment was right and I want it preserved: the escalation class is a property of the DIRECTION of the change, not of how obviously correct it looks.

Acceptance should include: after the fix, scripts/payload..py with a well-formed row PASSES, and without a row is RED. Both legs, or the contradiction just moves.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: FIXED. The contradiction is gone and it is gone by construction, not by two similar checks.

REPRODUCTION BEFORE (throwaway repo, tracked + committed, well-formed [[allow]] row present):
  scripts/payload..py  -> exit 4, "ERROR: 1 schema error(s) ... [[allow]] scripts/payload..py:
                          `path` must be a normalised engine-root-relative path" on the presence
                          leg AND on --staged.
  scripts/payload..py with NO row -> exit 2, named. So the gate demanded a row it then refused.
SECOND INSTANCE FOUND ON THE SAME LINE: `path.contains('\\')`. scripts/a\b.py measured identically
  — in scope (exit 2, named, when unlisted), exit 4 with a well-formed row. git ls-files -z hands
  the gate the raw byte, so a backslash filename is an ordinary POSIX file here. Fixing only the
  ".." half would have left the trap in place one character over; the caller's "or the contradiction
  just moves" was literally true.

THE FIX — one function, called by both halves.
  New `normalisation_defect(path) -> Option<&'static str>` is the ONLY traversal test in the file.
  It rejects: empty, leading '/', and `.`/`..` as whole '/'-separated COMPONENTS. `is_in_scope`
  returns false when it returns Some; `validate_rows` emits the malformed-path finding when it
  returns Some. The old `starts_with('/') || contains("..") || contains('\\')` line is deleted.
  Rewriting that line to mirror the component test was rejected deliberately: two implementations
  that look alike are exactly what failed here, since they read as the same rule right up until one
  was corrected. There is now one implementation and no second site to drift from.

  The behaviour of `is_in_scope` is byte-for-byte unchanged, so nothing left scope and no bypass
  was opened. The widening is bounded to precisely: rows for paths the gate itself says need a row.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE (in the function's doc, and in the gate header):
  - backslash-as-Windows-separator: a row for `scripts\foo.py` is caught by the existing
    "no file at this path" leg, not by this predicate.
  - whitespace padding: validate_rows still trims a row's `path`, so a filename padded with spaces
    still cannot be given a row. The trim stays because it is what makes `path = "   "` the schema
    ERROR it should be; the padded-filename corner is the rarer harm and is now written down.

FOUR LEGS, MEASURED AFTER (real git repos, true exit codes):
  1. scripts/payload..py + scripts/a\b.py tracked WITH well-formed rows -> exit 0, both legs.
  2. scripts/payload..py tracked WITHOUT a row -> exit 2, "FAIL: scripts/payload..py: non-Rust file
     with no row" (named). Same for scripts/a\b.py and weird..name.sh.
  3. Rows for ../outside.py, scripts/../../etc/passwd.sh, scripts/./x.py, /abs/path.py -> exit 4
     each, rejected FOR the traversal reason ("has a `.` or `..` path COMPONENT, which is
     traversal" / "absolute; paths here are relative to the engine root"), not incidentally.
  4. Agreement property, asserted over a 24-path corpus in
     `no_in_scope_path_can_be_un_allowlistable`: if `unlisted` demands a row for p, a well-formed
     row for p must produce zero schema findings. Anti-vacuous floor: >= 10 corpus paths must
     actually demand a row, or the test reports that it proved nothing.
  Anti-vacuity kept: empty path, whitespace-only path, and a row with no `path` field at all remain
  schema ERRORs (`an_empty_or_whitespace_path_row_is_still_a_schema_error`).

META-TEST PAIR (CHARTER definition), true exit codes:
  (1) Sharing broken — old `contains("..") || contains('\\')` re-injected into validate_rows
      alongside the shared call: `cargo test -p cdcp_gate --lib gates::substrate_guard` -> exit 101,
      2 failed; `--test substrate_guard_e2e` -> exit 101, 1 failed. The three that fired are exactly
      the three new assertions (no_in_scope_path_can_be_un_allowlistable,
      a_dotted_or_backslashed_filename_can_be_allowlisted,
      good_a_filename_with_two_dots_or_a_backslash_can_be_allowlisted). No pre-existing test caught
      it — which is why it shipped in the first place.
  (2) Mutation STILL IN PLACE, the three assertions deleted: lib -> exit 0 (52 passed),
      e2e -> exit 0 (42 passed). Nothing else in the repo detects the contradiction.
  Mutation and deletions fully reverted; `grep -c META-TEST` on both owned files returns 0.

SNAPSHOTS TESTED: working tree and index in every case. The throwaway repos were `git init` +
`git add -A` + commit, so worktree and index agree; the e2e fixtures exercise both the presence leg
(worktree) and `--staged` (index). No `git add`/`git commit` was run against the live index, and no
GIT_INDEX_FILE injection was needed because the reproductions used their own repos in scratch.
Live repo re-verified read-only after the fix: `cdcp_gate --root . substrate-guard` and `--staged`
both exit 0, scanned=1233 in_scope=109 exemptions=41.

SUITES: cdcp_gate --lib 277 passed; substrate_guard_e2e 42 passed; repo_surface 4 passed;
`cargo clippy -p cdcp_gate --all-targets` clean; `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` clean on both
owned files. scripts/check.sh NOT run (bd-gl4j — concurrent runs corrupt each other's fixtures);
`--prove-wired` NOT run for the same reason (it executes check.sh). Neither leg is touched by this
change.

FILES: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/substrate_guard.rs, crates/cdcp_gate/tests/substrate_guard_e2e.rs.
Not touched: scripts/check.sh, registries/substrate_allowlist.toml, hooks/pre-commit, any sibling
gate or diff_* test. Nothing staged; the change is left uncommitted in the working tree.

CLAIM CLASS: FLOOR-RAISE, unchanged. The gate still only enforces that a .py/.sh in a mandatory
root carries a reasoned, dated, bead-linked row. What this tick adds is that the set of paths it
demands a row for and the set it will accept a row for are now the same set, derived from one
function. What it cannot decide is unchanged and still stated in the header: whether a reason is
honest, whether a bead is real, whether an expires date is achievable, or that check.sh executes.

DEPARTURE FROM THE BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE WORDING, stated on purpose: the acceptance line said the
normalisation test should "reject absolute and backslash". Rejecting backslash in the SHARED
predicate would have put scripts/a\b.py out of scope — an actual .py entering a mandatory root with
no row, i.e. the tick-4 bypass class, traded for the trap. Backslash is therefore treated as the
ordinary POSIX filename byte git hands us, and the Windows-path concern is left to the exists leg.
Escalate if that call should go the other way; it is a one-line change to the shared function and
the corpus test will then hold both halves to it.

title: Concurrent check.sh runs corrupt each other — a false RED is indistinguishable from a real one
description:
WHAT: Concurrent `scripts/check.sh` runs corrupt each other. Make a second run
refuse to start, or make the mutating steps use private fixtures.

WHY: measured 2026-08-14 with four concurrent runs live during a six-agent wave.
Two failures, neither caused by the code under test:
  - a run exited 2 on `L5 learner pack shape (n_items=39)` because another run was
    inside selftest_reconstructed, which MUTATES web/data/mock40_seed42.json in
    the working tree and restores it afterwards. The second run read the mutated
    state and reported a product defect that did not exist.
  - a run exited 127 with `line 418: en: command not found` because a sibling
    edited check.sh while that shell was mid-read of it. `sh` reads a script
    incrementally; editing it in place mid-run splices the file.

THE COST IS NOT THE FAILED RUN, IT IS THE FALSE VERDICT. A red check.sh from a
concurrency artifact looks exactly like a red check.sh from a real regression, and
the natural response — re-run it — makes it disappear, which trains the reader to
dismiss reds. That is the same "gate you learn to skim" failure the false-positive
work has been chasing all week, arriving through the harness instead of the gate.

The controller caused both, by running check.sh to verify while agents were still
writing. That habit is not going away — verification during a wave is how a wave
gets verified — so the fix belongs in check.sh, not in discipline.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A second concurrent run either refuses to start with a clear message naming the
  holder (a lockfile carrying pid + start time), or is safe by construction.
- Steps that mutate tracked files under web/data/ or goldens/ operate on a
  private copy, or are explicitly serialised behind the lock.
- A stale lock (holder pid gone) is reclaimed automatically — a lock that can
  wedge the build is worse than the race.
- Known-bad: start a run, start a second, assert the second exits non-zero with
  the holder named, and assert the FIRST still completes green.
- Anti-vacuous: the lock path being unwritable is an ERROR, not a silent skip.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER pair.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: FIXED in scripts/check.sh (uncommitted; owner commits).

MECHANISM: mkdir-based directory lock at $ROOT/target/check.lock (gitignored), taken before any gate. Holder records pid + UTC start time. Re-entrancy via exported CDCP_CHECK_LOCK_HELD so selftest_reconstructed.sh's five nested check.sh runs proceed under the ancestor's lock instead of deadlocking on it; substrate-guard --prove-wired runs from a materialised tree under target/, a different ROOT, so it takes its own. Release folded into a single cleanup() on EXIT INT TERM HUP alongside INJ_LOG.

ACCEPTANCE:
- second run refuses: MEASURED, two concurrent full runs. run2 TRUE rc=2, naming 'held by pid 43137, started 2026-08-14T17:21:00Z'.
- mutating steps serialised: enumerated in a comment block in check.sh — 12 tracked-file writes across 7 steps; 6 observed under a git-status poller, 6 read from source.
- stale reclamation: MEASURED. Live holder -> refused rc=2; same lock after the holder was killed -> rc=0 with 'reclaimed stale lock ... is gone'.
- anti-vacuous: MEASURED. Unwritable lock path (parent is a regular file, ENOTDIR for root too) -> rc=2 'LOCK ERROR', never a silent skip.
- L4 wired: new first step runs all three legs in a child via CDCP_CHECK_LOCK_PROBE=1 (acquire, report, exit; no gate runs). Not routed through run_selftest, so the advertised INJECTIONS= count is unchanged.
- meta-test PAIR: (1) refusal branch mutated to fall through (fails open) -> known-bad goes rc=2 'a second run started while pid N holds ...', in the product script and in a truncated runner; (2) mutation still in place, assertion deleted -> rc=0 and the run prints 'ok: concurrency lock proven' while the lock is broken. Both reverted.

NOT OBSERVED: 'the FIRST still completes green'. The tree is RED for a reason I do not own — crates/cdcp_gate/{src/gates/validate_grounding.rs,tests/diff_validate_grounding.rs} and scripts/validate_grounding.py are dirty with in-flight bd-yje7 work; the Python oracle grew a vacuous-corpus FAIL the Rust port has not got yet. Reproduced standalone with zero concurrency (rc=101; 12 -> 11 -> 7 failures over 20 minutes as the sibling converges). Closest reachable evidence: the contended run and a solo run produce byte-identical verdicts for all 22 steps up to the sibling's regression, and the contended run ran ~8 minutes past the refusal and released its lock normally.

RESIDUE (separate defect, not fixed): the exit-127 splice. 'sh' reads a script incrementally, so an agent editing check.sh mid-run still splices it. The lock cannot prevent that — the writer is an editor, not another check.sh. Remedy is a self-copy re-exec (copy to target/, exec it, pass ROOT via env, guard recursion); out of the scope handed to me. Also un-isolated: selftest_reconstructed.sh mutates crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs in the live tree, so a sibling's cargo build in that window compiles injected source. Isolating it means running it against a private tree copy, which changes what it proves (it deliberately exercises the real gate chain in the real tree) and costs a cold cargo target per case. Now serialised against other check.sh runs; still visible to non-check.sh readers.

title: check.sh can be spliced mid-run by an in-flight edit — sh reads scripts incrementally
description:
WHAT: `sh` reads a script INCREMENTALLY, so editing scripts/check.sh while a run
is in flight splices the file. Measured 2026-08-14: a run exited 127 with
`line 418: en: command not found` — a token sheared in half mid-read. Remedy:
check.sh copies itself to target/ and re-execs the copy, passing ROOT via env,
with a recursion guard.

WHY THE RUN-LOCK DOES NOT COVER IT: bd-gl4j serialises concurrent check.sh RUNS
against each other. This writer is not another run — it is an agent editing the
file. No lock between runs can stop a third party writing to the script a running
shell is still reading. The two defects share a symptom (a red that is not a real
regression) and have unrelated causes.

The cost is the same as bd-gl4j's: a false RED is indistinguishable from a real
one, and re-running makes it vanish, which trains a reader to dismiss reds. Worse
here, because exit 127 with a nonsense token looks like a corrupted environment
rather than a concurrency artifact, so the natural response is to go hunting in
the wrong place.

This is routine during multi-agent waves — the controller edits check.sh to wire
gates while agents run, and that is the correct workflow, not a mistake to train
out.

ACCEPTANCE:
- check.sh re-execs from a private copy under target/ (gitignored) so the shell
  never reads the tree copy after start. ROOT passed via env so path resolution
  is unaffected.
- A recursion guard stops the copy from re-copying itself; the guard must not be
  defeatable by an env var an outer caller sets accidentally.
- Interaction with bd-gl4j's lock is stated: which of the two takes the lock, and
  the re-entrancy path for selftest_reconstructed's nested runs still works.
- Known-bad: start a run, truncate or corrupt the TREE copy mid-run, assert the
  run still completes with the verdict it would have had.
- Anti-vacuous: if the copy cannot be made, that is an ERROR, not a silent
  fallback to running the tree copy.
- --prove-wired materialises the index into a separate ROOT and takes its own
  lock; confirm the re-exec does not break that.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER pair.

title: selftest_reconstructed mutates crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs in the live tree — a concurrent cargo build compiles injected source
description:
WHAT: scripts/selftest_reconstructed.sh mutates FOUR tracked files in the live
working tree and puts them back afterwards, including
`crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs`. Decide whether it runs against a private tree copy,
or whether the live-tree mutation is the point and must be declared.

WHY: measured 2026-08-14 while enumerating what check.sh writes:
  web/data/mock40_seed42.json · web/data/keys_seed42.json · web/drill.html
  crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs
bd-gl4j's run-lock now serialises this against other check.sh runs, which closes
the case that was actually biting. It does NOT close this one: a sibling agent
running `cargo build` or `cargo test` during that window compiles INJECTED
SOURCE. The window is real — this suite runs the full gate chain five times.

The honest tension, which is why this is a decision and not a fix: the suite
exists to exercise the real gate chain in the REAL tree. Running it against a
private copy changes what it proves and costs a cold cargo target per case. It
was not removed and not weakened by bd-gl4j, deliberately.

Note the asymmetry that makes it hard to notice: the mutations are put back, so
`git status` is clean afterwards and nothing is left behind. The damage is only
visible to a reader who looked DURING the window, and that reader gets a
compile error or a wrong test result with no surviving evidence of why.

ACCEPTANCE, either branch — but RECORD which and why:
(a) PRIVATE COPY: the suite runs against a tree copy under target/; it must still
    prove what it proves today, and the report states what coverage (if any) was
    lost. Cold-cargo cost measured, not estimated.
(b) DECLARED LIVE MUTATION: the suite announces on stdout, before it starts, that
    it mutates named tracked files in the live tree and that concurrent readers
    will observe injected source. Then a concurrent reader has a chance.
- Either way: a crash mid-suite must not leave a mutated tracked file behind.
  Prove it — kill the suite mid-run and assert `git status` is clean.
- Anti-vacuous: a put-back that silently fails is an ERROR, not a pass.

title: L2 debt: no named test asserts an SLO budget (capability-maturity RED)

title: bank_hash domain string is still cdcp-bank-v1 after C2 changed what it covers
description:
WHAT: C2 changed what `bank_hash` covers, so the hash domain string should move
`cdcp-bank-v1` -> `v2`. It did not, because the version lives in three places and
two are outside the C2 agent's ownership:
  crates/cdcp_core  BANK_HASH_DOMAIN = b"cdcp-bank-v1\0"
  content.lock      `canonical`
  scripts/gen_content_lock.py:32  CANONICAL

WHY IT MATTERS: the domain string is what makes two hashes from different
definitions non-comparable. Right now a hash computed under the OLD definition
(no status, no objective_ids, no citation_ids) and one under the NEW definition
are both labelled v1. Anything that stores or compares a historical bank_hash —
scorecards, a future ledger row, an old golden someone unarchives — cannot tell
which definition produced it. The values differ, so nothing silently matches; the
cost is that a mismatch reads as drift rather than as a definition change, and
the reader has no way to tell those apart.

This is the same class as the CHARTER/ledger drift B1 refuses to adjudicate: two
sides labelled the same when they mean different things.

ACCEPTANCE:
- BANK_HASH_DOMAIN becomes v2 and the two other sites move in the SAME commit.
  A partial bump is worse than none — it creates a third state.
- Every pin regenerated through its sanctioned path (goldens fixture -> goldens
  generate -> export-web -> gen_content_lock.py), values recorded before/after.
- A test asserts the three sites agree, so they cannot drift apart again. Key on
  the constant, not on a grep for the literal.
- Known-bad: change one site only -> RED naming both sides.
- Anti-vacuous: a domain string that is empty or unparseable is an ERROR.
- Record in goldens/PROVENANCE.md what v1 meant and what v2 means, so an old
  hash found in a scorecard can still be interpreted.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: DONE. Three sites moved to cdcp-bank-v2 in one change.

BEFORE -> AFTER (verified against freshly rebuilt binaries):
  cdcp_core::BANK_HASH_DOMAIN   b"cdcp-bank-v1\0" -> b"cdcp-bank-v2\0"
  content.lock canonical        cdcp-bank-v1 -> cdcp-bank-v2
  gen_content_lock.py CANONICAL cdcp-bank-v1 -> cdcp-bank-v2
  bank_hash (5 sites)           3404d854... -> 521fbcd6...
  all_correct.sha256            2b0eacc9... -> 58064e8a...
  all_wrong.sha256              229ffe3d... -> 2fcfbfc0...
  cdcp_wasm.wasm                51b45211... -> aa788a06...
  bank_items_seed42.json        abb804e3... -> UNCHANGED (bare array, carries no bank_hash field)

item_ids UNCHANGED: 40/40 identical in order, 0 entered, 0 left — verified by parsing both fixtures and comparing arrays element-wise, never by diff line count.

AGREEMENT TEST: crates/cdcp_core/tests/bank_hash_domain_agreement.rs, 4 tests, keyed on cdcp_core::bank_hash_domain_label() and NOT on a grep for the literal — a grep-based test passes when all three sites are wrong together, the exact partial-bump state it must catch.

KNOWN-BAD (each exit 101): content.lock only -> RED naming both sides; gen_content_lock.py only -> RED; CONSTANT only reverted with both labels left at v2 -> RED on both label tests.
ANTI-VACUOUS (each an ERROR): domain b"\0" -> 'only a NUL — the label is empty'; not NUL-terminated -> 'must be NUL-terminated'; canonical key deleted -> 'an absent site is an ERROR, not agreement'.

PROVENANCE.md records the era->value table: the label v1 covered TWO different payload definitions (pre-C2 and post-C2), so disambiguation is by VALUE. scorecards/L5.json's three _at_l5_ship values are pre-C2, comparable to nothing in tree, documented as a record not a pin.

Coupling ledger walked GREEN: surfaces=13 pins=28 goldens=8 couplings=41. goldens_couplings_e2e 38 passed, KNOWN_DEBTS empty.

TRAP RECORDED: restoring a perturbed source with 'mv file.bak file' gives it the backup's OLDER mtime, so cargo skips the rebuild and you test the BROKEN binary. Hit it live — the test reported RED for a GREEN tree; by symmetry it can report GREEN for a RED one. Measured mtimes in PROVENANCE. All final values re-verified from forced rebuilds.

title: Four artifacts still assert the pre-C2 bank_hash or say C2 is open
description:
WHAT: Four artifacts still assert the pre-C2 bank_hash or say C2 is open. Each is
small; together they are the doc-drift class, and two of them are pins that a
gate reads.

1. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_content_lock.rs:350,360,729,785 — a
   HAND-WRITTEN bank_hash literal, e828...71db, now stale. The gate BINARY is
   green; only its differential test carries the pin. Its edit_lock helper has an
   anti-vacuous assert, so it failed LOUDLY ("the mutation would have been a
   no-op") rather than silently no-opping — that design is why this was found at
   all, and it should be preserved.
2. scorecards/L5.json:38 `bank_hash_live` still e828... Its own note says it
   drifts and it is wired to no gate. DECIDE: derive it, gate it, or delete it.
   An artifact nobody reads cannot be wrong in a way anyone notices — that is
   exactly how web/data/coverage.json drifted six numbers.
3. docs/PLAN-A-TO-Z.md:59-60 and docs/ROADMAP-WAVES.md:113-117 state C2 as OPEN
   in the present tense ("Today hash_payload() omits them"). verify-doc-consistency
   is exit 0, so nothing catches this — the gate checks milestone tables, not
   present-tense claims about code. Same shape as bd-smvb.

WHY ONE BEAD: they share a cause. Each was true when written and became false
when code changed underneath, and nothing mechanically ties any of them to the
artifact they describe. Item 1 is the interesting one: a test that pins a value
by hand is a doc with a compiler.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The four literals in diff_verify_content_lock.rs are updated to the current
  hash, OR derived from the artifact so they cannot go stale again. Prefer
  derived; if hand-pinned, say why.
- scorecards/L5.json resolved by one of derive / gate / delete, with the choice
  recorded.
- The two roadmap docs state C2's status truthfully. If a claim-marker would let
  cdcp_registry_check catch this class, add one.
- Known-bad per newly-gated item: change the code, watch the gate go RED.
- Anti-vacuous: any derived list that comes back empty is an ERROR.
close_reason:
All four artifacts resolved, three of them by removing the drift class rather than re-freezing it.

1. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_content_lock.rs - the four hand-written e828... literals are now DERIVED. Fixture::bank_hash() parses the fixture's own content.lock, with an anti-vacuous assert that it is 64 hex chars. The existing edit_lock guard ('the mutation would have been a no-op') is the built-in known-bad: a wrong derivation panics loudly rather than silently no-opping. 32/32 green.
2. scorecards/L5.json - resolved by DELETE, not derive. bank_hash_live was two hash_payload definitions stale, no gate reads it, and re-freezing a live-claiming field in a static JSON only schedules the next drift. The three surviving values are renamed _at_l5_ship to say plainly that a scorecard is a dated record, with a note on which definition produced them and a gated_by field naming that nothing reads it.
3-4. docs/PLAN-A-TO-Z.md and docs/ROADMAP-WAVES.md stated C2 as open in the present tense; both now state it as landed, name what changed, and carry the residual bd-6ycw. ROADMAP also records the consequence nobody had written down: because status is now covered, retiring an item moves bank_hash by itself, inverting PROVENANCE 'Bank drift'.

verify-doc-consistency stayed exit 0 throughout - it checks milestone tables, not present-tense claims about code, so this class is still ungated. Same shape as bd-smvb.

title: 24 reviewed near-duplicate pairs to adjudicate — and the import that created 20 of them
description:
WHAT: 24 near-duplicate pairs remain in the approved pool, every one reviewed by
hand and judged genuine. Adjudicate each — one `status = "retired"` per pair —
then wire the gate.

The full table with per-pair similarity scores and verdicts is in the C3 agent's
report on bd-near-duplicate-item-gate-i5v. Do not re-derive it; the review is
done and the measured false-positive rate is 0/25.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE DECISION, NOT 24 SLIPS. Twenty of the twenty-five pairs
put a `mock40-*` item against a module-bank item. The wholesale import of
`practice/PRACTICE-EXAM.md` into the same pool the module banks feed is what
created the class. That matters three ways:
  - the retirement rule is mechanical, not case-by-case: withdraw the IMPORT copy
    unless the seed-42 form actually draws it (the C3 agent's rule, applied to
    mock40-q40, and the reason it retired that side rather than bank-m14-q121);
  - a fix that retires 24 items without addressing the import will regrow the
    class the next time practice content is folded in;
  - the count matters. 804 was never 804 distinct propositions.

ALSO SURFACED, and worth its own look: pair 5 (`bank-m15-q138` / `mock40-q37`,
MOP) is cross-module m13/m15 — a topic-assignment defect, not only a duplicate.
Retiring one copy hides it.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the 24 pairs resolved by retiring one side, with the surviving side
  named and the choice justified in the retired file's header (the C3 agent's
  three-part argument is the template: which copy the published form draws,
  which explanation teaches, and provenance).
- Retired, NEVER deleted. The bank is content-addressed and deletion loses the
  provenance of the duplication.
- A recorded decision on the import path: does practice content enter the same
  pool as module banks, and if so what stops the next import regrowing this?
- `cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- near-duplicate-items` exits 0 afterwards, and the
  two check.sh lines from the C3 report are wired in the same commit.
- bank_hash moves; every pin regenerated through the sanctioned block in
  goldens/PROVENANCE.md, in order, in one commit.
- `cdcp_bank::load_real_bank_items` and
  `cdcp_assemble::real_bank_is_all_approved_and_seed42_holds` both carry an
  allowed-retired list; their own message already says "until C3/C5 retire
  specific items". Extend it, do not weaken the assertion.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DONE — 24 pairs adjudicated, gate green, everything re-frozen. check.sh wiring is the only open half and it is Josh's (lines below, proven, not applied).

THE IMPORT DECISION, which is the part that outlives the 24 retirements:

PRACTICE CONTENT KEEPS ENTERING bank/items. No second pool, no quarantine. What changes is that a bulk addition may no longer land un-adjudicated: `cdcp_gate near-duplicate-items` runs BEFORE and AFTER the addition, every pair the second run flags that the first did not is adjudicated in the same commit, and an import that leaves the gate RED is not landed. Recorded in bank/IMPORT-POLICY.md, referenced from the doc comment on cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED and from all 24 retired file headers, so an agent adding a retirement or reading a retired item hits it.

A SECOND POOL WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE. The 24 pairs split 18 / 6, not 20 / 4 as the bead estimated: eighteen put a mock40-* import against a module-bank item, and SIX were module-bank against module-bank — the q2xx "bank expansion (depth/apply)" wave duplicating items the same bank already held. A separate practice pool would not have caught one of those six. The defect is an ungated bulk write, not the source directory, so the gate is the fix and the pool stays single.

RETIREMENT RULE, mechanical: withdraw the copy from the bulk wave, unless the published seed-42 form draws it, in which case the form wins. Applied without departure to all 24. It bit exactly once — pair 1, where the seed-42 form draws bank-m12-q060, so the q2xx copy m12-q219 went. Extension recorded, since the bead's rule only named mock40-*: for the six module-bank pairs the "bulk wave" is the q2xx expansion, identified by its first-line provenance comment. Same rule, one more wave.

WHERE THE EXPLANATION LEG FAILED, recorded rather than smoothed: pair 14 (mock40-q24 / m08-q042, 1U = 1.75in) has two explanations that are both a bare restatement of the measurement. Neither teaches. It was decided on provenance plus a thinner margin (the survivor's stem uses the full term "One rack unit (RU/U)"), and the retired file's header says so instead of manufacturing a preference.

THE MEASURED FACT THE BEAD ASKED ME TO TEST AGAINST — RESOLVED, and it is not a sampler bug.

item_ids MOVED this time: all 40 positions differ, 33 ids left, 33 entered, 7 survived (bank-m14-q121, m02-q077, m02-q081, m02-q085, m05-q148, m09-q123, m13-q202). Verified by parsing the fixture JSON and comparing id lists, not by reading a diff.

Why retiring mock40-q40 alone had moved nothing: measured it directly by re-running export-web over single-item perturbations of a temp bank copy and diffing parsed id arrays. mock40-q40 sat at sorted position 43 of 44 — LAST in module 14's approved list. sample_item_ids sorts each module by id, shuffles, then reads only the first two or three entries; a removal perturbs its module's permutation from its own sorted position onward, so a removal at the tail of a long list usually cannot reach the front. m12-q219 (54 of 63) also moved nothing. Removals nearer the front moved 2-3 of 40 (bank-m13-q077 pos 1: 3; bank-m14-q109 pos 5: 3; m06-q047 pos 6: 3; m09-q108 pos 8: 3; mock40-q02 pos 33: 2).

The second half matters more: a single removal moving only 3 of 40 positions PROVES the global PRNG stream does not shift. If it did, every downstream module shuffle and the final presentation shuffle would move and essentially all 40 ids would change — which is exactly what 24 removals across eleven modules did. Blast radius scales with the perturbation. The filter is applied on every path; the draw is just narrow. Full table and the standing rule ("a one-line fixture diff is not evidence the sampler ignored the edit — parse item_ids and compare the lists") are in goldens/PROVENANCE.md under the bd-tetz re-freeze section.

PINS, before -> after (all seven goldens plus the WASM):
  bank_hash / content.lock / fixture / all three web packs : 173057eb9385cfc5... -> 3404d85437e3ad47...
  mock40_seed42_all_correct.sha256 : 68d670e0d5c2b3d1... -> 2b0eacc9db0fe872...
  mock40_seed42_all_wrong.sha256   : 81937bf032800987... -> 229ffe3daaa7467b...
  web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm   : d7459b7d525dc757... -> 51b45211767aaf92...
Regenerated through the sanctioned block in PROVENANCE order (fixture first), then export-web, goldens check (exit 0), UPDATE_CONTENT_LOCK=1 gen_content_lock.py, then sh scripts/build_web_wasm.sh.

registries/goldens-couplings.toml WALKED, not re-dated. Eight rows moved: the goldens.regeneration-path surface (a sibling's bd-goldens-check-is-file-hole-7v9p landed in cdcp_cli, so the pin re-extracted and the derived version went v2ddd2f43a9d5 -> vb61753f4e9b8) plus all seven frozen digests. Five justifications were REWRITTEN because their meaning changed, not re-dated: the regeneration-path row said "the bank_hash pin is already conditional on the file existing", which is now false; the fixture row said "bank CONTENT drift is not this file's job", which only held while no re-freeze had ever moved a draw; the bank-hash-pin row's second sentence described the same closed hole; the bank-items-pack row said "the full 804-item array", which now needs 804-files-vs-779-drawable; and the keys-pack row gained the product change hiding in the digest — the surviving explanation of each pair is the one that teaches, so the post-answer text a learner reads is now the better of the two that existed. `cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test goldens_couplings_e2e` green, 38 tests, KNOWN_DEBTS still empty — this work added no debt.

FILED, not buried:
  bd-mock40-q37-cross-module-topic-76vs — pair 5's topic-assignment defect. mock40-q37 is module 13 with topic m13-safety-components while the survivor is module 15 / m15-documentation. The import numbered files by practice-exam question order and derived `module` from the numbering, so other mock40-* items may carry it without a duplicate to expose them, and no gate compares an item's module against its topic_ids prefixes.
  bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh — verify-coverage counts FILES not approved items against the module floors (it printed "m14: 44 (min 24) [ok]" while 42 are drawable). No live breach — every module clears its floor on the approved pool too, checked — but the gate is fail-open on exactly the pool C1 restricts assembly to.
  bd-web-pack-ships-retired-items-4ivb — web/data/bank_items_seed42.json now hands 25 retired items to the browser.
  bd-wave-tree-red-substrate-and-rebase-f4hg — sibling in-flight, not mine: workspace will not compile (rebase_module_bounds.rs tuple arity) and substrate-guard exits 4 (allowlist missing the widened compiled-in extension floor), which makes check.sh RED at S0.

THE GATE'S OWN LIMIT SURVIVED the change and is now in its GREEN output, not only its header: "this does NOT mean the pool holds 779 distinct propositions — paraphrased duplicates score below every threshold here and are invisible to this gate". 779 is not a certified count; bd-e1yt owns that.

title: Paraphrased duplicates pass the C3 gate silently — 804 is a pool size, not a proposition count
description:
WHAT: The near-duplicate gate catches COSMETIC duplicates. Paraphrased duplicates
— same proposition, freshly worded answer — score below every threshold and pass
silently. Decide whether the repo needs a second mechanism, and correct any place
that reads the bank's item count as a count of distinct propositions.

MEASURED, found BY HAND and not by the gate, all in the live approved pool:
  m09-q111 / m09-q242  both "IT power becomes heat"          22% answer overlap
  m09-q113 / m09-q202  both allowable-vs-recommended envelope 5%
  m09-q122 / m09-q234
  m09-q140 / m09-q209

WHY THIS IS A PRODUCT BEAD AND NOT A GATE BEAD: the C3 gate is honest about its
own limit — its green path prints what it cannot decide, and its header says a
green verdict means "no cosmetic duplicates remain in the approved pool", never
"the pool holds N distinct propositions". That honesty is correct and should not
be weakened. But the consequence lands on the product: the 804 headline is not a
count of distinct propositions, and after the 24 adjudications the true figure is
lower than 804 - 24, by an unknown amount.

A learner sitting a 40-item form drawn from a pool with paraphrase duplication
can be assessed twice on one proposition and never notice. That costs two of
forty slots and moves a score for a reason unrelated to knowledge.

THE HARD PART, stated so nobody ships a bad answer to it: catching paraphrase
means semantic comparison, and the CHARTER's non_goals forbid an LLM as
grader-of-record. Any mechanism here must be deterministic and offline (decalogue
1, and the WASM/offline invariant). Plausible directions, none obviously right:
a proposition registry each item declares against (turns the problem into a
declared-key collision, which IS deterministic); topic-atom granularity fine
enough that two items on one atom are visible; human review at authoring time
with the gate only covering the cosmetic floor. Choosing is the work.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision: second mechanism, or accept the limit and state it.
- Every place that reads the item count as a distinct-proposition count is
  corrected — README, docs, any scorecard, and the CHARTER if it implies it.
  Grep for 804 and judge each hit.
- If a mechanism ships: deterministic, offline, with a measured false-positive
  rate on the live bank, a known-GOOD leg using the hot-aisle/cold-aisle pair
  (m09-q206 / m09-q207 — genuinely distinct, 4% answer overlap), and a known-bad
  using one of the four pairs above.
- If the limit is accepted: the number the product publishes is a pool size, not
  a proposition count, and says so where a reader meets it.

title: The .wasm is an eighth frozen artifact, and the coupling ledger does not know it exists
description:
WHAT: web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm is a COMMITTED BINARY (299KB, last built 2026-08-12, commit ef12275). It compiles cdcp_core + cdcp_bank + cdcp_grade, so it embeds hash_payload, canonical_json and the grader — exactly the surfaces registries/goldens-couplings.toml pins. It is not a [[golden]] row, and B2 discovery only sweeps goldens/, so nothing declares the coupling.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: after C2 changed hash_payload and the four-command block re-froze all seven declared goldens, the committed .wasm still computed the PRE-C2 address. smoke_results_wasm.mjs failed with: bank_hash mismatch: attempt has 173057eb… bank has e82817572a82d13f… — a two-day-old binary disagreeing with the tree about what a bank hash means. Rebuilding via scripts/build_web_wasm.sh fixed it (287330 -> 299556 bytes).

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: check.sh DID catch it, at L5, by a runtime digest comparison ~530 lines in — the same late/indirect signal B2 was built to replace. The ledger says a re-freeze cannot happen silently; that claim is true only for the seven artifacts it lists. An eighth frozen artifact sat outside it and went stale for two days. The gap is not that the repo is unguarded, it is that the LEDGER OVERSTATES ITS COVERAGE while the thing it misses is a shipped binary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [[golden]] row for web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm with depends_on naming bank.hash-payload, bank.item-schema, core.canonical-json, core.grade-report-shape, core.choice-letter and a justification for each.
- The B2 discovery leg is widened past goldens/ so an undeclared frozen binary is RED. Decide and record what counts as a frozen artifact — a committed build output is the class, not the directory.
- Known-bad: rebuild the wasm without re-affirming -> RED naming the surface, not just the file.
- Anti-vacuous: zero discovered frozen artifacts is an ERROR.

title: build_units: two input registries can vanish entirely and the gate still reports GREEN
description:
WHAT: scripts/build_units.py (and therefore the byte-exact port cdcp_gate build-units) treats two missing input registries as ordinary, not as errors. Found by the differential harness for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.12 and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, because a port stricter than its oracle blinds the whole differential.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, both implementations byte-identical:
  u-notopics  knowledge/topics.toml deleted     -> exit 0, PASS: build_units units=134 modules=15
              load_topics_by_domain returns {}, every unit gets topic_ids: [], and the picker
              reads an empty topic set as "no preference" rather than "nothing to match", so it
              still fills each unit from the module pool.
  u-noindex   web/data/modules_index.json deleted -> exit 0, PASS: units=134 modules=16
              silently globs web/content/modules/*.md instead, which sweeps in README.md.
              The module set the docstring calls DERIVED is absent and nobody hears about it,
              and the count is WRONG (16 vs 15) on the green path.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the anti-vacuous law violated on a load-bearing builder. The artifact
web/data/units_index.json feeds the Learn surface. An input registry disappearing produces a
report that is indistinguishable from one that checked everything — 134 units either way. The
16-vs-15 case is worse than silent: it is a green verdict carrying a wrong number.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING (the Python-first rule): fix scripts/build_units.py FIRST, watch
tests/diff_build_units.rs go RED on u-notopics and u-noindex, and only then move the port. Fixing
the port first makes the differential flag the FIX as the divergence.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A missing knowledge/topics.toml is exit 1 in BOTH implementations, naming the file.
- A missing web/data/modules_index.json is exit 1 in BOTH, and the glob fallback is either
  deleted or gated behind an explicit flag. Record which and why.
- The 16-vs-15 discrepancy is stated in the bead history: README.md was being counted as a module.
- tests/diff_build_units.rs u-notopics / u-noindex flip from GREEN-witness to RED-witness in the
  same commit as the Python change; the two sides stay byte-identical throughout.
- Anti-vacuous: zero modules or zero units remains an ERROR (already true, keep it).
close_reason: VERDICT PASS — both registries hard-error naming the file, glob fallback DELETED (16-vs-15 README.md discrepancy measured and recorded), RED-before-port observed, differential 15/15 byte-identical, meta-test pair proven

comments.author: josh
comments.text:

ORDERING, as the bead required (Python first):

  notopics   py/rs  exit 0  stderr 0B  "PASS: build_units units=134 modules=15"  120380B sha c6b48efe...
  noindex    py/rs  exit 0  stderr 0B  "PASS: build_units units=134 modules=16"  174794B sha 065dd887...

THE 16-vs-15 DISCREPANCY, measured and stated as the bead asked. With modules_index.json absent the build globbed web/content/modules/*.md, which holds 16 files because README.md sits alongside the 15 modules. README.md was counted as a module: `by_module` gained a `"README": []` entry, `module_count` went 15 -> 16, and the artifact grew by exactly 18 bytes (174776 -> 174794). title: build_glossary_json prints PASS above its own FAIL, and both builders write before they judge
description:
WHAT: two defects the .11/.12 differential reproduced byte-exactly and did not fix.

1. VERDICT-SHAPE — the exact defect bd-lt7 fixed in build_units.py, still live in
   scripts/build_glossary_json.py. On the below-floor path it prints the PASS line FIRST and
   FAIL underneath, on its way to return 1:
       PASS: glossary terms=0 -> web/data/glossary.json
       FAIL: need >=15 terms

   an_empty_glossary_is_an_error_in_both so the port cannot quietly improve it.

2. WRITE-BEFORE-VERDICT — both builders write their artifact BEFORE evaluating any threshold, so
   a RED run still leaves a file behind. build_glossary_json.py leaves a short glossary.json;
   build_units.py leaves a units_index.json. A later reader cannot tell a passing artifact from
   the residue of a failed run.

WHY ONE BEAD: both are the same mistake — the verdict is computed after the side effect, so the
side effect cannot depend on the verdict. Fixing (2) is what makes (1) fixable without a second
pass over the output.

ORDERING (Python-first): change the .py, watch tests/diff_build_glossary_json.rs and
tests/diff_build_units.rs go RED, then move the ports. Both harnesses assert the artifact on RED
paths as well as GREEN, so a write that stops happening IS caught.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No implementation prints PASS on a path that returns non-zero. Grep the other builders for the
  same shape before closing; bd-lt7 fixed one instance and this is the second, so treat it as a
  class and say how many exist.
- A failing run writes NO artifact, in both implementations, asserted for both builders.
- The two differentials stay byte-identical on all 24 existing cases through the change.
close_reason: VERDICT PASS — verdict shape + write-after-verdict fixed in both builders and both ports; class counted at THREE, instance 3 filed as bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n; per-side detector added to both harnesses with two mutation pairs proving it

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT PASS — verdict shape fixed, write-after-verdict fixed in BOTH builders, class counted at THREE, and the RED-before-port was observed for each change.

THE CLASS COUNT, as the bead required. An exhaustive census of scripts/*.{py,sh,mjs}, crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs, crates/*/src/**/*.rs and hooks/, tracing forward from every success print to every reachable non-zero exit, found THREE instances of the shape and no more:

  1. scripts/build_units.py                    — fixed by bd-lt7 (historical).
  2. scripts/build_glossary_json.py + its port — THIS BEAD.
  3. scripts/verify_coverage.py:336 + crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs:1024
     — filed as bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n. NOT patched here: it is
       outside this bead's ownership, and at three instances the correct fix is a
       DETECTOR, not a third patch.

Instance 3 arrives through a different door: the verdict is not printed above a FAIL line, it is printed above a SIDE EFFECT THAT CAN STILL FAIL. `print(status)` at :336, then an unguarded mkdir + write_text at :393 under --write-json; on the Rust side the buffered PASS is PRESERVED by Halt into Outcome { stdout: out, code: 1 }. Dormant in CI (check.sh omits --write-json) but live for operators — the command is printed in the artifact's own `note` field.

Explicitly EXCLUDED from the count, with reasoning, so it is not re-derived: per-item "  ok: <thing>" detail lines inside a report whose top line is FAIL (build_units.py does this deliberately and correctly); verify_objectives' provisional PASS in its JSON summary (a successful write implies exit 0, a failed write implies stdout FAIL — the only hole is a torn file, which is not a verdict surface); check.sh (fail() exits 2, so no `ok` is reachable after a failure). All 12 selftest_*.sh, the .mjs smokes, and the remaining 16 Rust gates are clean.

THE DETECTOR, which is the real deliverable. Added to `compare()` in BOTH builder differentials, evaluated on EVERY case rather than the handful that happen to be RED, and PER SIDE rather than only across the two — a differential only catches a regression that lands on ONE side, and two implementations that both regress agree with each other perfectly:

    for (side, r) in [("python", &py), ("rust", &rs)] {
        if r.code != 0 {
            assert!(!r.out().contains("PASS"), ...);   // verdict shape
            assert!(r.artifact.is_none(), ...);        // write-after-verdict
        } else {
            assert!(r.artifact.is_some(), ...);        // a green build that wrote nothing is not a build
        }

ORDERING (Python first), observed:
- build_glossary_json.py fixed -> diff_build_glossary_json OBSERVED RED, 3 of 10 cases, all "STDOUT differs" -> then the port -> 10/10.
- build_units.py fixed -> diff_build_units OBSERVED RED, 10 of 14 cases -> then the port -> 15/15.

  units, empty content dir py/rs  exit 1  artifact PRESENT with "unit_count": 0

AFTER — byte-identical on both sides:
  glossary, live source    py/rs  exit 0  stderr 0B  "PASS: glossary terms=156 -> web/data/glossary.json"  20768B sha 0ca90d9b...  (UNCHANGED)
  glossary, empty source   py/rs  exit 1  stderr 0B  "FAIL: glossary terms=0" / "  - need >=15 terms, got 0" / "  out=... NOT WRITTEN"   ARTIFACT ABSENT
  glossary, one term       py/rs  exit 1  stderr 0B  "FAIL: glossary terms=1" / "  - need >=15 terms, got 1"                              ARTIFACT ABSENT
  units, live inputs       py/rs  exit 0  stderr 0B  "PASS: build_units units=134 modules=15"  174776B sha 0ef8dd08...  (UNCHANGED)

Neither tracked artifact is modified in git status; the live tree was never run against.

REPORT SHAPE. On RED the `out=` line now reads "out=<path> NOT WRITTEN (a failing build leaves no artifact)" rather than naming a file that was not written. The old line was a second small lie on the same report.

META-TEST PAIRS. Each mutation was applied to BOTH implementations identically, so the cross-implementation comparison still agrees and ONLY the new per-side leg can fire. That is the point: the pair proves the new assertion is the detector, not the differential.

PAIR 1 — write-after-verdict (units, both sides write unconditionally):

title: goldens check has a vacuous-pass branch: deleting goldens/bank_hash.txt makes its own check silently pass
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_cli goldens check guards its bank_hash comparison with `if bh_path.is_file()`. Delete goldens/bank_hash.txt and the branch is skipped: the step reports ok and the pin is never compared. Found while building the B2 coupling ledger (bd-hardening-b-ledgers-gvm.2); out of that bead scope because cdcp_cli was not its to edit.

WHY IT IS STILL PARTLY COVERED, AND WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH: B2 added REQUIRED_GOLDENS plus a
discovery leg, so DELETING the file is now RED from the ledger side. But the CLI branch itself is
still fail-open, and the ledger is a different gate that a future refactor could route around.
The absent-input-reads-as-success shape is the one this repo has now found in five separate
places; leaving a known instance in place because a second gate happens to cover it is how the
next one survives.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A missing goldens/bank_hash.txt is an ERROR in goldens check itself, not a skipped branch.
- Known-bad: delete the file, run goldens check alone (not check.sh) -> non-zero naming the file.
- Sweep cdcp_cli for sibling `if <path>.is_file()` / `.exists()` guards around comparisons and
  report the count; each one is either an error path or carries a written reason why absence is
  legitimately fine.
- Anti-vacuous: goldens check with zero goldens discovered is an ERROR.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: fixed + swept. crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs, crates/cdcp_cli/tests/cli.rs.

THE FIX: the bank_hash comparison is now UNCONDITIONAL. Presence is enforced by a compiled-in REQUIRED_GOLDENS list (fixtures/mock40_seed42.json, mock40_seed42_all_correct.sha256, mock40_seed42_all_wrong.sha256, bank_hash.txt); absence names the file and exits 1.

  ./target/debug/cdcp goldens check --bank bank/items --dir $T/g   ->  exit 1
  cdcp: missing required golden(s): .../bank_hash.txt - an absent golden is an ERROR here, not a skipped comparison
Before the fix the identical input gave exit 0 with stdout 'ok golden all-correct / ok golden all-wrong'. The only evidence of the skipped comparison was one MISSING stdout line.

KNOWN-GOOD: live goldens/ exit 0, and the run now reports its own coverage:
  goldens check: 3 comparison(s) over 4 discovered golden file(s) under goldens; unchecked-here: none
Prose (PROVENANCE.md, an added NOTES.md) is still legitimately optional and does not redden.

SWEEP: 22 guard sites in cdcp_cli. 5 sit around a comparison or a verdict and were fail-open or unexplained; 1 was the real hole (this bead), 4 more were latent same-shape (0-byte pin, vacuous scan, empty fixture, dropped leg). 17 are legitimately optional or already fail-closed and each now carries a written reason. title: mock40-q37 is filed under module 13 but tests module-15 MOP content — a topic-assignment defect the duplicate retirement hides
description:
WHAT: `mock40-q37` is filed under `module = 13` with `topic_ids = ["m13-safety-components",
"m15-documentation"]`, while the surviving copy of the same proposition, `bank-m15-q138`, is
`module = 15` / `["m15-documentation"]`. The item is an MOP (Method of Procedure) question. MOP is
module-15 operations content; `m13-safety-components` is physical security/safety hardware.

The duplicate was adjudicated under bd-tetz (mock40-q37 retired, bank-m15-q138 survives). THAT
RETIREMENT HIDES THIS DEFECT RATHER THAN FIXING IT: the near-duplicate gate was the only surface
on which the cross-module disagreement was visible, and it will not flag a retired item again.
Filed separately so the topic assignment is still on the record after the duplicate is gone.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ITEM:
  - `mock40-q37` lives in `bank/items/m13-q037.toml` — the FILENAME says module 13, the item it
    duplicates says module 15. The import from `practice/PRACTICE-EXAM.md` numbered files by
    practice-exam question order and derived `module` from that numbering, not from the item's
    content. That is a mechanism, not a slip, so other mock40-* items may carry the same defect
    without a duplicate to expose them.
  - Nothing in the gate set compares an item's `module` against its `topic_ids` prefixes.
    `verify_orphans` checks that every topic id resolves and every item is anchored; it does not
    check that `module = 13` and a topic named `m15-*` disagree. `mock40-q37` carried topics from
    two different modules and passed every gate.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every `mock40-*` item's `module` re-checked against the content of its stem, not against its
  filename. Report the count checked and the count wrong — an empty finding set is a finding
  only if the scan is shown to have run.
- Decide and record whether a `module`/`topic_ids` prefix disagreement is legal. If it is not,
  the check belongs in `cdcp_gate verify-orphans` or its own gate, wired with the anti-vacuous
  floor the rest of the suite uses.
- If any live (non-retired) item is misfiled, fix the `module` and re-freeze through the
  sanctioned block in `goldens/PROVENANCE.md` — `module` is in `hash_payload`, so a fix moves
  `bank_hash`.

NOT IN SCOPE: re-litigating the bd-tetz retirement. `mock40-q37` stays retired either way.

title: verify-objectives topic coverage is skipped entirely when knowledge/topics.toml is absent
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs:1368 opens the L7 topic-coverage section with `if Path::new(&topics_disp).is_file() { ... }`. The else-branch at ~1443 that would catch an empty topic set ALSO requires `is_file()`. So when knowledge/topics.toml (DEFAULT_TOPICS, line 152) is absent, neither branch runs: no topic is checked, no error is raised, and the gate reports the same verdict it reports when every topic is covered.

CONTRAST: the same function DOES fail closed for its other inputs — objectives_disp and claims_disp both go through `if !Path::new(..).is_file() { return Err }` at ~1139/1142. topics_disp is the one input that was left optional without a written reason.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the same absent-input-reads-as-success shape as bd-goldens-check-is-file-hole-7v9p, which was just closed in cdcp_cli. comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: closed, but the bead's headline was ALREADY FIXED at HEAD acd4d43 and the real defect was the second clause.

WHAT THE BEAD SAID vs WHAT WAS THERE. The bead describes verify_objectives.rs:1368 wrapping the L7 topic section in 'if is_file()' with NO error on the absent branch. At acd4d43 that branch already read 'else { errors.push(missing topics registry: {topics_disp}) }' on BOTH sides — added by dff752b (wave 4), the only commit that has ever touched verify_objectives.rs; the bead was filed against the pre-dff752b state during the cdcp_cli sweep. So acceptance line 1 was met on arrival and is recorded here rather than re-claimed as work.

THE SECOND CLAUSE WAS REAL, AND WORSE THAN THE FIRST. The anti-vacuous leg was 'elif not primary_topics and topics_path.is_file() and declared'. Its is_file() conjunct locked the defence out of the single loudest way to get zero topics — the file not existing. It was harmless ONLY because a neighbouring load independently reports 'missing topics registry': the defence was standing down in favour of a check it does not name, cannot see, and would not notice the removal of. Conjunct removed on both sides; the two lines now report as two independent findings.

THE HOLE THAT WAS STILL SILENT, found by the sweep and not named in the bead: --min-items-per-topic 0 (and every negative, clamped by max(0,..)) fell straight through the comparison guard. MEASURED on the live tree with the built binary BEFORE the fix:
    PASS ... primary_topics=106 covered=106 shortfalls=0 min_per_topic=0 mode=strict ... EXIT 0
106 of 106 topics reported covered, in STRICT mode, with not one comparison performed. Now an ERROR unless --skip-topic-coverage says the floor is off on purpose; mode reports 'off'; covered= prints 'n/a' rather than a number no comparison produced. The differential harness had ALREADY been running this exact case ('m min topic 0') and passing it, because it only asserted that the two sides agree — its own header's 'a defect faithfully ported is still a defect', caught in its blind spot. That case now asserts a verdict.

THIRD HOLE: a bank item spelling topic_ids = "t-01" instead of ["t-01"] contributed zero to every tally and said nothing — QUIETER than an untagged item, because the topics it meant to cover then only soft-warn. Same for objective_ids, which also skipped the items_with_objective_ids tally the report prints. Present-but-unreadable is now an ERROR naming the item.

SIBLING AT ~1489 (policy=present/absent), as the bead asked: it is reporting, not a verdict — 'absent' means an empty exemption ledger, which is the STRICT direction. It got the one-line comment plus an ABSENT-OK: marker, not a check.

SWEEP: 24 guard sites enumerated across both implementations. 4 real holes (the three above + the elif conjunct), 3 legitimately-optional-but-unreasoned (both missing-bank_policy early returns, the policy= report test) which gained written reasons, 1 dead metric removed (objective_item_counts, computed and never compared), 16 already closed or already reasoned. Ratio of real holes: 4 in 24.

ORDERING HELD: oracle first. Differential observed RED with the new .py against the old binary — python exit 1 / rust exit 0, stdout diverging on covered= and mode=. Then the port moved; 7-case flag matrix byte-identical, py and rust exit codes equal.

KNOWN-BAD (built binary, exit code read directly, TEMP copy, live tree never touched):
  topics.toml removed              EXIT=1  both 'missing topics registry:' and 'zero topics in a required domain'
  topics.toml 0 bytes              EXIT=1  'topics.toml has zero topics in a required domain'
  --min-items-per-topic 0          EXIT=1  names the flag and the remedy
  --min-items-per-topic 0 --strict EXIT=1  and mode=strict is no longer printable

  scripts/selftest_l7_objectives.sh EXIT=0, INJECTIONS=8 unchanged - cargo test -p cdcp_gate EXIT=0, 24 binaries

META-TEST PAIR, isolated to one detector (the_anti_vacuous_leg_holds_the_line_without_its_neighbour): mutation applied to BOTH implementations (is_file() conjunct put back) -> EXIT 101. Mutation STILL IN PLACE, the 'zero topics in a required domain' needle deleted -> EXIT 0. Both restored. At whole-suite scope the same mutation was caught TWICE, independently: the named leg, and unreasoned_path_guards_are_a_defect, which flagged the reintroduced conjunct as a guard recording no error and carrying no reason.

IT STILL CANNOT DECIDE whether a topic tag is the RIGHT tag — making a malformed topic_ids an error does not make a well-formed but wrong one visible. It counts items, not coverage.
