title: The bound sweep cannot see a floor moved behind a named constant - build_glossary_json.py MIN_TERMS left the ledger silently
description:
WHAT: scripts/build_glossary_json.py used to read 'if len(terms) < 15:' and had an INVENTORY row in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs with verdict NotAModuleBound. On 2026-08-14 a sibling rebased it onto MIN_TERMS = 15 at line 46. The floor did not move. The literal did, behind a named constant, which is one of the spellings the sweep header states it cannot see.

HOW IT SURFACED: the stale row was caught by the STRICTER assertion added in bd-ggs7 - every INVENTORY row must be matched by the detector it names. The previous count-based assertion (matched.len() >= INVENTORY.len()) had gone green over the same tree hours earlier. The row was deleted with a comment recording why.

WHY IT MATTERS: MIN_TERMS is harmless (a glossary term-count floor, not a module bound). The pattern is not. Any live module bound can be made invisible to the sweep by naming it, and the sweep would then report a smaller open count without anything having been fixed. A refactor that improves the code silently shrinks the ledger.

OPTIONS:
- Detect assignments of the form NAME = 13..16 and require them to be inventoried too. Cheap, noisy, and honest.
- Or scope the claim: state in the sweep header and in the open-count assertion message that a named constant is out of scope, and accept that the count is narrower than it reads. This is already stated, but the count still reads broader than it is.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either the detector sees numeric module bounds bound to a name, with a known-bad that plants one and goes RED naming file and line, or the narrowed claim is stated at the count itself and not only in the header.
- Anti-vacuous: a detector added here must have a planted-input test proving it trips, not only the live tree.
close_reason: DETECTED, not narrowed. Shape::NamedBound added; three new hits, all adjudicated; open count still 0 and now states what it does not cover.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: closed by adding a detector, argued against narrowing the claim.

THE CHOICE. Detect the named-constant shape rather than narrow the claim in writing. The deciding fact is measured, not aesthetic: widening surfaced TWO lines nobody had in mind when the blind spot was written up — 'pub const MIN_TERMS: usize = 15;' in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/build_glossary_json.rs (the Rust port of the very gate that produced this bead) and 'const REPR_FIXED_MAX: i32 = 16;' in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/validate_grounding.rs. A narrowed CLAIM would have been accurate about the one line that prompted it and silent about the two it did not know existed. A written narrowing describes the hole; only a detector finds what is in it. The residual narrowing is still stated, at the count itself and not only in the header, because the count reads broader than three detectors.

THE DETECTOR. named_bound(line) -> Option<u32>. THE WHOLE LINE MUST BE THE BINDING: optional declaration keywords (pub/const/static/let/mut/var/readonly/export/local), a dotted identifier, an optional ': TYPE' annotation, a plain '=' (not '==', not '=>'), exactly two digits in 13..=16 not part of a longer number or a float, then end-of-line / ';' / ',' / a comment. A leading '#', '//' or '*' is refused outright — PROSE IS NOT LIVE CODE, the error this suite has made three times.

THREE NEW HITS, EACH WITH A VERDICT (measured over scripts/, crates/, web/assets/js/):
  scripts/build_glossary_json.py:46  MIN_TERMS = 15                  NotAModuleBound - the glossary TERM-count floor; the line that produced this bead
  crates/.../gates/build_glossary_json.rs:110  pub const MIN_TERMS: usize = 15;  NotAModuleBound - same floor, Rust port; found only by widening
  crates/.../gates/validate_grounding.rs:288   const REPR_FIXED_MAX: i32 = 16;   NotAModuleBound - CPython float-repr cutoff; the named twin of the already-inventoried 'decpt > 16' in verify_bank.rs
None is a module bound. PINNED OPEN COUNT STAYS 0, and its message now enumerates both what the zero covers (three shapes x three trees) and what it does not (computed bounds, config-read bounds, names bound to non-integers, tables split across files, trees outside SCANNED).

KNOWN-GOOD LEGS, one per legitimate 12-16 shape actually in this tree: the 15-minute reading-time floor (learn_chrome.js 'if (min < 15) min = 15;'), both mulberry32 shifts ('>>> 15', '>>> 14'), the 16-char hash truncation (results.js), the argparse 'default=15' (validate_grounding.py), the unnamed term-count comparison (smoke_learn_v2.py), two TOML fixture strings inside Rust source, four prose/comment forms, an equality test, a macro call, a match arm, a bound expression, 150 / 15.5 / 1400, a struct field, a tuple element. 21 cases, all assert None. Measured false positives on the live tree: ZERO.

ANTI-VACUOUS. SCANNED floors unchanged (scripts 40, crates 45, web/assets/js 12); the scan SET did not change, so they were re-measured, not re-derived: the trees hold 45, 63 and 16 files today (crates was 55 earlier the same day — it is the tree that churns, which is why its floor is not pinned to its count). the_per_tree_file_floors_reject_a_tree_that_vanished still proves each floor rejects a vanished tree.

META-TEST PAIR, real exit codes, run on a clean HEAD clone:
  mutation: appended a DEAD 'MAX_MODULE = 14' to scripts/smoke_weak_links.py. Behaviourally invisible, proven: script exit 0 before AND after, stdout byte-identical (diff exit 0). Only the detector can see it.
  leg 1 (mutation, assertion present):  cargo test --test rebase_module_bounds -> EXIT 101, 'scripts/smoke_weak_links.py:284: [named-bound] MAX_MODULE = 14 [binds 14 to a name]'
  leg 2 (mutation STILL IN PLACE, unexpected.is_empty() assertion deleted): EXIT 0, 40 passed.
Plus a planted-tree leg in the suite itself: the_sweep_goes_red_on_a_module_bound_hidden_behind_a_name plants a gate whose ceiling is 'MAX_MODULE = 14' with 'int(m[:2]) <= MAX_MODULE' below it, asserts NumericBound sees nothing there, and asserts NamedBound names file and line.

VERIFIED: rebase_module_bounds 40 passed / 0 failed on a clean HEAD clone; rustfmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean. Residual blind spot tracked as bd-ob8i.

title: verify_coverage prints its PASS verdict before a write that can still fail (class instance 3 of 3)
description:
WHAT: the third and last live instance of the PASS-above-FAIL class, found by the exhaustive census run for bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65. It arrives through a different door than the first two: the verdict is not printed above a FAIL line, it is printed above a SIDE EFFECT THAT CAN STILL FAIL.

  scripts/verify_coverage.py:335-336   status = "PASS" if not errors else "FAIL"; print(status)
  ...57 lines later...
  scripts/verify_coverage.py:393-394   out.parent.mkdir(...); out.write_text(...)   <- unguarded

  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs:1024-1025  status pushed into the out buffer
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs:1102,1105  the only fallible `?` sites after it,
                                                           each mapping to Halt

On the Python side there is no try/except in main() covering the write, so an OSError (bad path, read-only destination, ENOSPC, permissions) propagates and CPython exits 1 with a traceback underneath a stdout that already said PASS. On the Rust side Halt is not discarded: evaluate maps it to Outcome { stdout: out, stderr: traceback, code: 1 }, which PRESERVES the already-buffered PASS, and run then prints that stdout and exits 1. Stdout says PASS, the process says 1.

REACHABILITY: the path requires --write-json. check.sh invokes `cdcp_gate verify-coverage` without it, so it is dormant in CI today. It is NOT dead code: it is the documented operator command, embedded in the artifact its own `note` field prints (verify_coverage.py:383-385, "Regenerate via: python3 scripts/verify_coverage.py --write-json web/data/coverage.json").

WHY THIS IS A CLASS AND NOT A THIRD BUG: bd-lt7 fixed instance 1 (build_units.py). bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 fixed instance 2 (build_glossary_json.py plus its Rust port). This is instance 3. Three instances of one shape means the fix is a DETECTOR, not a third patch. The detector that already exists and is proven is the per-side leg qm65 added to both builder differentials:

    for (side, r) in [("python", &py), ("rust", &rs)] {
        if r.code != 0 { assert!(!r.out().contains("PASS"), ...); }
    }

asserted PER SIDE rather than only across the two, because a differential only catches a regression that lands on one side, and two implementations that both regress agree with each other perfectly. That leg was proven to be the detector by a mutation pair: mutate BOTH sides to print PASS first and the suite goes non-zero on 3 cases; delete the leg with the mutation still in place and the suite returns to zero.

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify_coverage.py and verify_coverage.rs both compose the report AFTER the --write-json write, so a failed write cannot land under a PASS. Both sides move together, PYTHON FIRST, and the verify_coverage differential is watched go RED before the port follows.
- The no-success-token-on-a-non-zero-path leg is added to the verify_coverage differential harness, per side, matching the two builder harnesses.
- A meta-test pair proves that leg is the detector: mutate both implementations back, suite non-zero; delete the assertion with the mutation STILL IN PLACE, suite zero.
- The census that found this is re-run and reports ZERO remaining instances, so the class is CLOSED rather than decremented.

NOT IN SCOPE, recorded so it is not re-derived:
- verify_objectives writes a provisional PASS into its JSON summary before later errors could be appended, but the only thing that appends after that point is the write-failure handler, which uses `if let Err(e)` rather than `?`. A successful write therefore implies exit 0, and a failed write implies stdout FAIL. The one residual hole is a torn file from a mid-write ENOSPC, which is not a verdict surface a reader trusts. Both ports get this right and are commented for it.
- scripts/verify_content_lock.py:348 prints an `ok` line inside a `try` whose `finally` can raise PermissionError. Same class, negligible probability, no action.

FOUND BY: exhaustive census of scripts/*.{py,sh,mjs}, crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs, crates/*/src/**/*.rs and hooks/ during bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65, tracing forward from every success print to every reachable exit. check.sh is clean (fail() exits 2, so no `ok` line is reachable after a failure). All 12 selftest_*.sh, the .mjs smokes, and the remaining 16 Rust gates are clean.
close_reason: verdict composed after the write in both implementations; per-side detector added and proven by a mutation pair (101 -> 0); general detector argued and filed as bd-j8b2 [bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n]

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: FIXED and verified. Both implementations now COMPOSE the report into a buffer and emit it only after the --write-json side effect has succeeded. A failed write prints NOTHING and exits non-zero. The write is atomic (temp file beside the target, then rename), so a refused or torn write leaves no partial artifact.

RED-BEFORE-PORT, observed: Python first, diff_verify_coverage RED on 13 of 17 (the same change also carried the approved-pool fix from bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh); port followed, back to green.

KNOWN-BAD, both sides, two doors, four-tuple read from the emitted exit code:
  (a) --write-json whose PARENT IS A FILE (mkdir refuses)
      python exit=1 stdout=0 bytes stderr=1170 bytes artifact=NO tmp_residue=NO
      rust   exit=1 stdout=0 bytes stderr=147 bytes  artifact=NO tmp_residue=NO   stdout IDENTICAL
  (b) --write-json TARGET IS A DIRECTORY (the atomic rename refuses AFTER the temp write — the leg that proves the cleanup)
      python exit=1 stdout=0 bytes tmp_residue=NO
      rust   exit=1 stdout=0 bytes tmp_residue=NO   stdout IDENTICAL
  the SAME failing write against the PRE-FIX implementation: exit=1, first stdout line 'PASS', 642 bytes of report.
Chosen over a chmod because a file-as-parent and a directory-as-target are deterministic and cannot be defeated by running as root — an injection that silently stops injecting is the failure this file exists to prevent.

DETECTOR, added per side to every case in the harness: assert_no_success_token_on_a_failing_path, keyed on SUCCESS_TOKENS = [PASS, coverage GREEN]. Per side and not merely across the two, because a differential only catches a regression that lands on ONE side — and that is not hypothetical here: the Python printed above an unguarded write and the Rust buffered the same verdict into Outcome.stdout, which Halt preserves. The two agreed, byte for byte, on a PASS above exit 1.

META-TEST PAIR, real exit codes:
  1. MUTANT-A planted on BOTH implementations (the printed verdict is always the success token; exit codes, the JSON status field, stdout emptiness and artifacts all untouched, so only the verdict-shape leg can catch it)
     -> cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test diff_verify_coverage  EXIT 101, 12 failed / 11 passed, all 12 on 'with the success token'
  2. MUTANT-A STILL IN PLACE, the single assertion deleted
     -> EXIT 0, 23 passed / 0 failed
  3. both restored -> EXIT 0, 23 passed. grep for MUTANT in the three files: 0.
Nothing else in the suite catches that mutation, which is what makes this the detector rather than a coincidence.

GENERAL DETECTOR — ARGUED, NOT SKIPPED, and filed as bd-j8b2. The static form (grep for a success token on a path reachable by a non-zero exit) is rejected: sound analysis needs interprocedural reachability across two languages, and the cheap approximation fires on every CORRECT gate (verify_coverage.py buffers PASS and returns 1 from the same function, correctly). Re-running the census with an AST scan produced exactly the predicted false positives — verify_injection_count.py:275 matched because a FAIL message QUOTES the word GREEN, and fetch_public_corpus.py:167 matched a per-item progress line. That is the same fooling recorded in the bd-0czh comment in this very file. The shared-composition-helper form is sound but opt-in and does not cross the Python/Rust boundary. The tractable form is a META-GATE asserting every diff_*.rs carries the per-side leg; measured 2026-08-14 that is 3 of 11 harnesses, so landing it would have turned EIGHT sibling-owned files RED mid-swarm for a defect none of them has been shown to have. bd-j8b2 carries the measurement, the roster, and the per-gate-token problem the implementer must solve.

CENSUS RE-RUN: AST scan over scripts/*.py plus a narrowed scan of the eight Rust gates that write a file. ZERO remaining genuine instances. The residual verify_content_lock.py:348 hole this bead already recorded as no-action is unchanged. The class is CLOSED for shipped code; bd-j8b2 is what keeps a FOURTH instance from being written tomorrow.

title: verify-coverage counts retired items toward module floors — it measures the file set, not the drawable pool
description:
WHAT: `cdcp_gate verify-coverage` and `cdcp_gate verify-bank` count every FILE under `bank/items`
toward the per-module floors in `knowledge/bank_policy.toml`. They do not filter on `status`. So
they measure a pool no learner is ever assessed from.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, immediately after bd-tetz retired 24 duplicates:

    verify-coverage:  m14: 44 (min 24) [ok]        <- 44 files
    actual drawable:  m14: 42 approved             <- what cdcp_assemble can sample
    verify-bank:      modules={... 14: 44 ...}     <- same file count
    near-duplicate-items: 804 item file(s) · 779 approved

C1 restricts assembly to `approved` items (`cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids`), and C2 folded
`status` into `hash_payload` precisely because the approved/retired split decides what a learner
can be assessed on. The coverage gate is the one place that asserts a module has ENOUGH items, and
it is measuring the other set.

NO LIVE BREACH TODAY — checked, and this is why it is a bug rather than an incident. Approved-only
counts after the 24 retirements, against their floors:

    m05 30/14  m06 130/55  m07 31/14  m08 32/18  m09 117/48  m10 33/12
    m11 69/30  m12 61/28   m13 46/22  m14 42/24  (all other modules unchanged)

Every module clears its floor on the approved pool as well. The defect is that the gate WOULD NOT
HAVE SAID SO if one did not: a module could be retired below its floor and `verify-coverage` would
print `[ok]` while `cdcp_assemble` quietly assembled a narrower exam. The gate reports a number
that is guaranteed to be >= the number it should be reporting, which is the fail-open direction.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: before bd-tetz the bank held exactly one non-approved item, so
file count and approved count differed by one and no reader would notice. It is 25 now, and will
grow every time a duplicate is adjudicated.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `verify-coverage` counts `status == "approved"` items against `domain_min`, and its output names
  BOTH numbers (files scanned, approved counted) so the two can never be confused again.
- Anti-vacuous, per house rule: a module with zero approved items is an ERROR naming the module,
  never a `[ok]` on a file count.
- Known-bad injection: retire a temp module below its floor -> the gate goes RED naming that
  module. Meta-test: delete the filter -> the injection test fails.
- Decide the same question for `verify-bank`'s `modules={...}` and `correct_dist={...}` summaries.
  Correct-letter diversity over a pool that includes retired items is measuring the wrong pool for
  the same reason. If the file-count view is deliberate there, say so in the output.
- `scripts/verify_coverage.py` (the differential oracle, if it still exists) moves in the same
  change or the diff test goes RED — do not let the two sides disagree about which pool they count.
close_reason: floors measure the approved pool; before/after table recorded, no breach, no floor lowered; known-bad proven against the pre-fix binary [bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh]

comments.author: josh
comments.text:

BEFORE/AFTER, every module, live tree (804 files, 779 approved, 25 retired). Format module: files->approved/floor:
  m01 36->36/20  m02 42->42/28  m03 38->38/20  m04 33->33/18  m05 31->30/14
  m06 136->130/55  m07 32->31/14  m08 34->32/18  m09 121->117/48  m10 35->33/12
  m11 72->69/30  m12 63->61/28  m13 48->46/22  m14 44->42/24  m15 39->39/16

title: web/data/bank_items_seed42.json ships 25 retired items to the browser
description:
WHAT: `web/data/bank_items_seed42.json` is the full bank array serialised straight off `BankItem`
and shipped to the browser for the WASM grade path. After bd-tetz it carries 804 elements of which
**25 have `status = "retired"`** — items `cdcp_assemble` can never draw, in a pack whose whole
purpose is grading a 40-item draw.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, parsed from the committed pack:

    len(bank_items_seed42.json)         = 804
    statuses present                    = ["approved", "retired"]
    elements with status == "retired"   = 25
    items the seed-42 form actually uses = 40

THREE REASONS THIS IS WORTH DECIDING RATHER THAN LEAVING:

 1. It is the only place a retired item reaches a learner's browser. Nothing in the current web
    code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids, so there is no live bug — but the pack is the
    input to any future "review the whole bank" or "search items" surface, and the first such
    surface will silently include withdrawn duplicates. A retired item is retired BECAUSE a better
    copy of the same proposition exists; showing it is showing the copy that lost.
 2. It carries the retired items' full text, so the 24 duplicate stems and keys are still shipped
    beside their survivors — the exact adjacency the retirement was meant to remove.
 3. The count is a trap. `registries/goldens-couplings.toml` used to describe this file as "the
    full 804-item array"; that row was rewritten under bd-tetz to say 804 is a FILE count and 779
    is the drawable pool, but the pack itself still hands 804 to anyone who calls `.length`.

NOT FIXED HERE because `export_web` lives in `crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs`, outside the bank/goldens
surface bd-tetz owned, and the pack's byte content is `cmp`d by `scripts/check.sh` L6 — changing
what it contains is a goldens re-freeze plus a coupling walk, which is a decision, not a tidy-up.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide, and record in the `web.bank-items-pack` row of `registries/goldens-couplings.toml`:
  does this pack ship the drawable pool (779) or the file set (804)?
- If it becomes approved-only, `export.pack-shapes` moves, the pack re-freezes, and all three web
  goldens re-affirm through the block in `goldens/PROVENANCE.md`, in order.
- Either way the pack gains something a reader can check the count against — an envelope field, or
  a `status` the consumer is required to read — so `.length` stops being quotable as the item count.
- Whatever is decided, `cdcp_wasm`'s dual-path test must still pass: the grade path needs every id
  the fixture draws, and only those.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: DECIDED + GUARDED here; the two live learner-facing defects filed as bd-7big (P0) and bd-qqwc (P1).

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND MEASUREMENT DISPROVED IT. It said 'nothing in the current web code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids, so there is no live bug'. There is. Two independent live exposures:

1. MODULE QUIZ (bd-7big, P0). web/assets/js/quiz.js filterByModule() filters by numeric module ONLY, never status. Transcribed its mulberry32 sampler + seed derivation (42 + module*1000, +15 for learn15) into node and ran it against the committed pack — the draw is deterministic, so these are exact, not probabilistic: 8 retired items served across the 30 module quizzes, 6 of 15 default quizzes affected (m05-q200, mock40-q18, mock40-q24, mock40-q22, m12-q219, mock40-q37; learn15: m05-q200, mock40-q40). The learner is SCORED on them: gradeByKeys counts them, WASM gradeDigest digests them, recordGradedWrongs pushes misses into cdcp.drill.missed.v1 + SRS, recordQuizResult feeds mastery.
2. LEARN-PAGE UNIT CHECKS (bd-qqwc, P1). build_units never reads status, so web/data/units_index.json already bakes retired ids into check_item_ids: 05-lighting__formulas-rules-of-thumb -> m05-q200, 11-network__formulas-rules-of-thumb -> m11-q226.

THE DECISION IS FORCED, NOT STYLISTIC — and this is why 'just filter the export' would have been a product outage. cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds the pack bytes to Bank::from_json_str which RECOMPUTES bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade HARD-FAILS on mismatch. Measured with cdcp bank-hash: 804-file bank = 3404d854..., 779 approved-only pool = b81a0019... (pre-bump). - manifest row missing status -> ERROR, asserted on the SERIALIZED BYTES not the struct (pre-C2 serde dropped the field and nothing noticed).
- ANTI-VACUOUS: empty drawn form / empty bank / zero approved -> ERROR.
KNOWN-BAD PROVEN: mark drawn item m01-q207 retired, re-export via --fixture -> exit 1, RED, naming it; baseline exit 0. All-retired bank -> exit 1 both paths. Empty bank -> exit 1.
COUNT CONFLATION KILLED: export-web now prints manifest_rows=804 / approved_pool=779 / drawn_form=40 side by side, so .length is no longer quotable as the item count.

Pack bytes UNCHANGED (abb804e3...) — it carries no bank_hash field, so the v2 domain bump left it byte-identical; it re-affirms bank.hash-payload at the new version anyway. Ledger GREEN 8 goldens (added the wasm row, bd-wasm-outside-coupling-ledger-9uft). Dual-path test green: grade path has every id the fixture draws.

title: Tree red at wave close: workspace will not compile (rebase_module_bounds) and substrate-guard exits 4
description:
WHAT: observed while landing bd-tetz, 2026-08-14. NOT bd-tetz's to fix — every file named here is
outside the bank/goldens surface and is being edited by a sibling right now. Filed so the state is
on the record rather than in one agent's report, and so nobody re-derives it.

Three separate reds, all in the same wave, all in `cdcp_gate`:

1. **The workspace does not compile.** `cargo test --workspace` exits 101 before running anything:

       crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs:511, :545, :546
       error[E0308]: expected a tuple with 5 elements, found one with 4
       expected `(&str, &str, Shape, Verdict, &str)`

   A 5th field was added to the fixture tuple and three closure patterns were not updated. Every
   per-crate suite passes when run individually, which is how it was missed.

2. **`cdcp_gate substrate-guard` exits 4 on the live tree** — so `scripts/check.sh` is RED at its

       ERROR: staged snapshot — registries/substrate_allowlist.toml: [scan].extensions is
       missing the compiled-in floor "pyw" | ... "bash" | ... "zsh" | ... "ksh"
       — the registry may widen the scan, never narrow it

   The gate's compiled-in extension floor was widened; the registry was not. Both halves have to

3. **`cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test substrate_guard_e2e` exits 101, 4 tests failing** —

EVERYTHING ELSE IS GREEN, measured with the built binary rather than `cargo run`:
`cargo test -p` green for cdcp_bank, cdcp_assemble, cdcp_core, cdcp_grade, cdcp_cli, cdcp_wasm;

the compiled-in floor. Close this bead when `cargo test --workspace` and `scripts/check.sh` are

close_reason:
STALE — filed mid-wave against a transient state, resolved before the wave closed. It described the working tree at roughly 23:00 on 2026-08-14, while the substrate-floor and module-bounds agents were mid-edit: cargo test --workspace exited 101 on rebase_module_bounds tuple arity and substrate-guard exited 4 because the index snapshot still carried the pre-widening allowlist.

Both were in-flight edits, not defects. The substrate exit 4 in particular was the TWO-SNAPSHOT RULE WORKING: the gate judges the subject and the policy from the SAME snapshot, and the staged snapshot legitimately still held HEAD's registry until both files were staged together.

Verified resolved: tick 10 (acd4d43) committed with check.sh exit 0, 76 ok-steps, 39 workspace test targets green, L4 WASM=GREEN.

KEEPING THE LESSON RATHER THAN JUST THE CLOSE: a bead filed against a concurrent tree state is a bead about a moment, not about the repo. The filing agent was right to surface it — it explicitly marked it 'sibling in-flight, not mine' — but the correct destination for that observation is the wave report, not the backlog, because nobody downstream can act on it and it reads like a standing defect. title: doc-facts: two prose surfaces carry present-tense claims no gate can see
description:
WHAT: two markdown surfaces are excluded from the doc-facts trigger obligation and their present-tense claims about code are therefore unguarded.

1. course-engine/goldens/PROVENANCE.md — lines 82, 169, 182, 199 make live present-tense claims about hash_payload, deny_unknown_fields and StdRng. Excluded because goldens/ has exactly one regeneration path and a sibling bead was re-freezing bank_hash through it during B3. A marker edit from this gate would put two workflows in one single-owner file.

2. course-engine/beads_compliance_audit/ — excluded by directory prefix. Its files are dated snapshots (**Date:** headers) whose sentences are past-tense by construction, and new passes land continuously, so an exact-path list would break the build on unrelated work. COST: a genuinely present-tense claim written into that tree is invisible.

WHY: both exclusions carry reason strings in registries/doc-facts.toml, which is the honest form, but a reasoned exclusion is still an uncovered surface. Naming them here is the difference between a known gap and a silent one.

ACCEPTANCE
- goldens/PROVENANCE.md either carries doc-facts markers (once the bank_hash re-freeze has landed and the file has one owner again) or the exclusion reason is rewritten to say why it never will.
- beads_compliance_audit/ snapshots either get a machine-readable as-of stamp that lets the gate treat them as past-tense, or the prefix exclusion stays with its cost restated.
- Either way, cdcp_gate doc-facts stays green and the reason strings still name what is out of reach.

title: Wire cdcp_gate doc-facts into scripts/check.sh (BUILT != WIRED)
description:
WHAT: the doc-facts gate (bd-hardening-b-ledgers-gvm.3) is built, tested and green on the live tree, but nothing in scripts/check.sh runs it. Until it does, a stale present-tense claim about code still merges.

WHY: B1 records the whole lattice on this distinction — a capability is gate-wired only when a step in check.sh fails red. A gate that exists and is not called reports exactly like one that passed, which is the failure class this milestone exists to close.

EXACT LINES, to go immediately after the capability-maturity step (same block, same style):

  step "doc-facts (prose claims about code match the tree)" \
    "$ENGINE/target/debug/cdcp_gate --root $ENGINE doc-facts"

Substitute the repos actual step/invocation helper — the requirement is only that a non-zero exit from `cdcp_gate doc-facts` fails check.sh, and that the step is unconditional (no skip-on-missing-toolchain branch: the gate needs nothing but the repo).

ACCEPTANCE
- ./scripts/check.sh runs `cdcp_gate doc-facts` and its ok-step count rises by one.
- Flipping one marker polarity in docs/ turns check.sh RED, and the failure line names the file, the line, the prose polarity and the tree polarity.
- registries/capability-maturity.toml can then honestly carry a doc-facts row at gate-wired or better, evidencing crates/cdcp_gate/tests/doc_facts_e2e.rs known-bad legs.
close_reason: WIRED. scripts/check.sh now runs 'cdcp_gate doc-facts' immediately after goldens-couplings; check.sh exits 0 at 76 ok-steps with it on the path. BUILT != WIRED closed by the step existing and running, not by the gate being green in isolation.

title: CHARTER.md narrative claims about code fall between capability-maturity and doc-facts
description:
WHAT: CHARTER.md is covered by capability-maturity only where a row quotes a TABLE CELL via charter_claim. Its narrative prose is covered by nothing.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, CHARTER.md:152, inside the L5 cell but written as narrative: "`fuzz/` is outside the workspace, so no `check.sh` step, no CI job and no `cargo test --workspace` ever builds or runs those targets." That sentence is a present-tense claim about Cargo.toml and check.sh. B1 compares the cell STATUS ("PARTIAL · property only") verbatim and never reads the sentence; doc-facts registers no row against CHARTER.md by deliberate division of labour, so two gates never argue over one cell.

The same claim IS covered elsewhere: docs/TESTING.md now carries [[fact:fact-fuzz-is-a-workspace-member=no]] against a toml_array_contains probe on workspace.members. So the fact is guarded — the CHARTER copy of it is not, and CHARTER is the document a reader trusts most.

Same shape applies to README.md, which was not surveyed for present-tense code claims in this tick.

ACCEPTANCE
- A decision is recorded, in one place, on which gate owns CHARTER.md narrative prose (extend capability-maturity to a narrative leg, or let doc-facts register CHARTER rows with an explicit non-overlap rule against charter_claim cells).
- README.md is surveyed for present-tense claims about code and each is either registered in registries/doc-facts.toml or named as out of reach with a reason.
- Whichever way it goes, no cell is checked by two gates and no sentence by none.

title: Substrate floor is client-side only: no commit path except plain `git commit` runs the hook, and nothing enforces on the pushed ref
description:
WHAT: bd-xmn5 closed the FILENAME half of the substrate floor (case, extension family, whole-tree scope, shebang, symlink/gitlink). The COMMIT-PATH half is deferred here because it lives in install_hooks.rs, scripts/check.sh and CI, none of which bd-xmn5 owned.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, git 2.53.0, in a clone of this repo with hooks/pre-commit INSTALLED and confirmed firing on an ordinary commit (exit 1, gate named the file). Each of the following created a commit carrying an unlisted scripts/payload*.py with the hook NEVER INVOKED (hook-fire counter stayed 0):
  git merge --no-ff side                      -> exit 0
  git cherry-pick feature                     -> exit 0
  git rebase rebasetarget                     -> exit 0
  git am 0001-payload3-on-side.patch          -> exit 0
  git commit-tree $(git write-tree) -p HEAD   -> exit 0
  git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit      -> exit 0
  git commit --no-verify                      -> exit 0
Also: a fresh clone has NO .git/hooks/pre-commit at all (ls -> rc 1), and the committed shim is mode 100644 in the index.

WHAT ALREADY COVERS IT: the PRESENCE leg. Every one of the above was caught by `cdcp_gate substrate-guard` on the resulting tree (exit 2, file named). So these are DELAYED detection, not invisibility — provided check.sh or cargo test runs. That is why this is deferred rather than urgent.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING: an enforcement point that a client cannot skip.
Options, cheapest first:
 1. install-hooks also installs pre-merge-commit / pre-applypatch shims (does NOT cover the sequencer or plumbing).
 2. A required GitHub check on the pushed ref. The workflow already runs check.sh; making it REQUIRED on the branch is the real boundary.
 3. A pre-receive hook, if a server we control ever hosts this.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either a server-side/required-check boundary exists, or a written decision that client-side-only is accepted and why.
- Every doc, header and commit message that says 'refused at commit' says WHICH commit path (substrate_guard.rs's header already does as of bd-xmn5; the rest of the tree has not been swept).
- If option 1 is taken, a known-bad per newly installed hook.

title: CI is RED at install-hooks --check: actions/checkout never installs the shim, and nothing in check.sh installs it either
description:
WHAT: scripts/check.sh line 313-315 runs `cdcp_gate install-hooks --check` and hard-fails. .github/workflows/check.yml runs check.sh on a fresh actions/checkout@v4, which has no .git/hooks/pre-commit. Nothing between the checkout and that line installs one.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 on a fresh clone of this repo (the closest local analogue of a CI checkout):
  git clone --no-hardlinks <repo> fresh
  ./target/debug/cdcp_gate --root fresh/course-engine install-hooks --check
  -> exit 2: '.../fresh/.git/hooks/pre-commit: NOT INSTALLED (BUILT != WIRED)'
So check.sh cannot get past step 313 in CI. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/repo_surface.rs::the_pre_commit_shim_is_installed_in_this_clone is the same failure by a second route, inside `cargo fmt/clippy/test` at line 436.

WHY IT MATTERS BOTH WAYS: a gate that is RED for an environmental reason on every run teaches the reader to ignore the colour. It is also the reason nobody has noticed that the hook is not, and cannot be, the enforcement point in CI (see bd-efm7).

FIX (one line, in the file bd-xmn5 was not allowed to edit):
  scripts/check.sh, immediately before line 313:
    echo "==> cdcp_gate install-hooks (a fresh clone has no hook; CI is a fresh clone)"
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- install-hooks || fail "install-hooks"
  install-hooks is idempotent (State::Installed prints 'already matches' and exits 0), so this is a no-op on a developer machine.

ALTERNATIVE if check.sh must not mutate .git/: add an explicit CI step before check.sh in .github/workflows/check.yml. Do NOT relax install-hooks --check; a --check that cannot fail is the fooled certificate this repo keeps finding.

ACCEPTANCE:
- install-hooks --check is GREEN in CI because the hook is genuinely installed, never because the step was weakened or skipped.
- A CI run is observed passing that step (not inferred).
close_reason:
FIXED IN THIS TICK, not deferred. scripts/check.sh now runs 'cdcp_gate install-hooks' immediately before 'install-hooks --check'. install-hooks is idempotent so it is a no-op on a developer machine, and it is the thing that makes the --check line meaningful in CI.

WHY THIS WAS A P0: the split was the worst possible shape. A fresh clone has no .git/hooks/pre-commit, and CI IS a fresh clone — so --check exited 2 on every CI run and 0 on every machine where anyone would notice. A gate that is red exactly where nobody looks and green exactly where everybody does is not a gate, it is a habit of ignoring one CI step.

Verified: check.sh exits 0 at 76 ok-steps with both lines on the path.

title: Decide whether the substrate floor covers the browser surface: 16 tracked .js/.mjs are outside it by deliberate omission
description:
WHAT: bd-xmn5 set the substrate floor's extension family to py/pyw/sh/bash/zsh/ksh and DELIBERATELY left js/mjs out. That decision is recorded in substrate_guard.rs's SCOPE DECISION section and in registries/substrate_allowlist.toml, and it is a decision, not an oversight — but it is unratified.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: `git ls-files` under course-engine reports 16 tracked files under web/assets/js and 4 .mjs under scripts/ (smoke_srs.mjs, smoke_mastery.mjs, smoke_hub_mastery.mjs, smoke_results_wasm.mjs). The four scripts/*.mjs ARE invoked by scripts/check.sh (`node scripts/smoke_srs.mjs || fail ...`), so they are load-bearing gates in a non-Rust language, exactly like the Python ones that carry rows.

THE ARGUMENT FOR LEAVING THEM OUT: web/assets/js is the browser surface and its migration story is wasm, not a port to a cdcp_gate subcommand; folding it into the substrate allowlist would make the row count stop meaning 'python/shell debt'.
THE ARGUMENT AGAINST: scripts/*.mjs is not the browser surface. It is four node gates on the check.sh path with no reason, no bead and no expiry, which is the precise state the substrate floor exists to end.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision, in substrate_guard.rs's header, either way.
- If mjs comes in: 'mjs' added to FLOOR_EXTENSIONS, four rows added with real reasons, and a known-bad showing an unlisted scripts/x.mjs go RED.
- If it stays out: the header says WHY the four check.sh node gates are not debt, in a sentence a reviewer can disagree with.

title: check.sh invokes nine gates through cargo run, so a sibling's build warning is indistinguishable from gate output
description:
WHAT: scripts/check.sh invokes every Rust gate as `cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- <gate>`. Nine call sites. Raised by the bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.11/.12 port agent, which was required to use the built binary in its own differentials for exactly this reason.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY IT IS P2 NOT P1: cargo writes build diagnostics to stderr, so a compile warning from an unrelated crate arrives interleaved with gate output. In a DIFFERENTIAL that is fatal — it reads as divergence, and it cost this project a false conclusion during wave 6. In check.sh the gates are invoked as `|| fail`, so contamination cannot change the verdict; the cost is ATTRIBUTION. A gate that fails because the workspace does not compile reports identically to a gate that fails because it found a violation. During a six-agent wave, that difference is the whole diagnosis.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: this exact confusion occurred while wiring wave 7. `substrate-guard` reported FAIL twice for two entirely different reasons (a staged-snapshot registry mismatch, then a nested --prove-wired child transcript leaking into the parent log) and both looked the same at a glance.

ACCEPTANCE:
- One explicit `cargo build -p cdcp_gate -p cdcp_cli --locked` step early, with its own ok line, so a compile failure is ITS failure and names itself.
- The nine gate call sites invoke ./target/debug/<bin> directly.
- The build step and the invocations agree on profile; a missing binary is an ERROR naming the build step, never a silent skip or a fallback to cargo run.
- Known-bad: plant a compile error in a crate the gates do not use, and confirm the failure names the build step rather than a gate.
- Anti-vacuous: if the binary is absent the step must fail, not fall back.
- Note the interaction with the nested --prove-wired child, which runs a full check.sh: whatever build step is added must be idempotent and must not recurse pathologically.

title: rebase_module_bounds.rs runs build_units.py against the LIVE tree during a test
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs (around line 684, before the bd-ggs7 rewrite) invokes scripts/build_units.py against the LIVE tree, which writes web/data/units_index.json during a test run. Found by the builder-port agent while it was being held to the opposite standard.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is precisely the pattern the differential harnesses were built to avoid, and the reason is not hypothetical. A test that writes a TRACKED artifact (a) makes `git status` a function of whether you have run the tests, (b) can mask a stale committed artifact by silently refreshing it, and (c) races every concurrent agent in a multi-agent wave — this repo runs six at a time.

THE ESTABLISHED CORRECT SHAPE, already implemented twice in tests/diff_build_units.rs and tests/diff_build_glossary_json.rs: materialise a tree COPY in temp, run there, and assert the produced bytes EQUAL the tracked artifact. That read-only comparison is strictly STRONGER than running live — it proves the committed artifact is current, which running live cannot, because running live makes it current.

NOTE: bd-ggs7 rewrote this file after the finding was reported. Re-confirm the invocation still exists before working it; if the rewrite removed it, close with the measurement rather than assuming.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No test writes a tracked artifact. Verify by running the full suite on a clean tree and asserting `git status --porcelain` is empty afterwards — that assertion is the real acceptance and it should become a test of its own.
- The live-tree invocation is replaced with the temp-copy + compare-to-tracked shape.
- Sweep the rest of the test suite for the same pattern and report the count; one instance found by a passing agent is rarely the only one.
- Anti-vacuous: a temp fixture that produces zero bytes is an ERROR, not a pass.
close_reason: CONFIRMED still present, replaced with the temp-copy + compare-to-tracked shape. Full suite on a clean tree now touches ZERO tracked files.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: the invocation still existed and is gone.

RE-CONFIRMED BEFORE WORKING IT, as the bead asked. After the bd-ggs7 rewrite the live-tree run was at crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs:1115 in build_units_known_good_the_live_tree_passes_over_all_declared_modules: capture(Command::new('python3').arg(root.join('scripts/build_units.py'))). scripts/build_units.py line 568 writes OUT = ROOT/web/data/units_index.json on the green path, ROOT being Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] — the live tree.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS MOST, because it changes how this class must be checked. On a clean HEAD clone, with the defect still in place, the full suite left 'git status --porcelain' EMPTY — and the mtime of web/data/units_index.json MOVED. The write happened; it was invisible because the tracked artifact was already current. A tree-cleanliness assertion cannot see an idempotent write, and an idempotent write is no less a race against six concurrent agents, and no less able to refresh a stale artifact instead of reporting it. So the acceptance below is asserted on mtimes as well as on porcelain.

THE FIX. live_units_fixture() byte-copies the four inputs build_units.py resolves off its own root plus every web/content/modules/*.md, with an anti-vacuous floor of 14 module files. The gate runs THERE; its write lands in the fixture. The leg then asserts the produced bytes are non-empty and byte-identical to the tracked web/data/units_index.json — which is strictly STRONGER than the live run it replaces, because running live MAKES the artifact current and therefore proves nothing about it, while the comparison PROVES the committed artifact is current without touching it. The module-15 assertions the leg existed for are unchanged.

THE REAL ACCEPTANCE, run in an isolated clone (five siblings are editing the live tree, so it could not be run there — the tree also carries an in-flight 197-line rewrite of verify_coverage.py):
  clean clone at HEAD acd4d43 + this file, fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR
  cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast   -> FULL_SUITE_EXIT=101
  git status --porcelain                  -> EMPTY
  find -newer <pre-run mark>              -> ZERO tracked files
The 101 is five isolation artifacts of the clone itself, none of them a write and none in this file: two capability-maturity rows whose commit evidence 467b429 a fresh 'git init' cannot name, two doc-facts exclusions pointing at the gitignored beads_compliance_audit/, and repo_surface's pre-commit shim not installed in a fresh clone. rebase_module_bounds itself: 40 passed, 0 failed.

SUITE-WIDE SWEEP FOR THE SAME PATTERN. Count of tests that WRITE a tracked artifact: ZERO, by the mtime sweep above, which is exhaustive in a way a text scan is not. Live-tree RUNS are a broader and healthier set — the checkers, which read the shipped tree and write nothing: this file runs verify_coverage.py (twice) and smoke_weak_links.py; diff_verify_doc_consistency.rs runs its oracle and the binary against the engine root five times through a helper; capability_maturity_e2e, doc_facts_e2e, repo_surface and the diff_* harnesses run the BINARY against the live root. None writes.

THE COMPILED GUARD. LIVE_RUNS ledgers every command in this file that resolves a script off the ENGINE root, each row answering one question — DOES IT WRITE — and a final assertion that no row answers yes. A live run is not forbidden (forbidding it would be over-strict; three legs here are checkers and running them against the shipped tree is their strongest form); an UNARGUED one is. That is exactly the step skipped when this instance entered. Its scan is compile-time (include_str! of this file), anti-vacuous (fewer than 2 found is an ERROR), and honest about its reach: it sees THIS file and paths spelled '.join("scripts/…")', not runs hidden behind a helper such as python_script() in diff_verify_doc_consistency.rs.

META-TEST PAIR for that guard, real exit codes, clean clone:
  mutation: a DEAD #[allow(dead_code)] fn planted_live_run() containing Command::new('python3').arg(engine_root().join('scripts/build_units.py')). Never called, so only the source scan can see it.
  leg 1 (assertion present): EXIT 101, '1 live-tree run(s) are not in LIVE_RUNS: ["scripts/build_units.py"]'
  leg 2 (mutation STILL IN PLACE, unledgered.is_empty() deleted): EXIT 0, 40 passed.

NOT DONE, filed instead: bd-conu — verify_coverage.py's --policy defaults to the LIVE knowledge/bank_policy.toml, so a fixture run with isolated --bank/--domains silently reads the shipped tree. Same coupling class, READ direction. It is the reason three legs in this file are RED against the live tree today and GREEN against a clean clone.

title: verify_coverage.py --policy defaults to the LIVE knowledge/bank_policy.toml, so fixture runs silently read the shipped tree
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_coverage.py line 116 sets DEFAULT_POLICY = ROOT / 'knowledge' / 'bank_policy.toml' where ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] — the LIVE engine root — and argparse uses it as the --policy default (line 373). A test that hands the gate an isolated --bank and --domains but no --policy therefore gets the SHIPPED policy file mixed into its fixture.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 while working bd-8mjs: three legs in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs went RED against the live tree and GREEN against a clean HEAD clone. The failing reports name '[[domain_min]] module 3..14 is not a required module in the domain registry' — twelve findings that come from the live knowledge/bank_policy.toml, not from the two-module fixture registry the case built. The report even prints policy=present for a call site that passed no --policy at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the live-tree coupling class of bd-rebase-bounds-live-tree-write-ohgr, in the READ direction. A gate that reaches outside the root it was pointed at cannot be given a known-bad honestly: every fixture case is silently a fixture PLUS whatever the shipped tree happens to hold that day, so a case can go RED for a reason the case did not inject, and — worse — a case could go GREEN because the live policy supplied something the fixture forgot. The failures are not deterministic across trees, which is how they showed up as a mid-wave surprise rather than in CI.

NOTE: verify_coverage.py is under active edit right now (197 insertions over acd4d43 as of 2026-08-14). This is filed rather than fixed because the owning agent is mid-change.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The policy path is resolved against the SAME root the bank and domains came from, or --policy has no default and its absence means 'no policy' rather than 'the shipped one'.
- A known-bad proving it: a fixture with an isolated --bank/--domains and no --policy must produce findings that mention ONLY modules the fixture registry declares. Today it names modules 3-14.
- The three legs in rebase_module_bounds.rs (verify_coverage_known_bad_a_declared_module_with_no_items_trips, verify_coverage_known_bad_an_exemption_without_a_reason_is_an_error, verify_coverage_known_good_a_recorded_exemption_with_a_reason_is_honoured) go green again without being weakened.

title: Module quiz draws RETIRED items and SCORES learners on them (quiz.js filters by module only)
description:
WHAT: web/assets/js/quiz.js filterByModule() filters web/data/bank_items_seed42.json by the numeric `module` field ONLY. It never reads `status`. The manifest ships all 804 bank files including 25 status="retired", so the module-quiz draw pool includes withdrawn items.

THIS IS LIVE AND LEARNER-FACING. bd-web-pack-ships-retired-items-4ivb assumed 'there is no live bug — nothing in the current web code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids'. That assumption is WRONG and was disproven by measurement.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 by transcribing quiz.js sampleItems() (mulberry32 + Fisher-Yates) and its seed derivation (42 + module*1000, +15 for mode=learn15) faithfully into node and running it against the COMMITTED pack. The draw is fully deterministic, so these are not probabilities — they are the exact items served:

  default 8-12 quizzes: module 5 -> m05-q200, module 6 -> mock40-q18, module 8 -> mock40-q24,
                        module 10 -> mock40-q22, module 12 -> m12-q219, module 13 -> mock40-q37
  mode=learn15 (5 Q):   module 5 -> m05-q200, module 14 -> mock40-q40

8 retired items served across the 30 deterministic module quizzes; 6 of 15 default module quizzes affected.

THE LEARNER IS SCORED ON THEM, not merely shown them. Chain verified in source:
  1. quiz.html?module=N is linked from every web/learn/NN-*.html page and from web/learn.html
  2. filterByModule -> sampleItems -> pack.items
  3. onSubmit -> gradeByKeys() counts the retired item in score_correct/score_total
  4. WASM gradeDigest() produces a GradeExact digest over an attempt containing it
  5. recordGradedWrongs() persists a miss into cdcp.drill.missed.v1 + SRS schedule (1d/3d)
  6. recordQuizResult() feeds cdcp.mastery.v1 practiced/mastered state

So a retired item is shown, scored, spaced-repetition-scheduled, and mastery-weighted. Retirement is not cosmetic: an item is retired because a BETTER COPY OF THE SAME PROPOSITION exists (cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED carries the per-id argument). Serving the retired copy drills the copy that lost.

WHY THE PACK CANNOT BE FIXED INSTEAD (already decided, do not re-litigate): the manifest must ship all 804. cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds the pack bytes to Bank::from_json_str which RECOMPUTES bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade hard-fails on mismatch. Measured: 804-file bank hashes 3404d854... , 779 approved-only pool hashes b81a0019... (pre-v2-bump values). An approved-only pack breaks EVERY client-side grade. Decision recorded in registries/goldens-couplings.toml web.bank-items-pack row and web/data/README.md.

FIX (one line, in the consumer):
  export function filterByModule(bank, moduleNum) {
    const arr = Array.isArray(bank) ? bank : bank && bank.items ? bank.items : [];
    return arr.filter(function (it) {
      return it && typeof it.module === 'number' && it.module === moduleNum
             && it.status === 'approved';
    });
  }
Also audit web/assets/js/drill.js and results.js: both look up by an id the learner already answered, so they are transitively fixed — but only if nothing else draws.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No module quiz at any module/mode serves a non-approved item. Re-run the deterministic sweep above and assert 0.
- Anti-vacuous: a module whose approved pool is empty must ERROR/adapt visibly, never render a 0-item quiz silently.
- A test pins it: known-bad = mark one drawn item retired in a fixture pack, assert the quiz pool excludes it.
- scripts/smoke_*.mjs or an e2e asserts no retired id can enter a graded attempt.

NOT MINE: web/assets/js is owned by another agent this wave. Filed with full evidence rather than edited.

comments.text: VERDICT: satisfied. filterByModule+isApproved in b5394d2. smoke_quiz_approved EXIT 0: 30 quizzes, 255 slots, 0 non-approved.

title: ESCALATION (Josh): nine unlicensed captures are gone from HEAD but remain in PUBLIC git history — accept HEAD-only, or authorise a rewrite?
description:
WHAT: A decision only Josh can make. bd-corpus-public-captures-not-licensed-class-kej removed nine body captures that the manifest itself recorded rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed" from knowledge/corpus/public/. HEAD is now clean and gated. The bytes are still reachable in the git history of a PUBLIC repository (github.com/JYeswak/cdcp-self-study), and in every clone, fork and cache made while they were there.

THE THREE OPTIONS, and why two are already leaning:
(a) ACCEPT HEAD-ONLY — the current state, and what the parent bead recorded as a NON-GOAL. Its reasoning: docs/flywheel/PREPUBLISH-SCRUB-2026-08-14.md applies a fortiori, because these are captures of PUBLIC WEB PAGES rather than standards-body text, no publisher AI policy aggravates them, and the repo was already public. That reasoning is sound as far as it goes.
(b) REWRITE HISTORY for the nine paths. Irreversible and external: it means a force-push to a public remote, breaking every existing clone and every open PR, and it does not reach forks or caches. ESCALATION-ONLY under the autonomy grant, and not something an agent may decide is warranted.
(c) NEITHER, and record why — e.g. a note in the repo stating the removal and its date, so a reader of the history knows the current posture without a rewrite.

WHY IT IS BEADED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the non-goal was recorded by a controller, not decided by Josh. A non-goal in a bead body and a decision are different objects, and the difference matters precisely because this one is about exposure on a public remote. Without a bead the next agent to sweep the corpus re-derives the same analysis and re-escalates, which is the re-litigation the autonomy grant "record every fork you resolve" clause exists to prevent.

NOTHING IS BLOCKED ON THIS. HEAD is clean, the corpus-redistribution gate is green and fails closed, and the anti-hallucination corpus measures 573,880 characters against a floor of 20,000 without any of the removed material. The parent bead is complete either way.

ACCEPTANCE (Josh, not an agent):
- A recorded decision: (a), (b) or (c), with its reason, so the analysis is not re-derived.
- If (b) is authorised, Josh runs it or explicitly authorises the exact command; an agent never force-pushes and never rewrites history on its own.
- If (a) stands, record it as a DECISION with its reason and close this bead. Standing still is a legitimate answer; an unrecorded standing still is not.

NON-ESCALATION FOLLOW-UP, noted here so it is not lost and does NOT need Josh: src-ocp-ready was removed with the other eight rather than re-licensed. OCP publishes individual specifications under named open licences (OCPHL, CC-BY) and this row may well be re-openable — but the artefact retained was a capture of a GitHub PROJECT PAGE, not of a licensed specification document, and no licence text granting redistribution of that page was located. Re-adding it is now a mechanical licence-evidence job under the new CORPUS-R7: record redistribution_evidence {licence, url, clause} naming the licence that covers the specific document, and the body may legitimately return. That is ordinary corpus work for an agent, not a decision.

title: units_index.json bakes RETIRED items into learn-page unit checks (build_units never reads status)
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/build_units.rs::load_bank reads web/data/bank_items_seed42.json and builds Item rows from id/module/topic_ids/stem/explanation/choices. It NEVER reads `status`. Same for the Python twin scripts/build_units.py. So retired items are eligible to become a unit's `check_item_ids`, and the result is COMMITTED into web/data/units_index.json.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 against the committed artifacts (134 units, 402 total check_item_ids):
  05-lighting__formulas-rules-of-thumb  -> check includes m05-q200 (retired)
  11-network__formulas-rules-of-thumb   -> check includes m11-q226 (retired)

These are served inline on the learn pages: web/assets/js/learn_units.js pickItems() branch 1 resolves unit.check_item_ids against the bank map and renders them as the unit's check questions. So a learner reading web/learn/05-lighting.html or 11-network.html is asked a withdrawn question.

This is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT exposure from bd-7big (module quiz). Fixing quiz.js does NOT fix this one — the retired ids are already frozen into units_index.json and would be re-emitted by the next build_units run.

WHY THE PACK IS NOT THE FIX: web/data/bank_items_seed42.json must ship all 804 items or client-side grading breaks (Bank::from_json_str recomputes bank_hash; cdcp_grade::grade hard-fails on mismatch). Decision recorded in registries/goldens-couplings.toml web.bank-items-pack and web/data/README.md. Consumers filter; the manifest does not.

FIX:
- build_units.rs load_bank: parse `status` into Item and exclude non-approved from check-item candidate selection. Keep the Python twin byte-identical (it is a differential oracle).
- Regenerate web/data/units_index.json; the two units above lose their retired check and must backfill from the approved pool.
- Anti-vacuous: a unit left with 0 check items after filtering is an ERROR or an explicit empty-ok, never a silent drop. Note build_units already reports units_with_checks>=2 / zero — that counter must not silently absorb this.

ACCEPTANCE:
- 0 retired ids among units_index.json check_item_ids, asserted by a test that parses the artifact.
- Known-bad: mark an item retired that is a current check_item_id, re-run build_units, gate goes RED (or the item is replaced) rather than silently re-emitting it.
- Rust and Python twins stay byte-identical (differential oracle preserved).

NOT MINE: crates/cdcp_gate and scripts/build_units.py are outside this wave's ownership. Filed with evidence.
