title: export_anki.py seed42 mode exports retired items into study decks
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py load_seed42_bank_items() reads web/data/bank_items_seed42.json and, in `--source seed42` mode, turns every element into an Anki card. The manifest ships all 804 files including 25 status="retired", and export_anki.py never reads `status`.

Consequence: a generated Anki deck contains 25 withdrawn duplicate items sitting beside the survivors that replaced them — the exact adjacency the retirement removed. `--source bank` (load_bank_items over bank/items) has the same gap.

Lower priority than bd-7big and the units_index bead because this is an opt-in export a learner runs deliberately, not a surface the product serves on its own. It is the same root cause: the manifest is the whole bank by design (see registries/goldens-couplings.toml web.bank-items-pack — filtering it breaks client-side grading), so every consumer that DRAWS must filter on status.

FIX: filter `it.get('status') == 'approved'` in both loaders; anti-vacuous — a deck of 0 cards is an ERROR, and so is a filter that drops everything.

ACCEPTANCE: no retired id in any generated deck; a test asserts the count equals the approved pool (779), not the file count (804).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the live tree while porting to Rust (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13). The number, not the estimate:

  bank/items/*.toml           804 files
  status = "approved"          779
  status = "retired"            25

  python3 scripts/export_anki.py   (the DEFAULT invocation — the one check.sh:779 runs)
    stdout                    cards=804
    dist/anki/cdcp_bank.tsv   806 lines = 2 operator comment lines + 804 card rows
    dist/anki/cdcp_bank.apkg  804 notes

Cross-checked by GUID rather than by count, because a count alone cannot say WHICH items shipped:
_guid_for(id) = sha1('cdcp-anki:'+id)[:10] was computed for all 779 approved and all 25 retired ids
and intersected with the guid column of the packaged collection.anki2:

    RETIRED items present in the shipped deck:  25 of 25
    approved present:                          779 of 779

Independently confirmed a second way, with the Rust port's built binary, by subtraction — build the
deck from the whole bank, then from the bank with the 25 retired TOMLs removed:
    cards=804  ->  cards=779,  TSV line delta exactly 25.

THE TITLE UNDERSTATES THE SCOPE. This is not limited to '--source seed42'. --source bank — the
DEFAULT, and the only mode check.sh exercises — has it too: load_bank_items() takes every
bank/items/*.toml carrying an 'id' and never reads 'status'. Retired ids in the shipped deck include
m05-q200, m09-q221, m09-q226, m11-q226, m12-q217.

THIRD CONFIRMED INSTANCE of the class, and the first in a DOWNLOADABLE artifact rather than a web
surface: bd-7big (module quiz SCORED learners on retired items), bd-qqwc (units_index baked retired
ids into learn-page checks), this. The original framing — 'an opt-in export a learner runs
deliberately, not a surface the product serves on its own' — is right about intent and wrong about
consequence: unlike a page view, the deck OUTLIVES the session. It syncs to the learner's phone and
enters their spaced-repetition schedule permanently, so a withdrawn question keeps being reviewed
long after the retirement that removed it. Raising priority from P3 to P2 on that basis.

REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED, in the port. crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs ships the retired
items exactly as the oracle does, and crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_export_anki.rs::
the_shipped_deck_contains_every_retired_item_and_that_is_reproduced_not_fixed PINS the number with
the subtractive measurement and says in its failure message that the ORACLE must be fixed first. A
port stricter than its oracle would make every differential case disagree and blind the whole
harness — the same discipline bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.12 used for its three defects.

MEASUREMENT NOTE worth keeping: the first version of that test located retired items by pulling each
one's 'stem' out of its TOML and grepping the TSV. It reported 6 of 25 — a TOML stem can be a
multi-line string, can carry escapes, and is stripped and tab/newline-flattened on its way into the
deck. It would have UNDER-reported the defect by 76% while looking like it had measured it. If you
verify the fix, verify it by subtraction.

title: The module-bound sweep still cannot see a bound that is COMPUTED or read from config
description:
WHAT: bd-8mjs closed the named-constant hole in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs — Shape::NamedBound now sees 'MIN_TERMS = 15', 'pub const MAX: usize = 14;', 'MAX=14'. Three shapes remain outside every detector in that file, and they are named at the pinned open count so the number does not read broader than it is:

1. A bound COMPUTED rather than written. 'MAX_MODULE = len(declared) - 1', 'range(1, MAX)', 'n - 1' where n came from somewhere. No literal, no binding to a bare integer, invisible to all three detectors.
2. A bound read from a config file or an environment variable. 'MAX = cfg["max_module"]' or os.environ. The literal moves out of the scanned trees entirely.
3. A name bound to something other than a bare integer that still carries the bound: a tuple, a list, a dict value, a chained expression.

WHY IT MATTERS, and why this is P3 and not P1: the bd-8mjs evasion needed no intent — rebasing a literal onto a named constant is ordinary refactoring hygiene, which is what made it dangerous. These three are different: none of them is something a refactor does by accident to a module bound. They are reachable, but only deliberately. The cost of chasing them is an over-strict detector, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which is a slower death than no gate. The named-bound detector was worth building because it found three real lines (two of them in a Rust port nobody had in mind) at zero false positives; a computed-bound detector cannot make that trade without a data-flow pass.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever is argued at the time):
- Either a fourth detector with real known-GOOD legs over the legitimate computed expressions already in the tree, and every new hit inventoried with a verdict,
- or a recorded decision that the residual stays uncovered, with the reason, so the next agent does not re-derive this from scratch. The residual is ALREADY stated at the count and in the module header; this bead exists so the statement has a tracking id rather than only prose.

title: README's per-suite injection column is hand-maintained and unenforced
description:
WHAT: the 'Gates proven to trip' table in README.md carries a per-suite n column (| selftest_orphan | 6 | ... |). verify-injection-count enforces the TOTAL at 5 advertisement sites and the SUITE COUNT, but its _ADVERTISED regex requires the number to be followed by 'injections|faults', so '| 26 |' in a table cell matches nothing. Every per-suite number is folklore.

WHY: this is bd-1sd.13 one column to the right, and it is already wrong-prone: closing bd-1sd.13 moved selftest_injection_count from 12 to 26 and the table cell had to be edited BY HAND, exactly the operation whose failure that bead documents. A reader sums the column to sanity-check the total; nothing makes the column agree with the receipts.

ACCEPTANCE:
- the per-suite receipts (INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>) are compared against the per-suite cells, not only against the total
- a cell that disagrees is RED naming file:line, suite, both numbers
- a suite row present in the table but absent from REGISTERED_SUITES, and vice versa, is RED
- anti-vacuous: a table that parses to zero suite rows is an ERROR, not a pass
- --write-readme regenerates the cells from the receipts
- known-bad injection added to scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh in both directions

comments.author: josh
comments.text: MEASURED 2026-08-14 while closing bd-1sd.13: the column is ALREADY wrong, and by more than one. Summing the per-suite cells as committed before this wave gives 4+2+1+2+8+5+6+7+12 = 47. The enforced total in the same section said 49, and check.sh was green — so two numbers in one README section disagreed by 2 and nothing said so, because only one of them is under a gate. (49 is the receipts' number: the orchestrator watched this gate go RED at 47-vs-49 when the suites moved.) After this wave the enforced total is 63 and the cells sum to 61. The column is not merely unguarded; it is measurably stale in the shipped README.

title: verify-injection-count --write-readme is unreachable from check.sh
description:
WHAT: verify_injection_count.py / cdcp_gate verify-injection-count document the advertised number as 'REGENERATED, never hand-maintained' via --write-readme. But the only log that carries every registered suite's receipt is the one check.sh mktemps, and check.sh deletes it in its EXIT trap and never passes --write-readme. So the regeneration path has no reachable caller: in practice the number is retyped by hand and the gate only says whether the typing was right.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 while closing bd-1sd.13: moving selftest_injection_count from 12 to 26 injections required typing 63 into five README sites by hand, because there was no way to reach the regenerator with a real log.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'regenerated, never typed' is a claim in the shipped module header and in README prose. A claim whose mechanism has no caller is the BUILT != WIRED failure inside a doc-truth gate.

FIX (mirrors what bd-1sd.13 shipped for the step count): honour an env flag in check.sh — CDCP_INJECTION_COUNT_WRITE_README=1 adds --write-readme to the verify-injection-count invocation, so a drifted total is repaired by re-running the chain rather than by retyping five sites. Keep the refusal-on-unsound-receipts leg.

ACCEPTANCE: adding an injection and re-running check.sh with the flag rewrites all five sites from the receipts; without the flag it is still RED; a known-bad proves the flag cannot launder an unsound total.

title: Widen the ABSENT-OK path-guard scan from two files to the cdcp_gate tree
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/anti_vacuous_topics.rs::unreasoned_path_guards_are_a_defect scans exactly two files — crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs and scripts/verify_objectives.py — for block-opening existence tests (is_file/exists/is_dir) that neither record an error inside the if/else chain they open nor carry an 'ABSENT-OK:' reason in that chain or the twelve lines above it. Widening it is ONE LINE: the targets array.

WHY IT WAS NOT WIDENED IN THE bd-9nyt WAVE (argued, not skipped):
1. Five sibling agents were editing crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/ concurrently. A gate that goes red on a file its owner cannot touch gets disabled, and a disabled detector is worth LESS than none, because it also carries the belief that the class is covered.
2. 'ABSENT-OK:' is a convention this test invented. Imposing it tree-wide unilaterally means every other gate author adopts one agent's comment syntax or is flagged for it. It should survive one wave in one place first.

MEASURED SCOPE OF THE WIDENING: 72 is_file()/exists()/is_dir() occurrences across crates/cdcp_gate/src/ as of acd4d43, concentrated in verify_content_lock.rs (12), verify_objectives.rs (9), validate_grounding.rs (9), build_units.rs (6), verify_coverage.rs (5), verify_bank.rs (5). Not all are block guards; the scanner only counts lines whose trimmed form opens an if/elif/else-if.

ACCEPTANCE:
- targets extended to crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs and the .py oracles still on the path.
- Every newly-flagged site either gains an error path or an ABSENT-OK: sentence, ONE OWNER AT A TIME. A blanket sweep that adds the marker everywhere converts the detector into decoration; the existing assertion 'reasoned * 2 < total' is the guard against that and must be re-tuned per-file rather than dropped.
- The planted known-bad legs in that test (bare guard FLAGGED, ABSENT-OK guard NOT flagged, else-with-error NOT flagged) must survive the widening unchanged.
- Known-GOOD: the live tree still passes check.sh.

WHAT IT CANNOT DECIDE (carry this forward): the scanner does not read what the guarded block DOES, so it cannot tell a skipped verdict from a skipped log line; it does not follow ? or a helper that raises elsewhere; and it cannot tell a true ABSENT-OK: from a lazy one.

title: verify-objectives --write-json can leave a summary saying status=pass under a FAIL verdict
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_objectives.py:~735 and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs:~1690 compute the summary's status BEFORE writing it:

    provisional = 'PASS' if not errors else 'FAIL'
    out.write_text(json.dumps(summary_for(provisional) ...))
  except OSError as e:
    errors.append(f'could not write summary to {out}: {e}')

So the ONE path that can turn a PASS into a FAIL after the status word is chosen is the write itself. If create_dir_all succeeds and the write then fails partway (target on a full or read-only filesystem, truncated then failed), the artifact left on disk carries "status": "pass" while the gate exits 1. A machine-readable receipt disagreeing with the verdict is the receipt an operator trusts.

FOUND: during the bd-9nyt sweep of verify_objectives. NOT fixed there because closing it means either writing to a temp file and renaming (behaviour change on both sides, and the differential compares the written bytes AND the stdout in tests/diff_verify_objectives.rs::the_written_summary_is_byte_identical), or emitting the status last — both larger than the bead in hand.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SHOULD STAY RECORDED RATHER THAN INFLATED: on a successful write provisional == final, because nothing else appends to errors after that point. Nothing in scripts/check.sh passes --write-json for this gate, and nothing in the repo consumes the file (grepped: no consumer outside the gate and its differential).

ACCEPTANCE:
- The written summary's status equals the printed verdict on every path, or the file is not left behind at all when the write fails.
- Python first, then the Rust port, then the byte-differential goes green again.
- Known-bad: point --write-json at a target whose write fails after the parent exists; assert no file on disk says pass while the process exits non-zero.

title: verify_coverage reads the same bank_policy.toml where ABSENCE LOWERS the floors
description:
WHAT: bd-9nyt reasoned verify_objectives' two missing-bank_policy.toml early returns as legitimately optional and marked them ABSENT-OK. The argument is sound FOR THAT GATE and only for that gate:

  verify_objectives applies its OWN floor of >=1 item per required module and reads the policy only for [[coverage_exempt]] rows and [[domain_min]] drift. An absent ledger therefore removes exemptions, leaves every declared module required, and makes the gate STRICTER. Nothing can hide in the absence.

verify_coverage.py / crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs read the SAME file for the SIZED [[domain_min]] floors. There, absence removes the floors — the opposite direction. Whether that path is guarded was NOT checked by bd-9nyt (verify_coverage.rs was owned by a sibling agent mid-wave and out of scope).

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the ABSENT-OK sentence now sitting in verify_objectives explicitly warns that absence being safe is a property of what a gate does with the rows, not of the file. The next reader who copies that comment into verify_coverage would be copying a false statement. This bead exists so that copy is caught.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Determine what verify_coverage does when bank_policy.toml is absent: does it fall back to a compiled-in floor, report an error, or silently apply no floor?
- If it silently applies no floor, that is the absent-input-reads-as-success class and it becomes an error path naming the file.
- If it legitimately falls back, it gets a written reason at the site, NOT the verify_objectives sentence copied verbatim.
- Known-bad per branch, with the real exit code from the built binary.

title: verify-bank enforces pool_min against the file set, not the approved pool — same class as bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh
description:
WHAT: `verify-bank` (scripts/verify_bank.py + crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs) counts every loaded item, whatever its status, in THREE places that all key on the drawable pool:

  scripts/verify_bank.py:169   `if pool_min is not None and exam_n is not None and n < pool_min` — the ENFORCED floor
  scripts/verify_bank.py:300   `correct_dist={...}` — answer-letter diversity
  scripts/verify_bank.py:301   `modules={...}` — per-module counts

MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the live tree, after bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh landed in verify-coverage:

    verify-bank:      items=804  pool_min=400 exam_n=40 multiplier~20.1x
                      modules={... 14: 44 ...}
                      correct_dist={A:198 B:228 C:190 D:188}
    drawable truth:   779 approved (25 retired), m14: 42, multiplier~19.5x

NO LIVE BREACH: 779 >= 400 either way, and the letter distribution over the approved pool is not obviously skewed. This is a defect, not an incident — but it is the SAME fail-open direction verify-coverage just had fixed: the file count can only ever be >= the number that matters, so `pool_min` can only ever be too generous, and `multiplier~20.1x` is a claim about a pool `cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids` will never draw from.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY: bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh asked its owner to DECIDE the question for verify-bank. The decision is that it is the same defect and must move the same way — but verify_bank.py and verify_bank.rs were owned by a different agent during the same wave, and reaching across would have meant two agents editing one differential. Recorded rather than done.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `pool_min` is enforced against `status == "approved"`. The report names BOTH numbers (items scanned, approved counted) wherever it prints a count, as verify-coverage now does, so the two populations can never be confused.
- `modules={...}` and `correct_dist={...}` either count the approved pool, or say IN THE OUTPUT which population they show. Correct-letter diversity measured over a pool that includes retired items is measuring the wrong pool for the same reason the floor was.
- Anti-vacuous: zero approved is an ERROR naming the condition, distinct from the empty-bank leg.
- Known-bad: retire items in a TEMP COPY of the bank until the approved pool is under `pool_min` WITHOUT deleting a file -> RED. That fixture leaves the file count untouched, so the current gate stays GREEN on it by construction, which is the proof the population changed.
- Python and Rust move together, PYTHON FIRST, and the verify_bank differential is watched go RED before the port follows.

PRIOR ART TO COPY, NOT RE-DERIVE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs cases (j)(k)(l) — `module_lines`/`retire_in_place` do exactly this injection and are ~90 lines.
notes:
VERIFICATION-GAP NARROWED (third attempt, shared target dir, scratchpad/U2.txt + D2.txt).

Both runs exit 101, and AGAIN not because of anything in this bead's files. Every error location, attributed:
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/build_units.rs:1973        (bd-qqwc, sibling mid-edit)
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_a11y.rs:876,881      (sibling)
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs:471,1371 (sibling)
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_learn.rs:387         (sibling)
ZERO errors in verify_bank.rs or diff_verify_bank.rs. The --lib run compiled the cfg(test) code path (that is where build_units.rs:1973 lives), so the SEVEN NEW UNIT TESTS in verify_bank.rs's mod tests DO TYPE-CHECK — rustc reported all 9 errors in the crate and attributed none to them. They still have not RUN: the crate cannot link while the siblings' files are red.

The 44th differential case is no longer an assumption. Its assertions were executed DIRECTLY against both implementations on a fixture carrying 'items = [1, 2]':
  PY_EXIT=1, RS_EXIT=1
  stdout 0 bytes on both, byte-identical
  python stderr: AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
  rust   stderr: verify-bank: AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
That is exactly what a_non_mapping_item_raises_identically_from_the_approved_pool_pre_pass asserts, so the moved raise point is measured, not assumed.

RESIDUAL, and it is now small: neither suite has been executed end-to-end through cargo since the sibling files went red. Re-run both once the crate is green — the bar is unchanged, exit code read directly, and not a build-script SIGKILL.

title: the verdict-shape class needs a META-GATE over the differential harnesses, not a fourth patch — measured 3 of 11 carry the leg
description:
CONTEXT: bd-lt7 fixed instance 1 (build_units.py). bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 fixed instance 2 (build_glossary_json.py + port). bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n fixed instance 3 (verify_coverage.py + port), and its owner was asked to decide whether a mechanism can forbid the shape GENERALLY. This is that decision, recorded so it is not re-derived, plus the one tractable mechanism and why it did not land in the same wave.

THE TWO OBVIOUS FORMS, AND WHY BOTH ARE REJECTED:

1. A STATIC SCAN ("grep for a success token printed on a path reachable by a non-zero exit") is NOT tractable, and the sound approximation is worse than no gate. Sound analysis needs interprocedural reachability across Python AND Rust. The cheap approximation — flag any file containing a success token that can also exit non-zero — fires on every CORRECT gate in the tree: verify_coverage.py buffers "PASS" and returns 1 from the same function, and that is right, because the token is only in the buffer when `errors` is empty. A scan cannot see that without evaluating the condition. And this repo has already measured the failure mode of message-keyed scanning: see the bd-0czh comment in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs — three fail-opens survived an audit because grepping each file for the message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. A scan that can be fooled by the same string that fooled the auditor is a GREEN gate certifying a wrong claim.

2. A SHARED REPORT-COMPOSITION HELPER (a Report type whose verdict is structurally last) is sound but OPT-IN. It prevents the shape only in the files that adopt it, does not cross the Python/Rust boundary, and an author who does not reach for it is not caught. It is a convention, not an enforcement — and this repo does not count conventions.

THE FORM THAT IS TRACTABLE: a META-GATE over the differential harnesses. Each harness already runs both implementations on every case and already knows its gate exit code. The detector is one leg — on any case where a side exited non-zero, assert its stdout carries no success token, asserted PER SIDE. That leg is PROVEN, twice, by mutation pairs: qm65 proved it in the two builder harnesses; rk9n proved it again in diff_verify_coverage.rs on 2026-08-14 (mutate both implementations to print the token regardless of the verdict -> suite exit 101 on 12 cases; delete that ONE assertion with the mutation still in place -> exit 0). The meta-gate asserts every harness CARRIES that leg, so a new gate cannot ship without it.

WHY IT DID NOT LAND WITH rk9n — MEASURED 2026-08-14, `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs`:

    CARRIES a per-side non-zero + success-token leg (3):
      diff_build_units.rs, diff_build_glossary_json.rs, diff_verify_coverage.rs
    DOES NOT (8):
      diff_validate_grounding.rs, diff_verify_bank.rs, diff_verify_content_lock.rs,
      diff_verify_doc_consistency.rs, diff_verify_injection_count.rs,
      diff_verify_knowledge_paths.rs, diff_verify_objectives.rs, diff_verify_orphans.rs

Landing the meta-gate in that wave would have turned EIGHT sibling-owned test files RED mid-swarm, for a defect none of them has been shown to have. That is a gate tripping on other peoples work in flight, not a gate proving a claim. Converted to this bead instead of skipped.

ONE MORE THING THE IMPLEMENTER MUST SOLVE, recorded because it is the real difficulty: the success token DIFFERS per gate (PASS, ok, GREEN, `PASS: glossary terms=`). A leg keyed on the literal "PASS" is message-keyed and is exactly the shape rejected in (1). The token belongs in a per-gate registry row the harness reads, not in a grep.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs` carries the per-side leg, keyed on a REGISTERED success token for its gate rather than on a literal.
- A meta-test enumerates the harnesses and fails when one lacks the leg. An empty enumeration is an ERROR, not a pass. An exclusion requires a reason string; an exclusion without a reason is a schema error.
- The meta-test is itself proven by a mutation pair: delete the leg from one harness -> the meta-test names that harness and is RED.
- The census that found instances 1-3 is re-run and reports ZERO remaining, so the class CLOSES rather than being decremented.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION: the meta-gate was built, and it does NOT take the shape this bead proposed. Recorded with the argument so it is not re-litigated.

WHAT THIS BEAD PROPOSED: a meta-test that asserts every crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs CARRIES a per-side leg ("on any case where a side exited non-zero, assert its stdout carries no success token"), keyed on a registered token, with the census re-run to zero.

WHAT WAS BUILT INSTEAD: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, which moves the leg OFF the harnesses and ONTO the gate binary. For every gate cdcp_gate list names, on an empty root and (where safe) on the live root, it asserts that exit == 0 is EQUIVALENT to "stdout opens a line with this gate is registered success token".

THREE REASONS, in order of weight.

1. THE LEG IS PER-CASE AND UNBOUNDED; THE DEFECT IS PER-GATE AND THERE ARE NINETEEN GATES. A per-harness leg protects only the cases that harness happens to run, and only for as long as that harness exists. The gate probe covers every case of every gate at once, including gates that never had a differential harness (capability-maturity, doc-facts, goldens-couplings, corpus-redistribution, near-duplicate-items, substrate-guard, verify-step-count, install-hooks — eight gates this bead is silent about).

2. IT NEEDED EIGHT SIBLING-OWNED FILES EDITED IN ONE WAVE, which this bead already identified as the reason it did not land with rk9n. That has not improved: four of the eleven harnesses were owned by other agents during the 2026-08-14 wave. The gate probe needs no edit to any file another agent owns.

3. THE ORACLES ARE NOW RETIRED. check.sh invokes none of the eleven .py scripts, and the standing policy is to retire an oracle at port time and convert its differential cases into direct tests. A leg installed in eleven harnesses that are being deleted is work with a known expiry. The gate probe outlives every harness in the tree.

WHAT IS PRESERVED FROM THIS BEAD, deliberately: the success token is a REGISTERED PER-GATE ROW in registries/differential_harnesses.toml, never a literal in a scanner — this bead is right that a leg keyed on "PASS" is the message-keyed shape rejected in its own section (1), and bd-0czh already measured three fail-opens surviving an audit because grepping for the message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. The tokens differ exactly as predicted: PASS, "PASS: build_units", "PASS: glossary", "verify_content_lock: PASS", "<gate>: ok:".

MEASURED WHILE BUILDING IT, and filed: near-duplicate-items prints NO success token on either path, so nothing but its exit code distinguishes green from red (bd-near-dup-no-success-token-gj9y). It is registered token_free WITH A REASON and the meta-gate PROVES the absence — neither probe may open a line with any word from the token vocabulary — rather than taking the exclusion on trust. An exclusion without a reason string is a schema error, as this bead required.

TOKEN MATCHING IS LINE-PREFIX, NOT SUBSTRING, and there is a known-GOOD leg for it: a gate that says "expected PASS, got FAIL" under exit 1 has not claimed to pass, and a message-keyed check would fire there. The detector is proven on planted synthetics in both directions (the_verdict_shape_detector_trips_on_a_planted_known_bad).

ANTI-VACUOUS: the gate roster comes from the BINARY, not the registry, so a new gate cannot ship unregistered; an empty roster is an ERROR; every gate must FAIL over an empty root; and at least one gate must be observed GREEN carrying its token, or the token side of the equivalence never ran and "no token on a failing path" passed for free.

STILL OPEN FROM THIS BEAD ACCEPTANCE: the per-harness leg is NOT installed in the eight harnesses that lacked it, and deliberately so. If the class is later judged to need both, that is a new bead, and it should be weighed against the retirement schedule for those files.

title: A restored perturbation can leave cargo testing the STALE binary — measured false RED, and by symmetry false GREEN
description:
WHAT: the standard perturb-then-restore pattern used by every meta-test in this repo can silently defeat the rebuild, so the test exercises a binary that does not match the source on disk.

MECHANISM: `cp file file.bak` then later `mv file.bak file` restores the CONTENT but gives the file the BACKUP OBJECT.S mtime, which is older than the perturbed version cargo already compiled. cargo compares mtimes, sees nothing newer, and skips the rebuild. The next invocation runs the binary built from the PERTURBED source.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-6ycw / bd-web-pack agent, recorded in goldens/PROVENANCE.md with the mtimes): its verification reported RED for a tree that was GREEN. The agent caught it, forced a rebuild, and both bank_hash and the wasm reproduced byte-identically.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A CURIOSITY: the observed direction was a false RED, which is loud and self-correcting. THE SAME MECHANISM PRODUCES A FALSE GREEN — restore a file, skip the rebuild, and the suite passes against the binary that still contains the mutation. Every meta-test PAIR in this repo depends on exactly this restore step, and a meta-test that cannot fail is a fooled certificate, which is Sev-0 by this project standard. We have run dozens of these pairs this week.

THE PAIRS AT RISK are every one following the house pattern: (1) mutate the gate, assert the suite goes non-zero; (2) with the mutation still in place, delete the assertion, assert it returns to zero; (3) restore. Step 3 is the one that rots, and a bad step 3 makes the NEXT pair meaningless rather than this one.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A documented restore that cannot lose the rebuild — `touch` the restored file, or restore by rewriting content rather than moving the inode, or force `cargo build` before the post-restore assertion. Pick one, state why, and put it where meta-test authors will read it (the pattern is described in several test headers and in CHARTER meta-test guidance).
- A known-bad that DEMONSTRATES the trap: restore naively, assert the suite reports the wrong verdict; restore correctly, assert it reports the right one. If the trap cannot be reproduced on demand, the fix cannot be verified.
- AUDIT: how many meta-test pairs run in this repo, and how many use a restore that is vulnerable? Report the count. A sample of previously-passed pairs should be re-run under a forced rebuild to confirm their verdicts still hold — if any flips, that is a separate finding and every conclusion drawn from it is suspect.
- Anti-vacuous: a rebuild step that finds nothing to rebuild when a file demonstrably changed is an ERROR, not a pass.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
WAVE RESULT 2026-08-14. Half 1 complete and measured. Half 2 audited but its re-run is BLOCKED, not passed.

THE TRAP IS REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, BOTH DIRECTIONS. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/restore_rebuild_trap.rs, 4 tests, all green in 6.34 s, built from a throwaway two-file cargo crate in a tempdir so it never touches this repo and can run beside any sibling suite.
  a_naive_restore_of_the_assertion_reports_a_false_green  - the Sev-0 direction: run the house pair to completion with a mv-shaped step 3 and the suite certifies exit 0 for a tree whose only honest verdict is RED.
  a_safe_restore_of_the_assertion_reports_the_true_red    - same tree, byte-rewrite restore plus a PROVEN rebuild, verdict 101.
  a_forced_build_after_a_naive_restore_is_itself_vacuous  - the anti-vacuous leg aimed at the remedy.
  touch_recovers_a_tree_that_was_already_restored_by_rename - the false-RED direction measured 2026-08-14, and touch pinned as the RECOVERY move.
Every case first asserts its own fixture discriminates (clean crate GREEN, perturbed crate RED) - a fixture that can only report one thing proves nothing.

THE PATTERN, ARGUED. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/rebuild.rs. Measured head-to-head:
  mv then cargo build  -> nothing rebuilt, fresh:true, Finished in 0.00s -> WRONG verdict
  cp then cargo build  -> fresh:false -> right verdict
  mv + touch then build-> fresh:false -> right verdict
PICK: byte-rewrite for the mechanism (it IS the restore, so there is no second step to forget) PLUS a forced build with a freshness assertion for the proof. Neither half alone is enough, and the argument turns on this: A FORCED cargo build ON ITS OWN IS VACUOUS - after a rename-restore it exits 0 and rebuilds nothing, i.e. the obvious fix passes in exactly the case it was written to catch. touch is demoted to the recovery move: it works, but it is a separate step whose omission is silent.
ALSO PINNED AS A TRAP FOR THE NEXT AGENT: do NOT prove freshness with artifact_mtime > source_mtime. The poisoned tree SATISFIES it. Compare the artifact's mtime before the build with its mtime after.

WHERE IT IS WRITTEN: .flywheel/CHARTER.md gauntlet section as step (3) of the pair; docs/TESTING.md new section 'Meta-test pairs: step 3 is the one that rots'; docs/PLAN-A-TO-Z.md line 54, which still carried the retired 'delete the assertion -> selftest RED' wording the CHARTER corrected on 2026-08-14 - fixed in place; crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/mod.rs header pointer.

MY OWN META-TEST PAIR, run under the pattern it certifies. TRUE exit codes, read off the child, never through a pipe:
  leg 1 - mutate the anti-vacuous branch of build_proving_rebuild to always report 'rebuilt' -> cargo test exit 101, EXACTLY ONE test red (a_forced_build_after_a_naive_restore_is_itself_vacuous). Single detector confirmed.
  leg 2 - mutation still live, delete that test's expect_err assertion -> exit 0. That assertion, and nothing else, is what bit.
  step 3 - both files restored by byte rewrite, then rebuild PROVEN: artifact mtime 1786753436.84 -> 1786753475.16. Suite green.
Cargo's rebuild-changes-artifact-mtime assumption was verified independently rather than assumed: touch source -> Compiling cdcp_gate -> mtime 1786753301.07 -> 1786753411.88.

AUDIT COUNTS: 19 recorded pairs; 13 exposed (mutated a cargo-compiled file); 6 not exposed (4 shell selftests, 2 Python-era); 0 of the 13 recorded a rebuild-safe restore. Ratio 13/19 = 68 percent exposed, 13/13 = 100 percent of those unproven. Floor derivation for the anti-vacuous clause: 5 in-source records and 12 closed-bead close_reasons name a meta-test today.

RE-RUN SAMPLE: NOT RUN. Five attempts, 240-600 s each, none reached a Compiling line - bd-syspolicyd-stall-blocks-all-builds-dp91 held the shared target lock for over an hour and a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR hangs identically. Tracked as bd-metatest-rerun-blocked-yhg6 with the 13 prioritised by consequence. No verdict is claimed for any of them.

FILED: bd-metatest-rerun-blocked-yhg6 (P1), bd-single-leg-metatest-closes-illw (P1), bd-stale-artifact-gate-urj0 (P2). Evidence merged into dp91.

title: A differential harness cannot see a defect both implementations share — measured, on a case it had been passing for weeks
description:
WHAT: the byte-exact differential harnesses assert that the Python oracle and the Rust port agree on stdout, stderr, exit code and bytes written. They cannot see a defect PRESENT IN BOTH. Two implementations agreeing on a vacuous pass is still a vacuous pass.

THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL. Measured 2026-08-14 in verify_objectives: `--min-items-per-topic 0` fell straight through the comparison guard and printed

  PASS ... primary_topics=106 covered=106 shortfalls=0 min_per_topic=0 mode=strict ... EXIT 0

106 of 106 topics reported covered, in STRICT mode, with not one comparison performed. The differential harness had been running that exact case (`m min topic 0`) and PASSING it for weeks, because both sides produced the same wrong answer. The harness header already says "a defect faithfully ported is still a defect" — and the defect landed in its own blind spot.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: agreement is a necessary condition for a correct port and is NOT a sufficient condition for a correct gate. Every case in every differential harness that asserts only agreement is silent about whether the shared behaviour is right. We now have roughly eleven of these harnesses and the count is growing with each port.

RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME: bd-j8b2 proposes a meta-gate over the harnesses for the VERDICT-SHAPE class specifically (measured 3 of 11 carry the leg). This bead is the general case — verdict shape is one instance of shared-defect blindness, not the whole of it.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision on what each differential case must assert BEYOND agreement. The candidate from the objectives work: assert the VERDICT, not only the agreement — that is, each case states what the correct answer IS, independently, and both sides are checked against it. That is more expensive per case and it is the only thing that can see a shared defect. Argue it against the alternatives.
- An audit: across all differential harnesses, how many cases assert agreement ONLY? Report the count and the ratio. That number is the size of the blind spot and it should be published where a reader meets the harnesses.
- At least the anti-vacuous and floor cases in every harness carry an independent verdict assertion, since those are the ones whose failure mode is silence.
- Known-bad: plant a defect in BOTH implementations identically, assert the harness now catches it. Under the current design it does not — that is the demonstration.
- Anti-vacuous: a harness whose case list is empty, or which compares an artifact neither side wrote, is an ERROR.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION, recorded so it is not re-derived (bd-4qje acceptance leg 1).

WHAT EACH CASE MUST ASSERT BEYOND AGREEMENT — and the answer is not the same for every case, which is why the earlier framing kept stalling.

(1) EVERY case states the correct answer independently and BOTH sides are checked against it. Rejected as a blanket rule — not because it is wrong, but because it prices in something now known to be temporary. Measured 2026-08-14: check.sh invokes NONE of the eleven .py oracles; all eleven are retired oracles. Under the retirement policy the second side goes away, so "both sides are checked against it" collapses to "the case asserts the verdict" — candidate (2). Paying the per-case cost twice, once against an oracle about to be deleted, buys nothing.

(2) EVERY case asserts an independent verdict; the byte-comparison stays only while the oracle does. ADOPTED. Agreement is NECESSARY for a correct port and NOT SUFFICIENT for a correct gate, and the independent verdict is the only half that survives retirement. The audit prices it: 36 of 326 cases assert nothing but agreement, so 36 cases (11.0 percent) evaporate to nothing the day their oracle is deleted, and 88 of 326 (27.0 percent) survive holding no claim about output at all.

(3) Independent verdicts only on the anti-vacuous and floor cases. Rejected AS THE CEILING, adopted as the ORDERING. Those cases matter most because their failure mode is silence and they go first. But the measured defect was not in an anti-vacuous case: "m min topic 0" was filed as an OPTION SHAPE. A rule scoped to the cases we already suspect cannot catch the ones we have misfiled — and 23 of the 36 blind cases sit in exactly that misfiled bucket, one test per harness named path_and_option_shapes_are_byte_identical, built to check argument parsing and then quietly given cases that change the gate semantics ("m strict flag", "m skip flag", "m both flags").

(4) A property-based oracle, or a third implementation. Rejected for now, on cost and on the same shared-defect logic: a third implementation written by the same hands against the same reading of the spec is a third vote for the same misunderstanding — it does not close the class, it makes agreement cheaper to obtain. A property oracle is the right long-run answer for the numeric gates and is not this bead.

THE PART THAT IS EASY TO MISS, and why a naive reading of (2) fails: REWRITING THE ASSERTION IS NOT ENOUGH. All 23 option-shape cases run against the LIVE tree, which is green. Asserting "this spelling still passes" on a tree that passes is worth nothing — no defect that suppresses a finding can appear in a run with no finding to suppress. The conversion must change the INPUT too: point the spelling at a tree with a KNOWN planted finding, and assert (a) the spelling normalises to the one resolved path, (b) the run scanned THAT tree — assert the item count, which is what catches a silent fallback to a default — and (c) it still reaches the planted finding and goes RED for it. Done for diff_verify_orphans.rs this wave: 7 blind cases to 0.

PUBLISHED AT: registries/differential_harnesses.toml (census, method, per-harness table, ratchet) and the module header of crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, which is the file a reader of this harness family meets. Remaining work filed as bd-diff-remaining-agreement-only-qgy9, bd-diff-coverage-agreement-only-25ux, bd-diff-injection-i32-comparator-fo1l, bd-diff-exit-code-only-verdicts-t6kv.

title: extract_key_literals scrapes any ".. ".into() as an emitted pack key, so an error string enters a shape pin
description:
WHAT: the goldens-couplings gate derives its `keys` pin for export.pack-shapes by scraping string literals out of the emitting function. It matches `"...".into()` regardless of what the string is FOR, so a literal used in an error message is recorded as an emitted pack key.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-6ycw agent): one of its new error strings entered the export.pack-shapes pin. It worked around it by writing `.to_string()` instead of `.into()` and noted the fact in the row — a correct local fix that leaves the scraper wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE STRING: this pin is load-bearing. It is what makes a changed pack shape RED under every frozen artifact. Two failure directions, and the second is the bad one:
  - FALSE POSITIVE (what happened): a non-key string enters the pin, so the pin over-describes the shape and an unrelated code edit forces a spurious ledger walk. Noisy, self-announcing.
  - FALSE NEGATIVE: a key emitted by any route the scraper does not recognise — a constant, a format!, a helper, a loop over a slice — is ABSENT from the pin. The pin then silently under-describes the shape, and a real pack-shape change passes the coupling ledger green. That is the fooled certificate, and nothing currently tells us whether it is happening.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE BEAD. Working around the false positive by avoiding `.into()` at call sites teaches authors to route around the scraper, which is exactly how the false negative arrives.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide what the pin should be derived FROM. Scraping literals out of a function body is a heuristic over syntax; the emitted key set is a property of the serialised OUTPUT. Deriving the pin by running the emitter and reading the keys off the produced JSON is the obvious alternative and should be argued for or against explicitly.
- Whichever is chosen: a key emitted by a route the deriver cannot see must be an ERROR, never a silent omission. Fail closed.
- Known-bad, both directions: (a) add a non-key literal, assert it does NOT enter the pin; (b) emit a key by a route the current scraper misses (a const, a format!, a helper), assert the pin goes RED rather than quietly shrinking.
- ANTI-VACUOUS AND LOAD-BEARING HERE: a pin that derives to ZERO keys, or fewer keys than the artifact actually has, must be an ERROR. A shrinking pin is the silent failure and it currently looks identical to a correct one.
- Audit the other derived pin kinds (fields, const, region, toml_array_contains) for the same asymmetry and report which fail open.

title: Six allowlist rows claim 'load-bearing check.sh gate, grandfathered pending the Rust port' for gates that are ported and no longer invoked
description:
WHAT: registries/substrate_allowlist.toml carries a `reason` per exempted .py file. Six rows still read some form of "Load-bearing check.sh gate ... Grandfathered pending the byte-exact Rust port" for files that ARE ported and that check.sh does NOT invoke:
  verify_orphans.py · verify_injection_count.py · verify_doc_consistency.py
  verify_knowledge_paths.py · verify_bank.py · verify_content_lock.py

MEASURED 2026-08-14: every one of those has crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/<name>.rs, and `grep -oE "python3 scripts/[a-z_]+\.py" scripts/check.sh` returns only six DIFFERENT files — export_anki, smoke_diagrams, smoke_feedback_links, smoke_learn_chrome, smoke_learn, smoke_weak_links. Those six are the only genuinely load-bearing Python left.

WHY IT IS A P1 AND NOT COSMETIC. The `reason` field is not decoration; it is the justification that keeps the exemption alive, and it is the only thing a reader consults when deciding whether a row may be removed. Six rows currently assert a status that would make removal WRONG ("check.sh hard-fails if it is absent, so it cannot simply be deleted" — verify_orphans) when in fact removal is exactly what is owed. The registry is arguing FOR keeping Python on a project whose Substrate Law wants it gone, using a fact that stopped being true when the port landed.

It also cost real work today: the controller issued a "fix the Python first, then the port" instruction to two agents based on the assumption that these files were still on the path. They are not. The instruction was corrected mid-flight.

THE UNDERLYING SHAPE, and the reason this belongs to milestone B: these reasons were true when written and became false when the code changed underneath, and nothing mechanically ties a row to the thing it describes. That is the doc-truth class B3 built `cdcp_gate doc-facts` for. A registry field is prose with a schema.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the six rows states its true status: ported, not invoked, retained (if at all) as a differential oracle, with the port bead named.
- A ROW THAT CLAIMS "load-bearing" IS MECHANICALLY CHECKED against whether check.sh actually invokes it. Derive the invocation set from scripts/check.sh; do not hand-maintain a second list. A row claiming load-bearing for a file check.sh never calls is RED, and so is the inverse — a file check.sh calls whose row does not say so.
- Known-bad both directions: flip a row to claim load-bearing for a ported gate -> RED naming both sides; add a python3 invocation to check.sh for a file whose row says oracle-only -> RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: zero invocations discovered is an ERROR (check.sh always calls something), and zero allowlist rows is an ERROR.
- Consider whether this is a doc-facts row rather than a new gate — the polarity lives in the registry prose and the probe is "does check.sh invoke this path". If doc-facts can carry it, prefer that over a twelfth bespoke gate.

title: Retire a differential oracle when its gate changes behaviour, instead of maintaining two implementations forever
description:
WHAT: record and enforce the policy the controller got wrong today, and apply it to the eleven retired oracles still in the tree.

THE DEFECT IN THE OLD RULE. The standing instruction was "PYTHON FIRST: fix the .py, watch the differential go RED, then move the port." That rule is correct only while the oracle is proving the port FAITHFUL — during migration, changing the Rust first makes the differential flag the FIX as the divergence. Its job COMPLETES AT PORT TIME. Applied afterwards it means every deliberate behaviour change is implemented twice, forever, and the second implementation is Python on a project whose Substrate Law puts Rust on the load-bearing path. The migration tool becomes a maintenance tax.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: eleven .py files have Rust ports and check.sh invokes NONE of them (verify_coverage, verify_objectives, verify_bank, verify_content_lock, verify_orphans, verify_doc_consistency, verify_injection_count, verify_knowledge_paths, validate_grounding, build_units, build_glossary_json). The only genuinely load-bearing Python is six unported smokes.

AND THE PROTECTION BEING PAID FOR IS BOUNDED, measured separately: a differential CANNOT see a defect both implementations share (bd-differential-shared-blindspot-4qje). verify_objectives reported "covered=106 of 106, mode=strict, EXIT 0" with not one comparison performed, and its harness passed that case for weeks because both sides produced the same wrong answer.

THE POLICY:
  1. A .py with no Rust port that check.sh invokes -> genuinely load-bearing. Do not grow it. Port it (epic bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd).
  2. A .py with a Rust port that check.sh does not invoke -> a retired oracle. NEVER add behaviour to it. A behaviour change is the trigger to RETIRE it.
  3. RETIREMENT IS CONDITIONAL, and this is the part that must not be lost: convert the harness cases into direct tests of the Rust that assert the VERDICT independently — what the correct answer IS — not that two implementations agree. Anti-vacuous and floor cases first; their failure mode is silence. If a case cannot carry across, KEEP the oracle and file the residual. Retiring an oracle and leaving the Rust with a weaker net than it had is a net loss.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The policy is written where agents will meet it, not only in this bead.
- Per-oracle disposition table for all eleven: retire now / retire when touched / keep with reason. Driven by the per-harness agreement-only ratio from bd-differential-shared-blindspot-4qje — a harness whose cases are ALL agreement-only cannot have its oracle retired without losing everything it tested, and that list is the stop-sign.
- Every retirement removes the allowlist row in the same change (see bd-allowlist-stale-load-bearing).
- Anti-vacuous: a converted harness that ends with zero cases, or whose floor cases were dropped in conversion, is an ERROR.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RETIREMENT BLOCKER FOUND, and it is the reason the six stale allowlist rows read the way they do.

scripts/check.sh HARD-FAILS if a ported oracle is ABSENT. Six presence checks, measured 2026-08-14:
  493  [ -f scripts/validate_grounding.py ]     || fail 'differential oracle for validate-grounding'
  501  [ -f scripts/verify_orphans.py ]         || fail 'orphan gate required'
  678  [ -f scripts/verify_coverage.py ]        || fail 'differential oracle for verify-coverage'
  709  [ -f scripts/verify_objectives.py ]      || fail 'differential oracle for verify-objectives'
  760  [ -f scripts/verify_doc_consistency.py ] || fail 'roadmap-truth gate required'
  800  [ -f scripts/verify_injection_count.py ] || fail 'drift guard required'

So  of any of those six takes check.sh RED at a step that says the file is REQUIRED. That is why verify_orphans' allowlist row says 'check.sh hard-fails if it is absent, so it cannot simply be deleted' — the row is describing a real mechanism. What makes it stale is the CONCLUSION, not the observation: the mechanism was correct while the .py was the implementation and is now a lock holding a retired oracle in place.

NOTE THE TWO SHAPES, because they retire differently. Lines 501, 760 and 800 assert the gate is 'required' — written when the .py WAS the gate. Lines 493, 678 and 709 already say 'differential oracle', so somebody had updated the wording without noticing the check itself had become a retention lock.

THIS IS ALSO WHY RETIREMENT MUST BE ATOMIC, and it belongs in the acceptance: retiring an oracle is a FOUR-part change in one commit — delete the .py, remove its allowlist row, remove its check.sh presence check, and convert its harness cases to independent verdict assertions. Any three of those without the fourth leaves the tree red or leaves a lie in a registry. A partial retirement is worse than none, exactly like the partial domain bump bd-6ycw refused to make.

CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT ERROR RECORDED HERE, since it bears on the count anyone reads next: my first pass grepped 'python3 scripts/[a-z_]+\.py' and reported SIX load-bearing Python files. The character class has no digits, so it silently dropped smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py. The real number is EIGHT. A pattern that cannot match a legal name under-reports without erroring — the same shape as the sweep that could not see a bound behind a named constant (bd-8mjs).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED — the disposition table in this bead's acceptance must be built on the TRANSITIVE invocation set, not on a grep of check.sh.

I wrote this bead claiming eleven ported .py files are retired oracles because check.sh invokes none of them. That grep was true and the conclusion was false: check.sh calls six other shell scripts, and those invoke oracles check.sh never names. Falsified by the bd-8exw agent with a measurement, not an argument — check.sh:719 -> smoke_slo.sh:31 hard-fails on scripts/verify_bank.py's absence and :150 TIMES python3 scripts/verify_bank.py. A temp root without the file exits 2. The agent refused my retirement instruction on that evidence and was right to.

CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (scripts/*.sh + scripts/*.mjs, 13 python3 invocations):
  STILL INVOKED despite being ported — retirement BLOCKED until the invocation is repointed:
    verify_bank.py · verify_coverage.py · verify_objectives.py · verify_orphans.py
  ALSO INVOKED, and its allowlist row falsely says 'not on the check.sh path':
    build_learn.py
  PRESENCE-CHECKED (-f, hard-fails on absence) — a second, independent retention lock:
    validate_grounding · verify_doc_consistency · verify_injection_count · plus the four above

SO THERE ARE THREE INDEPENDENT RETIREMENT BLOCKERS, not one, and a disposition table must clear all three per file:
  1. is it still invoked, directly or transitively?
  2. is it presence-checked by check.sh or a nested script?
  3. is its differential harness all agreement-only, so retiring loses everything it tested?
Clearing two of three and deleting the file leaves the tree red or a lie in a registry — the partial-retirement failure this bead already warns about, with more edges than I knew.

ONLY ONE RETIREMENT HAS HAPPENED: build_units.py, verified afterwards to have no surviving invocation in scripts/ or crates/. It does leave dangling advice — two error strings and a generated_by literal still tell users to 'run build_units.py' (bd-stale-build-units-py-refs-milf, plus new instances in smoke_learn_v2). Structurally safe, cosmetically wrong.

METHOD FINDING FILED SEPARATELY as bd-transitive-invocation-blindspot-lcfj. The short form for anyone reading this bead: grep python3 check.sh does not enumerate what check.sh runs.

title: verify-objectives counts the file set, not the approved pool — FOURTH instance of the bd-8exw class
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_objectives.py and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs (the live gate, scripts/check.sh:711) enforce TWO floors against every loaded bank item, whatever its status. Neither file contains a single occurrence of 'approved', 'status', or 'is_approved'.

  verify_objectives.py:575-578    per-module floor: 'domain module {mod}: {have} items < min 1' (MIN_ITEMS_PER_MODULE)
  verify_objectives.py:641-655    per-topic floor:  'topic {tid}: {have} items < min {min_topic}' (--min-items-per-topic, default 1)
  verify_objectives.rs:192,1434   pub const MIN_ITEMS_PER_MODULE: i128 = 1;  if i128::from(have) < MIN_ITEMS_PER_MODULE
  verify_objectives.rs:1519-1535  the same topic floor

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT: cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids draws only status == approved. A module or topic whose entire stock is retired reports [ok] here while being unreachable by every learner. The error runs one way only — the file set is a superset of the drawable pool — so the floor can only ever be too generous. Fail-open.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 live: 804 files, 779 approved, 25 retired. No CURRENT breach at min=1 (no module or topic is entirely retired today), so this is a defect and not an incident — the same status bd-8exw had. It was rebased AFTER bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh landed and did not inherit the fix.

ACCEPTANCE:
- MIN_ITEMS_PER_MODULE and min_topic are measured against status == approved.
- Every count the report prints names its population, as verify-coverage and verify-bank now do ('N scanned, M approved').
- Anti-vacuous: zero approved is an ERROR naming the condition, distinct from the empty-bank leg.
- Known-bad: retire every item under one topic in a TEMP bank copy WITHOUT deleting a file -> RED naming the topic, the approved count, and the floor. That fixture leaves the file count untouched, so the current gate stays GREEN on it by construction, which is the proof the population changed.
- Python and Rust move together, PYTHON FIRST, and the differential is watched go RED before the port follows.

PRIOR ART TO COPY, NOT RE-DERIVE: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs count_approved/is_approved/status_is_known (bd-8exw, landed 2026-08-14) and crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_bank.rs cases retiring_in_place_* / a_bank_of_only_retired_items_is_an_error_in_both_never_a_pass.

title: verify-orphans: a topic referenced only by RETIRED items is not an orphan, but is unreachable — FIFTH instance of the bd-8exw class
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_orphans.py:159-165 and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_orphans.rs:386-390 (the live gate, scripts/check.sh:503) enforce an implicit floor of >=1 REFERENCING BANK ITEM per declared topic:

  'orphan topic {t!r}: declared in topics.toml, referenced by zero bank items'

Neither file reads 'status' anywhere. So a topic whose only referencing items are all retired is NOT reported as an orphan — while being exactly as unreachable to a learner as one referenced by nothing. The gate's whole claim is reachability, and it measures it on a population cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids never draws from.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: 804 files, 779 approved, 25 retired, 106 topics. Not currently breached (no topic's entire stock is retired today), so this is a defect, not an incident.

NOTE the neighbouring leg that is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed': verify_orphans.py:139 / verify_orphans.rs:341 'empty bank: zero items loaded (vacuous orphan scan is ERROR)' is legitimately a scan-set property.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The orphan predicate counts APPROVED referencing items. A topic with references only from retired items is an orphan, and the message says so ('referenced by 0 approved items of N referencing').
- Anti-vacuous: zero approved items is an ERROR naming the condition.
- Known-bad: retire every item referencing one topic in a TEMP bank copy WITHOUT deleting a file -> RED naming that topic. The current gate stays GREEN on that fixture by construction.
- Python and Rust move together, PYTHON FIRST, differential watched RED before the port.

PRIOR ART: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs is_approved/count_approved (bd-8exw, landed 2026-08-14).

title: Learner-facing web consumers draw from the bank manifest WITHOUT filtering status — retired items can reach a learner
description:
WHAT: web/data/bank_items_seed42.json ships all 804 rows including the 25 retired ones. registries/goldens-couplings.toml:499 records the decision and the obligation it creates verbatim: 'because the manifest ships 25 retired items, every consumer that DRAWS from it must filter on status itself, and .length is a FILE count that must never be quoted as the item count.'

MEASURED 2026-08-14: `grep -n status web/assets/js/*.js` returns only HTTP-status and CSS-class hits. NOT ONE CONSUMER FILTERS ON ITEM STATUS.

  web/assets/js/learn_units.js:110   quick-check pool floor: if (pool.length >= 2) return pool.slice(0, n);
  web/assets/js/quiz.js:578,146-148  const pool = filterByModule(bankParsed, moduleNum) — module only, no status; then sampleItems(items, seed, QUIZ_MIN=8, QUIZ_MAX=12)

WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLINGS: bd-8exw, bd-qqwc, bd-objectives-counts-retired-items-f996 and bd-orphans-counts-retired-items are MISMEASURED GATES — a floor checked against the wrong population, with no learner-visible effect today. This one is a LIVE PRODUCT DEFECT: the module-quiz and quick-check paths sample client-side from the full manifest and serve retired items to a learner. crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs:611-630 refuses to write a non-approved item into the MOCK pack, so the mock path is protected and these two paths bypass that guard entirely. A retired item is one that LOST a near-duplicate adjudication (cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED carries the argument per id) — serving it serves the copy that lost.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every JS consumer that draws from bank_items_seed42.json filters status === 'approved' before sampling, at the point of the draw, not at load.
- No pool floor (learn_units.js:110 pool.length >= 2, quiz.js QUIZ_MIN/QUIZ_MAX) is evaluated against an unfiltered array.
- .length of the manifest is never rendered or logged as an item count without naming the population.
- Known-bad: a browser/e2e or node smoke that seeds a manifest whose module-N items are ALL retired and asserts the quiz refuses rather than serving them.
- Anti-vacuous: a module with zero APPROVED items must be an explicit refusal, never an empty-but-green quiz.

Owner note: web/assets/js/ and web/data/ were owned by other agents during the 2026-08-14 wave, which is why this is recorded rather than done.

title: sample_mock.py draws a mock from the file set — will hand you a form containing retired items
description:
WHAT: scripts/sample_mock.py:63 load_items() globs bank/items/*.toml and filters nothing. Then:

  :178-180  pool floor  — if len(items) < n: print(f'FAIL: pool {len(items)} < exam {n}')  (n = exam_n_items 40)
  :151      breadth     — min_modules_represented 8, but the check is a no-op (soft warning, still returns)
  and sample() draws from the unfiltered set.

So both the floor and the DRAW are on the file set. cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids is the correct implementation and filters is_approved().

CONTAINMENT (why P2, not P0): registries/substrate_allowlist.toml:266 and goldens/PROVENANCE.md:22 mark this script FORBIDDEN on the golden path, and nothing in scripts/check.sh invokes it. It is a loaded gun on the shelf, not a live defect — but its OWN docstring documents `python3 scripts/sample_mock.py --seed 42`, so anyone following the file will get a mock containing retired items and no warning.

ACCEPTANCE — pick ONE and do it, do not do both:
(a) DELETE the script and its allowlist row. It is superseded by cdcp_assemble + `cdcp_cli export-web`, which are correct. Preferred: a second sampler that disagrees with the real one is a liability whatever it says at the top of the file. OR
(b) Filter status == 'approved' at load, measure the pool floor and the breadth floor on the approved pool, make the breadth check actually fail instead of warning, and make zero-approved an ERROR.

Either way the docstring must stop advertising an invocation that produces a wrong artifact.

title: smoke_learn_v2.py re-asserts build_units' file-set coverage floor downstream — it will stay green while bd-qqwc is wrong
description:
WHAT: scripts/smoke_learn_v2.py reads web/data/units_index.json — the artifact scripts/build_units.py and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/build_units.rs produce — and re-asserts floors over it:

  :51-56  if units and with_checks / len(units) < 0.8      (the 80% unit-coverage floor)
  :32-40  01-mission-critical >= 4 units, 06-power >= 3, unit_count >= 50
  :58-60  M01: min(len(check_item_ids)) < 2

Every check_item_ids list in units_index.json is built from the file set (bd-qqwc: build_units.py:262 load_bank() never reads status; build_units.rs has zero occurrences of approved/status). So a unit whose two check items are BOTH retired counts as covered, here and upstream.

This is not an independent defect — it is the downstream half of bd-qqwc, and it matters because it will re-bless the artifact: once build_units is fixed, this smoke must move in the same change or it becomes the thing that says the wrong number is fine.

RELATED, same artifact: build_units.py:493 writes '"bank_item_count": len(bank)' into units_index.json (currently 804). That is a FILE count published under a label that reads as the item count — the exact thing registries/goldens-couplings.toml:499 forbids for the manifest. web/data/units_index.json:2 carries it today.

ACCEPTANCE:
- After bd-qqwc lands, the 80% floor, the per-module unit floors and the M01 check-item floor are measured over units whose check_item_ids are APPROVED items.
- units_index.json names its populations: bank_item_count keeps the file-set meaning ONLY if it is renamed or paired with an approved_count, following web/data/coverage.json schema_version 3, which already does this correctly ('item_count': 804 alongside 'approved_count': 779).
- Known-bad: a units_index fixture whose units' check items are all retired -> RED.

title: export_anki.py ships all 25 retired cards into the learner's deck
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py:77 ITEMS_DIR.glob('*.toml') loads every bank file and never reads status; the deck is written from that set. :634 'FAIL: zero items to export' is the only count floor and it is >0, so it never fires and never will.

CONSEQUENCE: the shipped Anki deck contains the 25 retired items. A retired item is one that LOST a near-duplicate adjudication (cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED records the argument per id), so the deck teaches the copy that lost, alongside the copy that won — i.e. the learner drills a near-duplicate pair as if it were two facts.

Same class as bd-8exw but on an EXPORT rather than a gate: the population is wrong at the point of production, not at the point of measurement.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The deck is built from status == 'approved' only.
- The export names both populations in its receipt ('804 scanned, 779 exported').
- Anti-vacuous: zero APPROVED items is an ERROR distinct from 'zero items to export'.
- Known-bad: a temp bank whose items are all retired -> the export refuses, naming the empty approved pool, rather than writing a deck of 0 cards or a deck of retired ones.

title: Docs and artifacts advertise a FILE count as the drawable pool: README '~798 / ~20x', TESTING.md 'py-only', units_index bank_item_count
description:
WHAT: three prose/artifact surfaces state a file count where the claim is about the pool a mock is sampled from. None is covered by doc-facts.

1. README.md:61 — '| L2 bank pool (~798 / ~20x) | green (verify_bank + grounding) |'. Both numbers are wrong in the same direction: the file set is 804 and the DRAWABLE pool is 779, i.e. ~19.5x, not ~20x. '~798' is additionally stale. The '~20x' is a claim about what can be sampled, so it must quote the approved pool.
   Same in docs/PHASE-L3.md:16 ('L2 bank library ~798 items') and docs/FEATURE_SURFACE.md:9.

2. docs/TESTING.md:56 — the parity table row 'pool_min / domain_min / letter diversity | — (corpus policy; py-only) | yes' says these floors are Python-only. FALSE since the port: scripts/check.sh:481 runs `cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- verify-bank`. The doc misdescribes which implementation is live, which is how a reader concludes the Rust does not check floors at all. TESTING.md:63/67 also still route the reader to `python3 scripts/verify_bank.py`.

3. web/data/units_index.json:2 — '"bank_item_count": 804', a FILE count under a label that reads as the item count. Tracked as part of bd-smoke-learn-v2-derived-floor-a20t; listed here so the prose sweep does not miss it.

MINOR, same shape, worth one line rather than a change: scripts/validate_grounding.py:47/62 and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/validate_grounding.rs:185 set MIN_SCANNED_ITEMS = 40 and DERIVE it in a comment as 'ONE TENTH of verify_bank's pool_min_items = 400'. The floor itself is CORRECT — that gate lints every item on disk, so a scan-set floor matches its own population — but the stated derivation is a drawable-pool number, so the next reader will take it for a pool floor. Add a clause saying the two populations differ on purpose.

ACCEPTANCE:
- README.md:61 and the two docs quote the APPROVED pool with its multiplier, and name the file count separately if they name it at all (the live gate now prints exactly this pair: 'items=804 scanned, 779 approved').
- docs/TESTING.md:56 says which implementation check.sh runs, and 63/67 stop pointing at the oracle as the way to run the gate.
- Ideally doc-facts grows a row for the pool claim so prose cannot outrun the registry again — that is the standing rule and this line is a live counter-example.
notes: Additional measured fact for the same surface (bd-8exw, 2026-08-14): knowledge/bank_policy.toml declares pool_target_items = 800 and pool_target_multiplier = 20, and NOTHING ENFORCES EITHER — verify-bank gates only pool_min_items = 400. On the approved pool the target is now MISSED (779 < 800) while the file set still clears it (804), and the gate's printed multiplier fell 20.1x -> 19.5x. So README.md:61's '~20x' is not merely stale: it is backed by an unenforced config row AND measured on the wrong population at the same time. Either enforce the target or delete it — an aspirational floor no gate reads is indistinguishable from a comment.

title: verify-bank: a bank_policy.toml with zero [[domain_min]] rows checks zero per-module floors and reports PASS
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_bank.py and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs read [[domain_min]] rows from knowledge/bank_policy.toml. If the table is absent or empty, the per-module loop iterates zero times and the gate reports PASS with no indication that fifteen floors were not checked.

This is the empty-input-set-is-a-pass pattern: a policy that LOST its domain_min rows reports identically to one that enforced all fifteen. The live policy currently carries 15 rows, so nothing is breached today.

DONE IN bd-8exw (partial, deliberately): both implementations now print '  domain_floors=N checked (approved pool)' in the PASS report, so a zero READS as zero instead of as silence. That makes the vacuity visible; it does not make it RED.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is a policy call and not a code call: should zero enforced domain floors be an ERROR? Arguments both ways —
  FOR: 'an empty input set is an ERROR, never a pass' is standing doctrine, and this is a textbook instance.
  AGAINST: bank_policy.toml's [[domain_min]] is optional by design (the gate has working built-in pool_min/exam_n defaults and no built-in module list), and ~30 differential fixtures deliberately declare no domain floors because they are testing something else. Making it RED means every one of those fixtures grows a domain_min row.

ACCEPTANCE (whoever takes it, decide the question first and record the decision):
- Either zero domain floors is RED when bank/items is non-empty, with every fixture updated in the same change — or the row count stays advisory and the reason is written into the gate header so the next reader does not re-open it.
- If RED: known-bad is a policy file with the [[domain_min]] table deleted -> RED naming the condition, on a bank that is otherwise green.

NOTE the related, already-correct legs so they are not swept up: 'zero items loaded', 'zero approved items (N scanned)', and the per-file 'items[] yielded zero items' are all ERRORs today (verified 2026-08-14, exit 1 on both implementations).

title: scripts/verify_bank.py cannot be retired: scripts/check.sh reaches it through smoke_slo.sh, one level of indirection
description:
WHAT: during bd-8exw the instruction was to retire the oracle — `git rm scripts/verify_bank.py`, drop its substrate_allowlist row, convert the differential into direct Rust verdict tests — on the stated premise that 'scripts/check.sh does NOT invoke python3 scripts/verify_bank.py anywhere'.

That grep is TRUE and the conclusion drawn from it is FALSE. check.sh reaches the oracle one level of indirection away:

  scripts/check.sh:719        sh scripts/smoke_slo.sh || fail "L7 SLO budgets"
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:31     [ -f scripts/verify_bank.py ] || fail "missing scripts/verify_bank.py"
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:150    run_timed "bank_verify" "$VERIFY_MS"  python3 scripts/verify_bank.py
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:96-99  run_timed fails on a NON-ZERO rc, not only on the wall clock

So both the FILE and its VERDICT are load-bearing on the check.sh path, and slo.toml:18-19 budgets it as bank_verify_ms = 10000.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 rather than argued — a temp root carrying slo.toml, scripts/smoke_slo.sh and the golden fixture, with verify_bank.py deliberately absent:
  smoke_slo: FAIL: missing scripts/verify_bank.py
  exit 2

The retirement was therefore NOT performed, under the conditional in the same instruction ('do not retire the oracle if that leaves the Rust with a weaker net than it had'). Both implementations were fixed together instead, PYTHON FIRST, and the differential was watched go RED (exit 101, 30 of 35 cases) before the port followed.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this row: `grep -n python3 scripts/check.sh` does not enumerate what check.sh runs. check.sh dispatches to sh scripts and to cargo, and both can reach anything. Any future 'is this script still on the path?' question must be answered by RUNNING the entry point with the file absent, not by grepping the entry point.

ACCEPTANCE, in order:
1. Decide where the bank_verify_ms wall should be measured. The obvious answer is the Rust gate — `cdcp_gate verify-bank` is what check.sh:481 actually enforces, and timing the oracle budgets a program nothing depends on for its verdict.
2. Repoint scripts/smoke_slo.sh:31/150 at the built binary, and update slo.toml:18's comment. NOTE the budget will need re-measuring: the Rust is not the same wall as CPython + tomllib over 804 files.
3. THEN, and only then, retire the oracle: git rm scripts/verify_bank.py, delete its registries/substrate_allowlist.toml row (substrate_guard's stale_row_for_a_deleted_file_is_red makes leaving it an error), and convert crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_bank.rs from byte-equality against the oracle into direct assertions on the Rust's verdict.
4. CARRY EVERY CASE ACROSS. The 43 cases in that file are the gate's whole behavioural spec. Two need real thought rather than mechanical translation:
   - the_correct_letter_order_is_pinned_and_hash_seed_independent — its behavioural leg (stdout byte-equal across four PYTHONHASHSEED values) and its structural legs (the ordered tuple exists in the .py source and the loops iterate it, not the frozenset) are BOTH oracle-specific. The Rust has no equivalent hazard because ALLOWED_CORRECT is an array and the counters are BTreeMaps, but the replacement must assert THAT — an array-order pin plus a 'no HashMap in this gate' source check — or the coverage is lost, not carried.
   - an_oracle_raise_matches_on_stdout_and_exit_code_but_not_traceback_text — becomes a direct assertion that the raise paths emit empty stdout, exit 1, and a non-empty stderr naming the exception.

Both are carryable, which is why this is a scheduling problem and not a refusal.

title: export_anki.py ships 25 RETIRED bank items into the learner Anki deck
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py never reads BankItem.status. load_bank_items() globs every bank/items/*.toml (804) and load_seed42_bank_items() returns every row of web/data/bank_items_seed42.json (804). Both are 779 approved + 25 retired. --source bank and --source seed42 therefore emit 25 WITHDRAWN questions as Anki cards. --source keys is fine (40 drawn-form items, already approved-only by export-web's write guard).

WHY IT MATTERS: the Anki deck is a SHIPPED LEARNER ARTIFACT — registries/substrate_allowlist.toml calls it exactly that ('Load-bearing check.sh step: V11 Anki export, a shipped learner artifact'). Anki is a spaced-repetition tool, so this does not merely SHOW a withdrawn item once, it drills it on a schedule, off-platform, where no gate can reach it afterwards. An item is retired because a BETTER COPY OF THE SAME PROPOSITION exists (argument per id in cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED), so the learner memorises the copy that lost.

THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSUMER OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE. bd-7big (quiz.js draw) and bd-qqwc (units_index check items) are fixed 2026-08-14; learn_units.js pickItems topic/module fill was a third, found in the same sweep and fixed with them. This one is outside that wave's ownership and is filed rather than edited.

DO NOT FIX BY FILTERING THE PACK. web/data/bank_items_seed42.json must ship all 804 rows or client-side grading breaks: cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds those exact bytes to Bank::from_json_str which recomputes bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade hard-fails on a mismatch. Decision recorded in web/data/README.md and the web.bank-items-pack row of registries/goldens-couplings.toml. THE MANIFEST SHIPS WHOLE; THE CONSUMER FILTERS.

FIX: filter status == 'approved' in load_bank_items() and load_seed42_bank_items(). Report both counts separately (manifest rows AND approved pool) — collapsing 804 and 779 into one number is the exact confusion that produced this whole defect class.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No exported card carries a non-approved item id, for every --source.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a filter that removes every row is an ERROR naming the fault, never an empty deck. Zero cards exported is a FAILURE.
- KNOWN-BAD: retire one more item that the deck currently carries, re-export, assert the card is gone AND that the card count dropped by exactly one.
- The gate must be executable, not a source-level grep: scripts/smoke_quiz_approved.mjs is the shape (it imports the shipped module and runs the committed pack through it).
close_reason: Anki bank/seed42 export excludes retired+draft; 0/25 retired GUIDs in apkg; 28/28 diffs green

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-14. export_anki.py + cdcp_gate export-anki retain() drop status in {retired,draft} for bank/seed42 sources. Measured: python3 scripts/export_anki.py --format apkg wrote 779 notes; GUID ∩ 25 retired ids = empty. diff_export_anki 28/28 including the_shipped_deck_excludes_every_retired_item (default TSV == TSV after deleting retired TOMLs).
VERDICT: satisfied.

title: smoke_quiz_approved.mjs is BUILT but NOT WIRED into check.sh
description:
WHAT: scripts/smoke_quiz_approved.mjs landed 2026-08-14 with bd-7big. It is the enforcement point for 'no learner-facing surface draws a non-approved bank item' — it imports the SHIPPED web/assets/js/quiz.js and web/assets/js/learn_units.js and runs the COMMITTED web/data/bank_items_seed42.json through them, so it asserts what a learner is actually served rather than re-implementing the draw. It passes today (exit 0). NOTHING RUNS IT.

BUILT != WIRED. A gate nobody executes reports exactly like a gate that found nothing. The bd-7big wave could not add the check.sh line because scripts/check.sh was owned by a sibling agent that wave.
