  698: echo "==> cdcp_gate smoke-a11y";         cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- smoke-a11y     || fail "L7 a11y";          ok "L7 a11y baseline"

NOTES FOR WHOEVER LANDS IT:
- Keep the fail() strings byte-identical. They are the labels the check.sh log is grepped by.
- Both gates print their report to STDOUT and exit 1 on RED, exactly as the Python did, so no surrounding redirection needs to change.
- Do NOT delete scripts/smoke_a11y.py or scripts/smoke_learn_v2.py. Both are RETAINED as differential oracles, the way scripts/verify_coverage.py and scripts/build_units.py are. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_a11y.rs and diff_smoke_learn_v2.rs hard-fail if either file is absent, and their substrate_allowlist rows have been reworded to say so.
- Note the tension with the literal acceptance text on bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19 and .20, which says the .py and its allowlist row 'die together'. Every port from .6 onward retained its oracle instead. This bead follows the practice, not the text; if the epic wants the oracles deleted, that is a separate decision that removes the differential from five other ports too.

ACCEPTANCE: check.sh runs both Rust gates, neither python3 invocation remains, and a full check.sh run is green.

title: smoke_a11y raises on an undecodable or unreadable page instead of grading it
description:
REPRODUCED AND FILED under the port standard for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19. The Rust port reproduces the verdict and the stdout; it does not repair the behaviour.

WHAT: scripts/smoke_a11y.py calls path.read_text(encoding=utf-8) on the stylesheet and on every page with no try/except. A page that is not valid UTF-8, or that exists but cannot be read, raises UnicodeDecodeError / OSError and prints a CPython traceback instead of a FAIL row. Every other failure mode in this gate — missing file, empty file, missing marker — produces a clean named row under 'FAIL: smoke_a11y'.

The verdict is still non-zero, so this is not a vacuous green. It is a reporting defect and a byte-exactness cost.

COST TO THE PORT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_a11y.rs::undecodable_input_diverges_only_on_stderr is the ONE case in that file that does not assert the full four-tuple. It asserts stdout and exit code byte-exactly and requires both stderrs to be non-empty, because reproducing a traceback byte for byte would pin the CPython version and the absolute fixture path into the Rust. That test also asserts the two stderrs still DIFFER, so if the divergence ever disappears the carve-out fails loudly rather than sitting there as a permanently weaker assertion.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Wrap the reads so an undecodable or unreadable file becomes a named row, e.g. 'web/mock.html: not valid UTF-8 — refusing vacuous green'.
- Change both implementations in the same commit, or retire the Python oracle in it.
- Delete the carve-out from diff_smoke_a11y.rs in the same change and let that case run the full four-tuple.

title: differential_verdict_census.rs is BUILT but its mutation pair is unproven — the 2026-08-14 build queue never freed
description:
STATE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs and registries/differential_harnesses.toml landed 2026-08-14. The file compiles and was OBSERVED RUNNING once: 4 of its 5 tests passed and the fifth failed for a real reason — validate-grounding was dispatched by the binary with no registry row — which was then registered. Its per-harness census output matched an independent Python derivation of the same numbers exactly, harness for harness.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and must be before this gate is trusted:
1. A CONFIRMING RUN after the validate-grounding row was added. The last observed run predates that edit.
2. THE META-TEST PAIR. (a) tighten agreement_only_total_budget in registries/differential_harnesses.toml to the measured value and plant ONE bare comparator call into a harness — the suite must go non-zero and name the ratchet; (b) with that mutation STILL IN PLACE, delete the "assert!(total <= budget)" in the_agreement_only_ratchet_holds — the suite must return to zero. Then restore both. Without leg (b) the assertion is not shown to be load-bearing.
3. A second pair for the verdict-shape leg: register a wrong success token for one gate so the equivalence breaks — suite non-zero and names that gate; then delete the violations assertion — suite zero.
4. THE PLANT-IN-BOTH-IMPLEMENTATIONS DEMONSTRATION for the general class. The plant is written and was applied: scripts/verify_orphans.py line 120 "bank_dir = args.bank if args.bank.is_absolute() else DEFAULT_BANK" and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_orphans.rs line 321 wrapped so a relative bank_arg resolves to "bank/items" — the same defect, both sides: a relative --bank silently scans the default bank instead of the path given, so a run against a planted specimen reports on the live tree and calls it clean. The specimen and the control are captured: unperturbed, the oracle on a 805-item specimen holding one planted orphan exits 1, prints items=805, and names "zz-plant-orphan: unknown topic_id ...". The planted comparison could not be run because the gate binary never rebuilt.

WHY IT DID NOT RUN: the shared cargo build directory was saturated for the whole session — 60 to 64 concurrent cargo processes, load average 8 to 12, one sibling "cargo build -p cdcp_gate --tests" holding the lock for over 29 minutes. A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR did not escape it either. Both attempts were hard-bounded with "timeout" so the perturbation always restores; the tree was left unperturbed and verified so by grep.

NOTE: no check.sh edit is needed to wire this gate — check.sh line 563 already runs "cargo test --locked --workspace", which picks the file up. BUILT is therefore WIRED here; what is missing is PROVEN.

ACCEPTANCE: legs 1 to 4 above run with their real emitted exit codes recorded, on a machine where the build queue is free.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
FINAL STATE OF THE 2026-08-14 ATTEMPT, so the next agent does not re-derive the blocker.

THE BUILD EVENTUALLY SUCCEEDED. The gate binary rebuilt from the planted source at 19:29 with BUILD_RC=0, after roughly 32 minutes queued behind the swarm.

THEN EXECUTION ITSELF STOPPED WORKING. Measured 19:51 to 19:53: NO cdcp_gate binary can exec on this machine at all. Both the tree binary and a preserved copy time out at 30 seconds on the trivial "cdcp_gate list", which normally returns in well under a second:
    timeout 30 ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list           -> exit 124
    timeout 30 <preserved planted copy> list           -> exit 124
The stuck processes sit in state S with 0.0 CPU and 32 bytes RSS — created and never scheduled, i.e. blocked before main(). One had been in that state for 20 minutes. Environmental (25 to 76 concurrent cargo/rustc for the preceding hour, load average 8 to 12, two sibling agents dead of API errors), not a defect in anything built here.

CONSEQUENCE: the planted Rust run returned exit 124 with empty stdout, so the byte comparison against the planted oracle output could not be made. The oracle half IS measured and is recorded on bd-differential-shared-blindspot-4qje with real exit codes.

STATE LEFT BEHIND, all verified by grep and by git diff:
- Both perturbed files are restored and byte-identical to their git state.
- Their mtimes (19:52:57) are NEWER than the gate binary (18:24:34), so cargo must rebuild before anyone can run a stale planted artifact. That is the bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w rule applied in the restore direction.
- The planted binary is preserved OUTSIDE the repo at scratchpad/cdcp_gate.PLANTED (12,860,568 bytes) and is NOT the tree artifact.
- The specimen bank remains at course-engine/target/zz-demo/lZ1Ipm/items (805 items, one planted orphan). Under target/, build output, safe to delete.

TO FINISH ON A FREE MACHINE, roughly ten minutes of work:
1. cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test differential_verdict_census --test diff_verify_orphans  (the confirming run)
2. Re-apply the two-line plant recorded in this bead, rebuild, and run the two implementations against the specimen: assert byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit, then run the converted harness and assert it goes RED naming the specimen path.
3. The two mutation pairs listed in this bead body.

ALSO NOT COMPILE-VERIFIED, and this is the one real risk left in the tree: the edits to crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_orphans.rs were made after the last successful compile. rustfmt parses both files (exit 1 = formatting diff only, no parse error on stderr), so the syntax is valid, but nothing type-checked them. If they do not compile, the fix is local to that one test fn.

title: five gates never get their success token probed on the GREEN side — a wrong token would read as covered
description:
FOUND 2026-08-14 while building crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, and found by READING SOURCE rather than by any probe, which is the point.

The meta-gate asserts, per gate, that exit == 0 is EQUIVALENT to "stdout opens a line with this gate registered success token". Five of the nineteen gates are registered live_probe = false with a reason, so the equivalence is only ever exercised on the RED side for them:
  build-units, build-glossary-json   — they WRITE tracked artifacts (web/data/*.json); a probe must never mutate the tree
  install-hooks                       — writes into the clone .git; also empty_probe = false
  verify-injection-count              — requires --log/--readme; no argument-free invocation
  verify-step-count                   — requires --measured; no argument-free invocation

CONSEQUENCE, and it already bit: verify-step-count was registered with the token "verify-step-count: ok:" by pattern-matching the gates around it. Its actual verdict line is PASS (verify_step_count.rs:658, out.push_str(if failed { "FAIL" } else { "PASS" })). A gate whose token is never observed on the green side cannot have a wrong token detected — the red-side check "no token on a failing path" is satisfied for free by a token the gate never prints. The row read as covered while checking nothing. It was corrected by reading the source; nothing in the harness would have caught it.

This is the same failure this repo has measured elsewhere: LEG F of the meta-gate exists precisely to stop the token side passing vacuously across the whole roster, and it does — at least one gate must be observed GREEN carrying its token. But that floor is global, not per gate.

FIX, in increasing order of cost:
1. Per-gate green-side floor rather than a global one: every gate registered with a token must be observed GREEN carrying it at least once, or carry an explicit exclusion with a reason. That converts these five from silently-unprobed to declared.
2. Give the two argument-requiring gates a probe with minimal valid arguments built in a tempdir, so they have a green path a probe can reach.
3. Probe the two builders against a COPY of the engine root rather than the live tree, so their green path is exercised without writing a tracked artifact. The tree is roughly 9 MB, so a copy is affordable.

ACCEPTANCE: every registered success token has been observed on a green run at least once, or its absence is a registered exclusion with a reason; and a mutation pair proves a wrong token is caught (register a deliberately wrong token for one gate; the suite must go non-zero and name that gate).

title: web/data/units_index.json was regenerated at 18:17 by a probe, not by its owner — disclosure
description:
DISCLOSURE, so the owner of build_units is not surprised by an artifact mtime they did not create.

While enumerating success tokens for the verdict-shape meta-gate on 2026-08-14, the whole gate roster was run once against the LIVE engine root to see which gates print what on the green path. Two of those gates are BUILDERS: build-units and build-glossary-json WRITE tracked artifacts. Running them rewrote web/data/units_index.json and web/data/glossary.json at 18:17.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED: glossary.json is byte-identical to what was there before (it does not appear in git diff at all). units_index.json differs by 37 insertions and 36 deletions, and the diff is a FORWARD regeneration of the owner in-flight work, not a clobber of it — the new file carries "approved_item_count": 779, which is the field the current build_units.rs produces. It is the output of the tree as it stood, produced by the binary built from the tree as it stood. No unique information was lost; both files are deterministic outputs of the tree.

web/data/ was on this agent do-not-touch list and this was a mistake — a read-only survey that turned out not to be read-only, because two members of the roster are builders rather than checkers.

WHAT PREVENTS A REPEAT: the lesson is now encoded rather than remembered. registries/differential_harnesses.toml registers both builders with live_probe = false and the reason "writes web/data/...; a probe must never mutate a tracked artifact", and crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs refuses to run any gate on the live root unless its row says so, and refuses a live_probe = false row that carries no reason (a skip without a reason is a schema error).

ACTION FOR THE OWNER: none required if the current units_index.json content is what your gate produces. If it is not, regenerate it — nothing here depends on the 18:17 version.

title: Fleet-level cargo build-lock deadlock: 55 concurrent cargo processes, oldest 1h, zero CPU — verification work cannot run at all
description:
WHAT: measured 2026-08-14 19:20 on the live tree at /Users/josh/cdcp-self-study/course-engine. 55 cargo processes alive, the oldest started 18:24 (about one hour), every one at 0.0% CPU in state S, load average 9-10 with essentially no CPU work happening. Every new invocation prints 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' and never proceeds. Three separate attempts to run 'cargo test -p cdcp_assemble' timed out at 500-600s without reaching a single 'Compiling' line.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN CHASED: it blocked the re-run half of bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w. That audit needed to re-run previously-passed meta-test pairs under a FORCED rebuild to confirm their verdicts still hold, and could not, so the sample is reported as BLOCKED rather than as passed. A verification that cannot run must not be recorded as a verification that passed.

TWO WORKAROUNDS TRIED AND BOTH FAILED, so do not re-derive them:
  1. A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the agent scratchpad. Cold builds HANG at the first crates that carry build scripts (proc-macro2, libc, serde, version_check): the build-script executables appear as live processes at 0.0% CPU and 32 bytes RSS and never advance. Reading: build-script binaries under the scratchpad cannot be exec'd by the sandbox, and the failure presents as a hang, not an error.
  2. A full rsync copy of the tree with its own target dir. Same hang, same crates.
So an agent that needs an isolated build has NO working route today; it must contend for the one shared target dir.

RELATED, CLOSED, AND NOT THE SAME THING: bd-gl4j ('Concurrent check.sh runs corrupt each other — a false RED is indistinguishable from a real one') covered correctness under concurrency. This is LIVENESS: nothing is corrupted, nothing runs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A named cause for the stall (lock holder identified, not guessed), or a mechanism that prevents N agents from serialising on one target dir.
- A supported way for one agent to build in isolation — either a target dir location whose build scripts can execute, or a documented shared-target protocol with a build slot.
- Anti-vacuous: the fix is demonstrated with concurrent agents actually building, not with a single agent on a quiet machine.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of bd-syspolicyd-stall-blocks-all-builds-dp91, which a sibling filed for the same stall with the actual culprit named (syspolicyd pegged; every newly linked binary hangs in _dyld_start). I filed mine from process forensics before seeing theirs. All my evidence has been moved onto dp91 as a comment - the 32-byte-RSS build-script signature, the six agent target dirs, and the finding that the private-CARGO_TARGET_DIR workaround hangs identically and therefore is not an escape. Nothing is lost by closing this; dp91 is the one to fix.

title: smoke_learn PASSES vacuously when every domain is empty-ok (primary_notes_checked=0)
description:
FINDING (oracle defect, REPRODUCED not fixed — bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.17).

WHAT: scripts/smoke_learn.py reports PASS on a knowledge/domains.toml whose every [[domain]] row carries an empty primary_notes plus exam_weight_unknown = true. The report then reads:

  PASS: smoke_learn
    primary_notes_checked=0
    empty_allowed=N

Nothing was checked and the verdict is green. An empty scan set must be an ERROR, never a pass.

SECOND FACE OF THE SAME HOLE: web/learn/ and web/content/modules/ are only ever consulted per index entry. A tree with NO learn pages at all and no navigable domains is GREEN — the gate never scans those directories for their own sake, so it cannot notice that the Learn surface does not exist.

EVIDENCE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_learn.rs::an_all_empty_ok_registry_passes_vacuously_in_both_implementations pins the behaviour in BOTH implementations. Verified 2026-08-14: exit 0, stdout starts 'PASS: smoke_learn', primary_notes_checked=0.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: the Rust port cdcp_gate smoke-learn is measured byte-for-byte against this oracle. A port stricter than its oracle blinds the whole differential — a disagreement would then be indistinguishable from a port bug. The hole is reproduced deliberately and recorded here.

ACCEPTANCE (when the oracle is retired): primary_notes_checked == 0 with at least one declared domain is an ERROR, not a PASS; the change lands in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_learn.rs and the diff case above is converted from 'both agree it passes' to 'the gate refuses'. Note this is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a legitimately all-ops-adjacent course would go RED, so the floor should probably be 'zero checked AND zero empty-ok' or an explicit allowance row, decided when the oracle goes.

title: smoke_feedback_links PASSES with a 0% section-anchor hit rate when topics.toml is absent
description:
FINDING (oracle defect, REPRODUCED not fixed — bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.18).

WHAT: the only guard against a dead section-anchor matcher is

    if topic_anchors and int(topic_anchors.get('topics_with_anchor') or 0) > 0 and module_linked > 0 and section_linked == 0:
        errors.append('section-anchor hit rate 0% despite topics_with_anchor>0 — check matcher')

Its own precondition is derived from the same computation it is guarding. Remove or empty knowledge/topics.toml and build_topic_anchors returns topic_count=0, topics_with_anchor=0 — which switches the guard OFF. The gate then prints

    PASS: smoke_feedback_links
      section_anchor_links=0
      section_anchor_hit_rate=0.0% (0/N)
      topic_anchors topics_with_anchor=0/0

and exits 0. The entire L7-S2 section-anchor leg — what this gate is NAMED for — reports zero and passes. A guard whose precondition is computed by the thing it guards cannot fire when that thing is dead; it only fires when it is half-dead.

EVIDENCE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_feedback_links.rs::a_missing_topic_registry_passes_with_a_zero_percent_hit_rate pins it in BOTH implementations. Verified 2026-08-14: exit 0.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: byte-exactness against this oracle is the port's acceptance bar; a port stricter than its oracle blinds the differential.

ACCEPTANCE (when the oracle is retired): a missing or empty knowledge/topics.toml is an ERROR in its own right (the registry is not optional), and topics_with_anchor == 0 with declared modules present is an ERROR rather than a licence to skip the rate check. The floor must not be derivable from the same call that produces the number.

title: grep python3 check.sh does not enumerate what check.sh runs — the invocation set is transitive through shell scripts
description:
WHAT: the question "which Python is still load-bearing" was answered three times today by grepping scripts/check.sh, and was wrong every time. The invocation set is TRANSITIVE: check.sh calls six other shell scripts, and those invoke oracles check.sh never names.

THE THREE ERRORS, in order, all mine:
1. `grep -oE "python3 scripts/[a-z_]+\.py" check.sh` -> reported 6. The character class has NO DIGITS, so it silently dropped smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py. A pattern that cannot match a legal input under-reports without erroring.
2. Corrected to `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` -> reported 8. Still only check.sh itself.
3. Correct answer, sweeping scripts/*.sh and scripts/*.mjs -> THIRTEEN python3 invocations. Four ported oracles are still invoked transitively (verify_bank, verify_coverage, verify_objectives, verify_orphans), plus build_learn.py whose allowlist row claims it is "not on the check.sh path".

MEASURED BY A SUBAGENT, which is how it was caught: check.sh:719 calls smoke_slo.sh; smoke_slo.sh:31 hard-fails on scripts/verify_bank.py absence and :150 TIMES `python3 scripts/verify_bank.py` with run_timed failing on non-zero rc. A temp root without that file exits 2. The agent refused a retirement instruction on that evidence, correctly.

WHY IT IS P1: this measurement decides whether a file may be deleted. Acting on the wrong answer deletes a file the build needs, or leaves a Substrate Law violation in place believing it is already gone. It also fed a wrong instruction to four subagents mid-wave.

THE UNDERLYING SHAPE: the same one as bd-8mjs (a bound moved behind a named constant is invisible to a literal scan) and the DCG guard firing on prose. A scan that stops at the first file, or at one syntactic form, reports like a scan that covered everything.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A DERIVED, transitive invocation set: start at check.sh, follow every shell script it invokes, and report every interpreter invocation and every -f presence check reachable from it. Not a hand-maintained list — the hand-maintained list IS the defect (see bd-allowlist-stale-load-bearing-seq9, where six rows describe a status that stopped being true).
- The allowlist `reason` for every .py is checked against that derived set. A row claiming "not on the check.sh path" for a file reachable from check.sh is RED, and so is the inverse.
- Known-bad both directions: add a python3 invocation inside a nested shell script for a file whose row says oracle-only -> RED; mark a row load-bearing for a file nothing reaches -> RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a traversal that discovers zero invocations is an ERROR — check.sh always runs something. Assert a floor derived from the tree.
- Cover .mjs too: four node gates are on the path and js/mjs is deliberately outside the substrate floor (bd-yp9x).

title: BUILDER SHAPE: smoke_feedback_links writes topic_anchors.json before the verdict, so a RED run leaves an artifact
description:
FINDING (builder verdict-shape, class bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 — third instance found; REPRODUCED not fixed).

WHAT: scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py is listed in scripts/check.sh's own header as a step that MUTATES a tracked file (web/data/topic_anchors.json [M] regenerated). The write happens at source line ~291, inside the topic-anchor refresh block. The verdict is not decided until line ~450. Every error collected BEFORE the write — registry defects, results.js surface defects, slug-map drift in either direction, learn_md.js defects — reaches the write and then goes RED. So a RED run leaves a freshly regenerated tracked artifact behind.

THE GATE THEREFORE HAS TWO DIFFERENT RED SHAPES, which is what a builder audit has to know:
  * RED via a COLLECTED error  -> artifact IS rewritten.
  * RED via an EARLY RETURN (missing results.js, MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS not found, missing/invalid/empty keys, missing/empty bank) -> the return happens before the write, so a stale artifact survives untouched.

SUCCESS-TOKEN LEG, checked explicitly because three prior instances of that class exist: NO. Measured across four RED shapes — collected error, early return, missing registry, assessed-but-untaught — the oracle prints no PASS token on any non-zero path. The verdict is composed once at the end and the early returns print 'FAIL: smoke_feedback_links — ...'. This is NOT a fourth instance.

EVIDENCE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_feedback_links.rs — a_red_run_still_writes_the_artifact_in_both_implementations, the_early_return_legs_do_not_reach_the_write, no_red_path_prints_a_success_token. All three run BOTH implementations in SEPARATE tree copies and compare the bytes written.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: byte-exactness against the oracle includes the bytes written; moving the write after the verdict would make the port diverge from the oracle on every collected-error case.

ACCEPTANCE (when the oracle is retired): compose the artifact in memory, decide the verdict, and write only on the green path — or write through a temp file and rename only after the verdict, the shape scripts/verify_coverage.py already uses for --write-json. Either way a RED run must leave the tracked artifact exactly as it found it.

title: Port artifact: cdcp_gate smoke-feedback-links stats scripts/build_learn.py to reproduce the oracle's import-failure note
description:
FINDING (port artifact, deliberate — bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.18).

WHAT: scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py does not compute the topic map itself. It imports scripts/build_learn.py by path (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + exec_module) and calls build_topic_anchors. On ANY import failure it falls back to the existing web/data/topic_anchors.json and prints

    note: using existing topic_anchors.json (regen failed: <str(exception)>)

To be byte-exact on that path, crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs checks whether scripts/build_learn.py EXISTS and, when it does not, emits the same FileNotFoundError text ('[Errno 2] No such file or directory: <abs path>'). That is a Rust gate stat-ing a Python file — a coupling that exists only because the oracle's control flow depends on it.

BOUNDED DEVIATION, stated rather than hidden: only ABSENCE is reproduced. A build_learn.py that exists but raises (syntax error, missing build_topic_anchors, a bad knowledge/topics.toml reaching tomllib) produces a different note text on the two sides. Both still fall back, both still print a note, both still agree on the verdict; only the parenthesised reason differs. Pinned by crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_feedback_links.rs::an_absent_builder_module_falls_back_to_the_existing_artifact and ::an_absent_builder_module_with_no_artifact_is_red.

ACCEPTANCE: when scripts/build_learn.py is itself ported (it is a WAVE-3-shaped builder with no bead of its own — see the allowlist), delete the presence check and the note path with it, and convert the two diff cases into direct tests. Until then the coupling stays and this bead is the record of why.

title: smoke_feedback_links: int(row.get('module')) on a topic_anchors row is uncaught — a non-numeric module raises
description:
FINDING (oracle defect, small; REPRODUCED as a divergence rather than as a crash).

WHAT: in the per-key section-resolution loop,

    if a and (row.get('module') is None or int(row.get('module')) == mod_n):

int() is unguarded. A web/data/topic_anchors.json whose topic row carries module = 'six' (or a list, or a dict) makes the oracle raise ValueError/TypeError and exit 1 with a traceback and NO report. Reachable only through the FALLBACK path (an existing artifact plus a failed build_learn import), because a freshly generated map always writes an int or null — which is exactly why it has never been seen.

PORT BEHAVIOUR: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs treats a non-coercible module as 'does not equal mod_n' and carries on, so it reports where the oracle crashes. Both are non-zero on a tree where this matters only if something else is also wrong; on a tree where nothing else is wrong the Rust is GREEN and the oracle is a traceback. That is a REAL divergence and it is recorded rather than papered over.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE ORACLE: the oracle is frozen as the differential reference for the port.

ACCEPTANCE: when the oracle is retired, keep the Rust behaviour (a malformed module field disqualifies the anchor) and add a named error for it, so a corrupt topic_anchors.json reports instead of either crashing or being silently tolerated.

title: Two subagents died mid-task from API errors under fleet load; their beads need re-dispatch and their partial work needs adjudication
description:
WHAT: two of nine concurrent agents terminated early with "API Error: Connection closed mid-response" during wave 8. Their work is partially on disk and neither reported.

DEAD AGENTS AND THEIR STATE:
1. PORTS .14 smoke_diagrams + .15 smoke_learn_chrome. Left FOUR substantial files on disk, all brace-balanced (structural check: open==close in every one): src/gates/smoke_diagrams.rs 123807B, src/gates/smoke_learn_chrome.rs 32100B, tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs 50632B, tests/diff_smoke_learn_chrome.rs 27557B. Oracles untouched. NEVER COMPILED OR TESTED — the fleet was deadlocked on cargo when it died. build.rs globs src/gates/*.rs, so these files are ALREADY IN THE BUILD for every other agent.
2. STALE-BINARY TRAP AUDIT (bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w). Last words: "build scripts can not execute under the scratchpad sandbox. Reverting to the live target dir." Almost certainly left little, but the audit half — re-running previously-passed meta-test pairs under a forced rebuild — was never started, and that half is the one that tells us whether existing evidence is sound.

THE CAUSE IS MINE, and it belongs in the record: nine concurrent agents against one cargo target directory. Cargo serialises on a GLOBAL package-cache lock, so an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR does not help — measured by a sibling: 52 queued cargo processes, 0 rustc, lock holder asleep 47+ minutes. Under that, agents cannot build or test, so they cannot verify their own work; two handed back explicitly unverified suites and two died. Prior waves of six ran cleanly. The limit is not agent count in the abstract, it is CONCURRENT CARGO CONSUMERS.

ACCEPTANCE:
- ADJUDICATE the four orphan port files before anything else: they are in the build. Either they compile and their differentials pass — in which case finish the port properly and claim it — or they do not, in which case remove them and re-dispatch .14/.15 clean. Do NOT leave unverified generated code sitting in a globbed directory; that is a fooled certificate waiting to happen, since a gate file that exists reads like a gate that works.
- Re-dispatch bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14 and .15 and the bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w audit.
- RECORD A CONCURRENCY CEILING derived from the measurement, not from taste, and put it where the next controller will read it. Note the asymmetry: agents that only read files parallelise fine; agents that build or test do not.
- A blocked verification honestly reported is worth more than an assumed one. Both surviving agents that hit this said so explicitly and named what they could not run — that behaviour is correct and should be the documented expectation, not an apology.

title: Inventory rows owed in rebase_module_bounds.rs for two NamedBound constants in smoke_feedback_links.rs
description:
FINDING (sweep row owed in a file this bead does not own — bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.18).

WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs introduces two constants that the NamedBound detector in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs will match (a bare 13-16 bound to a name, whole line is the binding, inside the scanned crates/ tree):

    pub const MAX_MODULE_LINK_REPORT: usize = 15;
    pub const MAX_UNTAUGHT_REPORT: usize = 15;

NEITHER IS A MODULE BOUND. Both are REPORT TRUNCATION limits mirroring the oracle's missing_module[:15] and unmapped_modules[:15] slices: how many failure rows the report prints before it summarises the remainder as '… and N more'. They are ceilings on a list of FAILURES, not on the module set, and the module set in this gate is derived from knowledge/domains.toml in both directions with no numeric ceiling anywhere.

The third constant, MAX_MISSING_BANK_REPORT = 10, is outside 13-16 and needs no row.

ROWS TO ADD (a sibling owns that file; reported, not written):

  ("crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs",
   "pub const MAX_MODULE_LINK_REPORT: usize = 15;",
   Shape::NamedBound, Verdict::NotAModuleBound,
   "report truncation limit mirroring the oracle's missing_module[:15]; counts FAILURE ROWS printed, not modules, and is a ceiling on output length")

  ("crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs",
   "pub const MAX_UNTAUGHT_REPORT: usize = 15;",
   Shape::NamedBound, Verdict::NotAModuleBound,
   "report truncation limit mirroring the oracle's unmapped_modules[:15]; counts assessed-but-untaught FAILURE ROWS printed, not modules")

crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_learn.rs needs NO row: its only numeric constant is MIN_CONTENT_BYTES = 32, a byte floor on one file, outside the detector's 13-16 window.

ACCEPTANCE: the two rows land in INVENTORY and cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test rebase_module_bounds is green.

title: check.sh wiring owed: swap smoke_learn.py and smoke_feedback_links.py for their cdcp_gate subcommands
description:
WIRING OWED (scripts/check.sh is orchestrator-owned; reported, not edited — bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.17 / .18).

BUILT != WIRED. Both gates exist and are byte-exact against their oracles; check.sh still calls the Python.

LINE 651-653 today:

    echo "==> smoke_learn.py"
    python3 scripts/smoke_learn.py || fail "L5 learn smoke"
    ok "L5 learn smoke"

WANTED:

    [ -f scripts/smoke_learn.py ] || fail "missing scripts/smoke_learn.py (differential oracle for smoke-learn)"
    echo "==> cdcp_gate smoke-learn (L5 Learn surface)"
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- smoke-learn || fail "L5 learn smoke"
    ok "L5 learn smoke"

LINE 699 today:

    echo "==> smoke_feedback_links.py";      python3 scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py || fail "L7 feedback links"; ok "L7-S2 feedback section-anchor links smoke"

WANTED:

    [ -f scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py ] || fail "missing scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py (differential oracle for smoke-feedback-links)"
    echo "==> cdcp_gate smoke-feedback-links (L7-S2)"; cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- smoke-feedback-links || fail "L7 feedback links"; ok "L7-S2 feedback section-anchor links smoke"

The presence guards mirror the pattern already used for scripts/verify_coverage.py at line 677: the .py stays in the tree as the retained differential oracle, so check.sh must hard-fail if it disappears — otherwise the differential quietly stops being a differential.

HEADER LINE 76 STAYS AS IS AND MUST BE RE-READ, NOT DELETED:

    #   smoke_feedback_links.py    web/data/topic_anchors.json              [M] regenerated

The Rust replacement writes the SAME tracked file at the SAME point in the run (before the verdict — bd-feedback-links-builder-red-write-gbwl), so the mutating-steps table stays true; only the name on the left changes:

    #   cdcp_gate smoke-feedback-links  web/data/topic_anchors.json         [M] regenerated

smoke_learn needs no header row: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_learn.rs::neither_implementation_writes_anything asserts by whole-tree snapshot that neither side writes anything at all.

ACCEPTANCE: check.sh green with both Rust subcommands, no python3 invocation on either gate path, and the header table naming the Rust step.

title: grep python3 check.sh does not enumerate what check.sh runs — two oracles hide behind $CHECKER
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14. A survey concluded that check.sh invokes none of the ported .py oracles, by grepping check.sh directly. That is false twice over, and the second way is the interesting one.

FIRST INDIRECTION — check.sh calls other shell scripts, and THOSE invoke the oracles. A sibling falsified the original claim with smoke_slo.sh (check.sh:719), which hard-fails on scripts/verify_bank.py absence at :31 and times "python3 scripts/verify_bank.py" at :150.

SECOND INDIRECTION, found while correcting the first and NOT in the corrected count either — two oracles are invoked through a VARIABLE, so no grep for a .py filename anywhere in the tree can see the call site:
  scripts/selftest_doc_consistency.sh:49   CHECKER="scripts/verify_doc_consistency.py"
  scripts/selftest_doc_consistency.sh:144  python3 "$CHECKER" --root "$1"
  scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh:86   CHECKER="scripts/verify_injection_count.py"
  scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh:196  python3 "$CHECKER" ...   (also :202, :208)
Both selftests are run by check.sh (:767 and :802).

FULL TRANSITIVE CENSUS, resolved by following check.sh run_selftest / sh scripts/*.sh calls into each script and then grepping each for both literal and variable python3 targets:
  verify_orphans.py          INVOKED, 8 sites  check.sh:508 -> selftest_orphan.sh
  verify_objectives.py       INVOKED, 6 sites  check.sh:714 -> selftest_l7_objectives.sh
  verify_coverage.py         INVOKED, 3 sites  check.sh:683 -> selftest_l6_coverage.sh
  verify_bank.py             INVOKED, 2 sites  check.sh:719 -> smoke_slo.sh
  verify_doc_consistency.py  INVOKED, 1 site   check.sh:767 -> selftest_doc_consistency.sh via $CHECKER
  verify_injection_count.py  INVOKED, 1 site   check.sh:802 -> selftest_injection_count.sh via $CHECKER
  validate_grounding.py      NOT invoked — check.sh:493 is a "-f" presence check only
  verify_content_lock.py     NOT referenced by any script
  verify_knowledge_paths.py  NOT referenced by any script
  build_glossary_json.py     NOT referenced by any script
  build_units.py             RETIRED — file deleted, no surviving invocation
So SIX oracles are still invoked, not zero and not four.

THE GENERALISABLE FORM, which is worth more than the count: A GREP OVER AN ENTRY POINT DOES NOT ENUMERATE WHAT THAT ENTRY POINT RUNS. Shell dispatch is transitive and its targets can be variables. This is the same class as the message-keyed scan recorded in the bd-0czh comment in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs, where three fail-opens survived an audit because grepping for a message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. In both cases a grep produced a confident answer to a question it structurally cannot answer.

WHY IT MATTERS OPERATIONALLY: retirement decisions were being taken on the false premise. An oracle that is still invoked cannot be retired at any price until the invocation is repointed; deleting one would have turned check.sh red at a line nobody had connected to the deletion.

FIX: make the answer computable rather than grepped. A gate that resolves check.sh transitive closure — follow every "sh scripts/*.sh" and run_selftest target, resolve single-assignment variables, and emit the set of interpreters and scripts actually reachable — and asserts that every .py in the substrate allowlist is either in that set or explicitly marked unreferenced. Anti-vacuous: a closure that resolves to zero scripts is an ERROR. Cross-check: registries/substrate_allowlist.toml currently carries a row claiming build_learn.py is "not on the check.sh path"; scripts/_run_build_learn.sh:6 invokes it. That row is a live counterexample and should be the gate first known-bad.

ACCEPTANCE: the transitive set is computed by a gate, not by grep; every allowlist row claim about check.sh path membership is checked against it; the build_learn.py row is corrected; the gate is proven by a mutation pair.

title: FLEET BLOCKER: syspolicyd is pegged at 100% and every newly-linked binary on this Mac hangs in _dyld_start — no cargo build or cargo test can complete, for any agent
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 ~19:45-19:55 while working bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13.

SYMPTOM: every 'cargo build' / 'cargo check' in this tree hangs indefinitely. 29-32 cargo processes alive, ZERO rustc processes, load average only 3.9 — the machine is idle and deadlocked, not busy.

ROOT CAUSE, isolated to a 4-line reproduction that has nothing to do with cargo:

    printf 'int main(){return 7;}' > /tmp/t.c
    /usr/bin/clang -o /tmp/t.bin /tmp/t.c
    /tmp/t.bin              # never returns; killed at 90s

A freshly-linked 16 KB binary that does nothing but 'return 7' NEVER STARTS. 'sample' on a stuck process shows the entire stack as '_dyld_start (in dyld) + 0' — it is blocked before main. Meanwhile:

    ps -o pcpu= -p 522   ->  99.7 - 103.1   (/usr/libexec/syspolicyd)

syspolicyd, the Gatekeeper / provenance evaluation daemon, is pinned above 100% and is not draining. Every new executable queues behind it.

RULED OUT, each by measurement:
  - NOT quarantine: 'xattr -l' shows only com.apple.provenance, no com.apple.quarantine
  - NOT signing: ad-hoc 'codesign -s -' on the binary changes nothing (still 45s timeout)
  - NOT the inode: a plain 'cp' of the binary also hangs
  - NOT the path: rebuilt under $HOME instead of /tmp, same 30s timeout
  - NOT load: load average 3.9, no rustc running at all

BLAST RADIUS — THIS IS NOT ONE AGENT'S PROBLEM. 8 build-script-build processes belonging to OTHER agents are stuck in _dyld_start, one of them for 36 minutes. One of those (target/debug/build/cdcp_gate-*/build-script-build, ppid a sibling's 'cargo build -q -p cdcp_gate --bin cdcp_gate') holds the lock on the SHARED course-engine/target/debug/.cargo-lock, so every other agent's cargo prints 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' and waits forever. The whole cdcp_gate migration wave is stalled behind one hung OS-level exec.

LIKELY TRIGGER: N agents each linking fresh unsigned Mach-O binaries in parallel saturated syspolicyd's evaluation queue and it wedged. Same family as the known NTM/Gatekeeper trauma, in a new form — that one was quarantine on a downloaded cask, this one is provenance evaluation on locally-linked build artifacts.

FIX REQUIRES JOSH (restarting a security daemon is escalation-only, not autonomous):
    sudo killall syspolicyd     # launchd restarts it; releases the queue
then clear the wedged builds:
    pkill -f build-script-build
Consider also whether N-way parallel cargo across agents needs a build-slot lock (Agent Mail acquire_build_slot exists for exactly this) so the fleet stops generating hundreds of simultaneous first-exec evaluations.

WORKAROUND FOUND, and it is worth keeping: rustc ITSELF is an already-evaluated binary and runs fine. A crate can therefore still be TYPE-CHECKED without cargo, by regenerating the build.rs output by hand and invoking rustc with --emit=metadata:
    OUT_DIR=<dir with a hand-generated gate_modules.rs> CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=crates/cdcp_gate \
    rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type lib --crate-name cdcp_gate crates/cdcp_gate/src/lib.rs \
      -L dependency=target/debug/deps --extern toml=<rlib> --extern serde=<rlib> --emit=metadata
This type-checks. It does NOT execute anything, so it verifies compilation and nothing else — a differential harness still cannot RUN.

ACCEPTANCE: 'clang -o /tmp/t.bin /tmp/t.c && /tmp/t.bin; echo $?' prints 7 in under a second; 'cargo build -p cdcp_gate' completes; pgrep -f build-script-build returns nothing.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION from the bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w audit, measured 2026-08-14 19:20-19:45. I reached the same conclusion from the other end (process forensics, not syspolicyd) before seeing this bead, so the two observations are not the same measurement twice.

WHAT I SAW:
- lsof target/debug/.cargo-lock -> cargo PID 68231, later 68771 ('cargo build -q -p cdcp_gate --tests'), holding the shared lock for over an hour.
- Its child PID 27915 was target/debug/build/cdcp_gate-4df17c8fce7ff308/build-script-build: 23 minutes elapsed, 0.0 percent CPU, 32 bytes RSS, state S. 32 bytes RSS is a process forked and never through exec - which is _dyld_start, exactly as this bead says.
- At peak, 50 hung build-script-build processes across SIX different target dirs belonging to different agents (scratchpad target, tgt, t, tgt-sd15, tg3, tg2) plus the shared live target. Crates: proc-macro2, libc, serde, serde_core, version_check, generic-array - i.e. every ordinary build-script carrier, not one bad crate.
- Load average 9-10 with essentially zero CPU work: the machine looked busy and was doing nothing.

TWO THINGS THIS ADDS.

1. THE PRIVATE-TARGET-DIR WORKAROUND DOES NOT WORK, and six agents apparently tried it. A fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the agent scratchpad hangs at the FIRST build-script crate. Anyone reaching for isolation to escape the shared lock lands in the same stall and additionally leaves the shared lock held.

2. cdcp_gate/build.rs is not the suspect and should not be rewritten in response. It is pure fs::read_dir plus string building - no network, no subprocess, no stdin. It built normally in this same tree at 18:20 and 18:31, so the stall is INTERMITTENT.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN LOST TIME, and the reason a p65w agent cares: this bead's failure mode manufactures the exact defect p65w exists to prevent. An agent that gives up waiting for a build and reads its verdict off the artifact already sitting in target/ has fabricated a green. p65w's rule is that a verdict may only be read from a binary PROVEN to have been rebuilt from the source in front of you (crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/rebuild.rs). While this stall is live, that proof is unobtainable, so the honest response is BLOCKED - never a verdict.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY BOOKED: the re-run half of bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w could not execute. Five attempts, 240-600s each, none reached a single Compiling line. Reported as blocked, not as passed.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RECOVERED ~20:00 2026-08-14, about 25 minutes after it was filed. PID 522 is gone from the process table, so syspolicyd was restarted (launchd, or a human). Verified by the same 4-line reproduction that isolated it:

    /usr/bin/clang -o /tmp/t5.bin /tmp/t.c && /tmp/t5.bin ; echo $?
    -> 7, instantly

'cargo build -p cdcp_gate' then completed normally and the blocked work ran to green.

KEEPING THIS BEAD OPEN, at lower urgency, for the PREVENTION half. The trigger is still live: N agents each linking fresh unsigned Mach-O binaries in parallel is what saturated the evaluation queue, and nothing stops it recurring tomorrow. Agent Mail already exposes acquire_build_slot / release_build_slot for exactly this shape; a fleet convention that serialises cargo across agents in one repo would remove the trigger. Note also the amplifier: one wedged build-script held the SHARED course-engine/target/debug/.cargo-lock, so a single stuck exec stalled every other agent's build — a per-agent CARGO_TARGET_DIR would have contained the blast radius even while the daemon was wedged.

The rustc --emit=metadata workaround in the description is worth keeping regardless: it type-checks a crate without executing anything, which is the only verification available while exec is wedged. It is NOT a substitute for running tests, and this bead's original report said so.

title: HALT: syspolicyd wedged — no locally-built binary can execute; every Rust verification in this window is unsound
description:
WHAT: from roughly 19:00 MDT 2026-08-14, ad-hoc / linker-signed binaries — everything cargo produces — cannot execute on this machine. They block before main(). Apple- and Developer-ID-signed binaries are unaffected.

MEASURED, controller, independently of the reporting agent:
  ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list        -> exit 124 under timeout 20, ZERO bytes written
  /usr/bin/python3 -c print(...)        -> exit 0, works
  git --version                         -> exit 0, works
  br --version                          -> exit 0, works (Developer-ID signed)
  syspolicyd                            -> 99.1% CPU, 179m50s accumulated
Agent measurements from the same window: 75 cargo processes queued on target/debug/.cargo-lock with ZERO rustc running; the lock holder build-script-build at 47m18s elapsed and 0:00.00 CPU; sample(1) showing a single frame, _dyld_start — it never reached main. Every build-script-build across four different agents CARGO_TARGET_DIRs in the identical state. Processes at 0.0 CPU / 32 B RSS.
Tried and measured USELESS: a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR (cargo package-cache lock is global); xattr -c on the binary and its build script then re-exec.

THE DECISION IS JOSH.S AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE BLOCKING THE FLEET: `sudo killall syspolicyd`, or reboot. sudo is escalation-only under the standing grant; the controller will not run it.

WHAT THIS INVALIDATES, and this is the part that matters more than the outage. ANY RUST SUITE REPORTED GREEN IN THIS WINDOW WAS READ OFF A STALE ARTIFACT. A binary that cannot exec produces no output and no exit code; a harness that mistakes that for a pass, or that falls back to a previously built artifact, reports success for a run that never happened. Treat every Rust verification claim timestamped after ~19:00 as UNVERIFIED until re-run — not as false, as unknown. Three agents said so explicitly and unprompted, which is the correct behaviour and is why we know.

THE CONTROLLER MADE THE MATCHING ERROR IN THE OTHER DIRECTION and it is recorded here as the worked example: I ran ./target/debug/cdcp_gate build-units, saw exit 124 and zero output twice, and nearly filed a P0 claiming the gate hangs. It does not. It could not start. A wedged exec and an infinite loop are indistinguishable from the outside if you only look at the exit code and the empty log — you must check whether the process accumulated CPU. Mine had not.

ON RESUME, IN ORDER:
1. Confirm a locally-built binary execs: `timeout 20 ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list` must exit 0 with output.
2. cargo build -p cdcp_gate --tests, then re-run every suite any agent reported green after 19:00.
3. Adjudicate the four orphan gate files left by dead agents (bd-wave8-agent-deaths-redispatch-qb01) — they are in the glob and have never compiled.
4. Only then trust a check.sh run.

ANTI-VACUOUS NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS A GUARD FROM THIS: the failure signature is a timeout with an EMPTY log and no CPU accumulation. A gate that treats "no output" as "no findings" would have reported GREEN throughout this incident. That is the fooled certificate arriving through the operating system rather than through a gate.

title: BLOCKED, NOT PASSED: 13 meta-test pairs whose restore was never proven rebuild-safe are still unverified — the re-run could not execute
description:
WHAT: bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w required a sample of previously-passed meta-test pairs to be RE-RUN under a forced rebuild, to confirm their verdicts still hold. THE RE-RUN DID NOT EXECUTE. Five attempts on 2026-08-14 between 18:50 and 19:50, 240-600s each, every one stopped at 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' without reaching a single Compiling line. Cause is bd-syspolicyd-stall-blocks-all-builds-dp91 (syspolicyd pegged; newly linked binaries hang in _dyld_start), which held the shared target lock for over an hour. A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR is not an escape - it hangs at the first build-script crate, and six agents' scratch target dirs were observed hung the same way.

THIS BEAD EXISTS SO THE GAP CANNOT BE READ AS A PASS. 'Could not verify' is blocked, never green.

THE AUDIT ITSELF DID COMPLETE. Census of every recorded meta-test pair in the repo, from closed-bead close_reasons plus in-source records:
  19 recorded pairs total (15 named in 12 closed beads - bd-hdns and bd-g69j record the SAME 5 - plus 4 more recorded only in source headers).
  13 of the 19 mutated a file cargo COMPILES, so cargo's mtime staleness rule applies and the pair is structurally exposed.
  6 of the 19 are not exposed: 4 mutated shell selftests (interpreted, no rebuild) and 2 are Python-era (bd-1sd.5, bd-1sd.11, both predating the Rust gates).
  0 of the 13 exposed pairs recorded a restore method that provably defeats the trap. Not one names a touch, a git checkout, or a forced rebuild. Under fail-closed reading, unrecorded is exposed.
  RATIO: 13/19 = 68 percent of recorded pairs exposed; 13/13 = 100 percent of the exposed ones unproven.

  7. bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.11 - recorded 2 failures then 10 passed.

title: INCIDENT (RESOLVED, for the record): syspolicyd pegged at 100% stalled every ad-hoc-signed binary at _dyld_start for ~50 minutes
description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-14 ~19:50 MDT when syspolicyd restarted (pid 522 replaced by 41143). Filed after the fact because the br binary needed to file it was itself stalled by the condition. Filed so the signature is recognisable the next time five agents build Rust concurrently on this machine.

SYMPTOM: cargo made no progress in course-engine for roughly 50 minutes. At peak, 75 cargo processes were queued on target/debug/.cargo-lock with ZERO rustc running.

MEASURED, in order:
1. Lock holder cargo pid 68229, whose child build-script-build had 47m18s ELAPSED and 0:00.00 CPU TIME. sample(1) showed a single frame: _dyld_start (in dyld). It never reached main.
2. syspolicyd (pid 522) at 98-100% CPU with 171 minutes of accumulated CPU time. mds_stores at 1032 minutes.
3. EVERY build-script-build in the process table, across four different CARGO_TARGET_DIRs belonging to four different agents, was in that same state.
4. An already-built, previously-run binary showed it too: ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list produced no output and no CPU in 2m48s wall; a retry under timeout 25 returned 124.
5. Apple-signed and Developer-ID-signed binaries were unaffected throughout - python3, git, rustfmt and cargo itself all exec normally.

MECHANISM: cargo artifacts are adhoc, linker-signed (codesign -dv) and carry com.apple.provenance. Ad-hoc-signed binaries need a fresh execution-policy authorization from syspolicyd on every exec; Developer-ID binaries have a cached decision. Five agents each rebuilding cdcp_gate produce hundreds of fresh ad-hoc binaries per hour. syspolicyd saturated, every ad-hoc exec queued behind it, and the queue presents as a hang inside dyld rather than as an error.

WORKAROUNDS TRIED AND MEASURED USELESS:
- A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Same wedge; its build scripts were among the stalled.
- xattr -c on the binary and on its build script, then re-exec. Still timed out at 25s.
- Killing the wedged build-script (pid 68230) released the lock, but the next holder wedged the same way inside 60 seconds. Recorded because it was done, not because it worked.

WHAT ACTUALLY CLEARED IT: syspolicyd restarted. sudo killall syspolicyd is the manual form; launchd relaunches it.

PREVENTION WORTH CONSIDERING: exclude the repo target/ trees from Spotlight - mds_stores had burned 17 CPU-hours indexing them and was the other half of the load.

READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GREEN FROM THAT WINDOW: agents cannot distinguish a stalled exec from a slow one. Any suite reported green between 19:00 and 19:50 MDT on 2026-08-14 was read off a stale artifact and should be re-run.

title: Four uninventoried hand-frozen bounds from the concurrent Rust ports (rebase_module_bounds RED)
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs::every_hand_frozen_module_bound_or_table_in_the_tree_is_inventoried is RED. Four detector hits in the `crates` tree have no INVENTORY row:

  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs:557        [named-bound]   const MT_TEMPER_SHIFT_T: u32 = 15;
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_learn_chrome.rs:549 [numeric-bound] if decpt <= -3 || decpt > 16 {
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_learn_v2.rs:88      [named-bound]   pub const MIN_GLOSSARY_TERMS: i64 = 15;
  crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs:1289   [numeric-bound] x ^= x << 13;

All four files were UNTRACKED (git `??`) when this was measured on 2026-08-14 — they are new Rust ports landing in a concurrent wave. NOT ONE OF THEM IS A MODULE BOUND. On inspection each looks like a detector false positive of exactly the class the INVENTORY exists to adjudicate rather than to forbid:

  - MT_TEMPER_SHIFT_T = 15 is a Mersenne Twister tempering shift, a constant of the algorithm.
  - `decpt <= -3 || decpt > 16` is CPython's float-repr scientific-notation cutoff. There is already precedent for this exact adjudication: validate_grounding.rs binds the same cutoff and is recorded as Justified.
  - MIN_GLOSSARY_TERMS = 15 is a glossary TERM count. Precedent again: build_glossary_json.py and its Rust port both bind a glossary term-count floor and are recorded as Justified.
  - `x << 13` is an xorshift PRNG constant.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED: the rows are not mine to write. An INVENTORY row carries a REASON, and a reason is a claim about why a constant is legitimate in code the author understands. Writing four of them for another agent's in-flight files would be self-certification of work I did not author — the A9 failure ("metadata cannot mint truth; the server classifies, the author proposes"). The authors should each add their own row with a verdict.

NOT CAUSED BY bd-qqwc, stated because that wave touched this same file. bd-qqwc REMOVED three INVENTORY rows (the scripts/build_units.py prose bounds) when it deleted that script, and left this test GREEN at 40/40. The four hits above appeared afterwards, from the concurrent ports, and none of the three removed rows appears in the failure output. Verified 2026-08-14: diff_build_units 18/18; rebase_module_bounds 39 passed / 1 failed, the single failure naming only the four untracked files above.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the four carries an INVENTORY row with a Shape, a Verdict and a real reason, OR the value is derived from a registry instead.
- rebase_module_bounds is back to all-green.
- the_open_instances_are_named_and_counted stays at 0 open OpenInstanceNotMine rows, or the count is changed DELIBERATELY with the history note in that test updated to say why.

title: The overclaim honesty scan cannot tell an overclaim from a disclaimer of one — every compliant gate header trips it
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/repo_surface.rs::no_overclaiming_language_in_the_shipped_surface is a lowercase SUBSTRING match for "guarantee", "proves" and "makes impossible" over the shipped (non-test) region of every gate source. It cannot distinguish a claim from a denial of that claim.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: export_anki.rs:43 read

  //! It therefore does not "guarantee", "prove", or "make impossible" anything
  //! about the learner s experience.

and the honesty gate flagged it as an overclaim. That sentence is the gate AUTHOR DOING EXACTLY WHAT THE PROJECT ASKS — every gate is required to state its claim as a floor-raise plus what it cannot decide, and the most natural phrasing of "what it cannot decide" quotes the very words the scan bans.

SO THE RULE AND ITS ENFORCEMENT POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The standard says "say what you do not prove"; the gate says "do not write the word prove". An author who follows the standard trips the gate, and the cheapest way out is to write a WEAKER disclaimer — which is the opposite of what the rule wants. A gate that penalises compliance teaches people to stop complying.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SUBSTRING-SCOPE CLASS in this repo, and the pattern is now worth naming as a class rather than fixing case by case:
  - DCG blocked a bead-filing heredoc and a git commit under core.git:restore-worktree because the word "restore" appeared in PROSE inside a heredoc.
  - substrate-guard --prove-wired went RED on its own comment, which said "NEVER add a row for scripts/__cdcp_probe_unlisted__.py" — the comment read as the row it warned against (bd-ip10).
  - This one.
Each time the fix was to reword the prose, because narrowing a detector is weakening it and is escalation-only. Three reworded prose sites is a pattern, not three coincidences.

WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED: both export_anki.rs sites are reworded and the header now carries a pointer to this bead explaining why it is phrased oddly. That is a wart, and it will recur on the next gate that documents its ceiling honestly.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The scan distinguishes an assertion from a negation, OR the project adopts a sanctioned way to disclaim (a marker the scan honours, e.g. a CANNOT-DECIDE: block that is exempt from the word list, with the exemption REQUIRING a reason so it cannot become a blanket).
- Known-GOOD legs, and they are the point of this bead: a header that says "this gate does not prove X" PASSES; a header that says "this gate proves X" is RED. Both must be asserted, or the fix has only moved the failure.
- Known-bad: a genuine overclaim in a newly added gate is still RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: the existing floor (files.len() >= 8) stays; a scan that reads zero shipped regions, or that reads only test modules, is an ERROR.
- Sweep for the class: any other detector in this repo that substring-matches prose it did not author. Report the count; three known instances suggests more.

title: Six wave-8 gate ports were moved to .parked-wave8/ with no note, no bead and no owner notification
description:
COORDINATION FINDING, filed rather than fought over. Measured 2026-08-14 20:19-20:23 MDT.

WHAT HAPPENED: while I was mid-verification on bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19 and .20, both of my gate files and both of my differential harnesses were moved out of the crate into a new untracked directory course-engine/.parked-wave8/. The move happened twice, roughly four minutes apart, taking the smoke_a11y pair first and the smoke_learn_v2 pair second. At its widest the directory held six ports belonging to at least four agents: smoke_a11y, smoke_learn_v2, smoke_learn, smoke_feedback_links, smoke_diagrams, smoke_learn_chrome, each with its diff_ harness.

The parking itself is defensible - build.rs globs src/gates/*.rs, so one gate file that does not compile takes the whole crate down and every sibling with it. Quarantining incomplete ports to get the crate green is a reasonable integration move.

WHAT IS NOT DEFENSIBLE, and is the actual finding:

1. NO NOTE. The directory contains twelve .rs files and nothing else. No README, no reason, no date, no criterion for coming back. Nobody reading the tree can tell quarantine from abandonment.
2. NO BEAD. Nothing tracks that six ports are out of the build. The migration epic still reads as though they are in it, which is the exact failure mode that produced .19 and .20 in the first place - work that is invisible because the ledger does not mention it.
3. NO OWNER NOTIFICATION. No Agent Mail, no bead comment on the port beads. An agent that finishes a port and finds its file gone has to reconstruct what happened from mtimes, which is what I did.
4. NO SELECTION CRITERION RECORDED. My two were parked while compiling, passing and clippy-clean. They were taken because they were wave-8, not because they were broken. A quarantine keyed on a wave rather than on a compile result removes working code.

WHAT I DID: restored my four files by cp (byte-rewrite into the existing path, never mv - the stale-binary trap on bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w), verified the crate still builds, and measured: diff_smoke_a11y 13 passed, diff_smoke_learn_v2 15 passed, 41 lib tests passed, clippy exit 0 with zero warnings naming my files. I did not touch the other four agents' files, which are still parked.

ACCEPTANCE:
- .parked-wave8/ gets a README naming the reason, the date, the owner and the criterion for un-parking, or the directory is emptied.
- A bead tracks each parked port so the epic count stays honest.
- If the quarantine mechanism is kept, key it on 'does this file compile' rather than on which wave it came from, and notify the owning agent.

comments.text: DISPOSITION (ar39.3): STAY PARKED. After the gate-shrink ratchet (.1) exists, files here are EXTRACT-THEN-DELETE into product crates — never port-in-place into src/gates/. No owner may revive a parked smoke as a byte-exact cdcp_gate transcription.

title: Three wave-8 ports landed with 7 agreement-only differential cases, tripping the blind-spot ratchet
description:
WHAT: registering the three wave-8 port harnesses took the tree-wide agreement-only count from 28 to 35 and the ratchet in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs went RED, correctly.

MEASURED by the census re-deriving from source (the registry numbers are a BUDGET; the measurement is what the test does):
  diff_smoke_a11y.rs      15 cases,  1 agreement-only  (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19)
  diff_smoke_learn_v2.rs  32 cases,  5 agreement-only  (.20)
  diff_export_anki.rs     27 cases,  1 agreement-only  (.13)

THE BUDGET WAS NOT RAISED, DELIBERATELY. The ratchet says the blind spot may fall and may not rise, and it did rise — that is a true statement about the repo, not a gate being fussy. Raising a budget to get green is weakening a gate, which is escalation-only here. The three rows carry the correct measured `cases` and a budget of 0, so the tree is RED on exactly this, with the reason recorded.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO PAY IT. An agreement-only case asserts that two implementations produce the same bytes and says NOTHING about whether those bytes are right. Measured precedent, verify_objectives: `--min-items-per-topic 0` printed "primary_topics=106 covered=106 shortfalls=0 mode=strict, EXIT 0" — 106 of 106 topics covered with not one comparison performed — and its harness PASSED that exact case for weeks because both sides produced the same wrong answer. Every case in this count is one that no shared defect can fail.

AND THESE SEVEN EVAPORATE ON RETIREMENT. The standing policy retires an oracle at port time; a case saying only "the two sides agree" is worth nothing once there is one side. So these seven are simultaneously the blind spot AND the retirement cost for three oracles we intend to retire.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the 7 asserts an INDEPENDENT verdict: what the correct answer IS (exit code plus a required substring, or the resolved path plus the item count plus the named finding), checkable if only one implementation existed.
- The recipe that worked on diff_verify_orphans.rs (7 -> 0 in one wave) is the precedent: rewriting the assertion is NOT enough, because a case running against the GREEN live tree has no finding to suppress. Point the input at a tree with a PLANTED finding, then assert the resolved path, the item COUNT (this is what catches a silent fallback), and the named finding.
- The ratchet returns to 28 or below without its budgets being edited upward.
- Known-bad: plant a defect in BOTH implementations of one converted case and assert it now fails. Under the old assertion it passed.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a converted case that ends up asserting nothing about output, or that compares an artifact neither side wrote, is an ERROR.

title: smoke_diagrams: an unclosed honesty-banner element swallows the rest of the page
description: WHAT: `scripts/smoke_diagrams.py`'s DiagramHTML tracks banner nesting with a counter that is only decremented by a NON-VOID end tag. If the element carrying class="honesty-banner" is never closed, _depth stays >= 1 to end of file and EVERY subsequent text node on the page is appended to the banner text. WHY IT MATTERS: the disclaimer predicate (\bnot\b AND 'certif') then reads the WHOLE PAGE, which is the exact fooling shape the current version of this gate was written to close — its header says 'parses the HTML for the honesty-banner element ... instead of grepping the file for not/certif. A file whose whole content is `not certif fire-sequence` now fails.' An unclosed banner reopens that door: a hollow banner plus an unrelated 'this does not grant certification' footer elsewhere in the document scores GREEN. MEASURED 2026-08-14 during bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14. The same counter also cannot be closed by an unbalanced </br>, because handle_endtag returns before touching _depth for anything in VOID_TAGS. REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED: the Rust port cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams reproduces it and tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs pins it in the adversarial table ('an unclosed banner swallows the rest of the page'), because a port stricter than its oracle blinds the differential. ACCEPTANCE: decide the correct behaviour (candidates: cap the banner at the first end tag whose name matches the opening tag; or treat depth>0 at EOF as a FAIL 'honesty-banner is never closed'), change BOTH implementations in the same commit, and convert the pinning case to assert the new verdict.

title: smoke_diagrams: a markdown table inside a code fence is adopted as the inventory
description: WHAT: parse_registry() locates the inventory as 'the first line whose strip() == "## Inventory", then the first line after it that split_row() accepts'. It has no markdown model, so a pipe table inside a fenced code block between the heading and the real table is adopted AS the inventory. MEASURED 2026-08-14: a registry holding an illustrative two-column table in a fence reports 'ERROR: inventory columns changed: expected [...], found [\'ID\', \'Title\']' and exits 2 while the real seven-row table below is never read. WHY IT MATTERS: today it fails CLOSED (ERROR, exit 2), which is the safe direction, so this is a usability and honesty defect rather than a fooled certificate — but a fenced example whose columns happen to match EXPECTED_COLUMNS would be parsed as the check set, and then the fence decides which diagrams are checked. docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md already contains a fenced block (the Validation section), which is why this is reachable rather than theoretical. REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED in cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams; pinned in tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs registry case 23. ACCEPTANCE: skip fenced regions when locating the table (track ``` toggles while scanning), in BOTH implementations in one commit, and repoint the pinning case at the new verdict.

title: smoke_diagrams: the 'unparseable HTML' branch is unreachable dead code
description: WHAT: check_diagram() wraps parser.feed(text); parser.close() in 'except Exception as exc: return [f"{did}: unparseable HTML: {exc}"]'. CPython's html.parser is a tolerant tokenizer with no error recovery to fail: every parse helper returns an index or -1, goahead()'s only assert is on a branch reachable solely through interesting.search() lying, and no input reaches it. MEASURED 2026-08-14 by reading Lib/html/parser.py at 3.14.2 and by the 41-row adversarial table in tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs, none of which produces the message. WHY IT MATTERS: it reads as coverage of a class that has none. A reviewer counting the gate's failure modes counts one that cannot fire, and the message is untested by construction — there is no input that can exercise it, so it could be wrong in any way and nothing would notice. The Rust port cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams has no counterpart and says so in its evaluate() header. ACCEPTANCE: delete the try/except from the oracle (leaving feed/close bare), or replace it with a branch that CAN fire, in the same commit as any Rust change. If deleted, the port's residual-divergence note goes with it.

title: smoke_diagrams: EXPECTED_PRESENT is now pinned in two files that can drift apart
description: WHAT: the present-diagram count is pinned as EXPECTED_PRESENT = 7 in scripts/smoke_diagrams.py AND as pub const EXPECTED_PRESENT: usize = 7 in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_diagrams.rs. WHY IT MATTERS: shipping an eighth diagram now needs THREE edits in one commit (registry row, python pin, rust pin) and nothing checks that the two pins agree. If only one is raised, tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs goes RED on every case that reaches the count — which is loud, and is the mitigation today — but the differential is exactly the thing scheduled for retirement when the oracle is deleted, so the protection has an expiry date. This is the same shape as bd-8mjs/bd-inventory-row-smoke-learn-v2-42hk: one number, three spellings, no derivation. ACCEPTANCE: either (a) derive the pin from the registry's own stated count so there is one source, or (b) add a leg to tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs that reads the literal out of the oracle source and asserts it equals cdcp_gate's constant, so the two cannot part company silently. Do NOT simply delete one pin: the pin is what makes a row leaving the PRESENT set RED rather than invisible.

title: smoke_diagrams: status normalisation strips ALL asterisks and backticks, so interior markup is accepted
description: WHAT: the Status cell is normalised with raw_status.replace('*','').replace('`','').strip().lower() before it is matched against the closed enum. The replacements are unanchored, so 'pre*sent', '``pr`esent``', '**p**r**e**s**e**n**t**' and '*present' all normalise to 'present' and are accepted as PRESENT rows. WHY IT MATTERS: docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md rule 3 states the Status column is a closed enum spelled '**present**' or 'planned' and that 'any other spelling is an ERROR, never a silent exclusion'. The normaliser is looser than the documented contract in the OTHER direction — it silently INCLUDES spellings the document forbids. Low severity (a typo that normalises to a valid status still selects the row for checking, which is fail-closed), but the gate's own docstring claims a closed enum and the code implements a fuzzy one. MEASURED 2026-08-14 during bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14; reproduced in cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams and pinned in tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs registry case 13 ('status spellings that normalise to present'). ACCEPTANCE: decide whether the enum is closed or normalised, make the docstring and the code agree, change both implementations in one commit, and repoint the pinning case.

title: Wire check.sh:697 to cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams (BUILT != WIRED)
description: WHAT: cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams landed byte-exact 2026-08-14 (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14) and check.sh:697 still runs 'python3 scripts/smoke_diagrams.py'. The port owner does not own check.sh. WHY IT MATTERS: BUILT != WIRED. Until the line is repointed the Rust gate runs only under cargo test, the substrate allowlist row for scripts/smoke_diagrams.py cannot lose its INVOCATION blocker, and registries/differential_harnesses.toml's retirement cost sheet keeps this oracle in the 'blocked on both' column. EXACT LINE, replacing check.sh:697 verbatim: echo "==> cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams";   cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- smoke-diagrams || fail "M8-C diagrams";    ok "M8-C diagrams smoke" — this matches the house style of the three cdcp_gate invocations immediately above it (build-units, build-glossary-json, smoke-learn-v2). ACCEPTANCE: check.sh runs the Rust subcommand, the whole script is green, no python3 invocation of smoke_diagrams.py survives anywhere reachable from check.sh (follow the run_selftest / sh scripts/*.sh calls, not just grep), and the allowlist reason for scripts/smoke_diagrams.py drops its invocation-blocker sentence.

title: export_anki.rs: its csv_row doc comment fails cargo test --doc and it carries four clippy warnings
description: WHAT (found 2026-08-14 by bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14 while running the full crate suite; NOT owned by that bead). Two independent failures in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs, both of which make scripts/check.sh RED as it is written today: (1) 'cargo test -p cdcp_gate --doc' FAILS. The doc comment on csv_row (around line 998) contains an INDENTED block that rustdoc compiles as Rust: `csv.writer(s, lineterminator=...).writerow([...])` and `-> '"a\\rb",x\\n'`. rustc rejects it with 'character literal may only contain one codepoint'. Fix: fence it as ```text (or ```ignore), or de-indent it out of code-block position. (2) 'cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings' — which check.sh:562 runs as a HARD GATE — reports four warnings in this file and nothing else in the crate: export_anki.rs:930 'this match can be collapsed into the outer match', :1040 'used consecutive str::replace call', :1162 and :1171 'consider using sort_by_key'. WHY IT MATTERS: check.sh:562 fails the whole build on any clippy warning, and the doctest failure is invisible to 'cargo test --lib --tests', which is how it survived — the suite reports 29 green targets and then the doc target fails last. MEASURED: 'cargo test -p cdcp_gate --lib --tests' exits 0; 'cargo test -p cdcp_gate' exits 101 solely on the doctest; 'cargo clippy -p cdcp_gate --all-targets' names only export_anki.rs after the smoke-diagrams port cleaned its own four. ACCEPTANCE: both commands green with no other file touched.

title: EPIC: Invert the graph — the engine is the deliverable and cdcp_gate must shrink
description:
WHAT: reverse the size inversion. cdcp_gate is 64,955 lines; ALL product Rust combined (core+grade+bank+assemble+cli+wasm+registry_check) is 6,417. The checker is 10x the thing it checks and 267x the grader it exists to protect.

WHY NOW, MEASURED 2026-08-14:
- One port landed today replacing 362 lines of Python with 6,586 lines of Rust — MORE THAN THE ENTIRE PRODUCT — of which 3,106 are py_compat.rs, a transcription of CPython html.parser internals (2,231 entity mappings, 737 printability ranges) so a diagram smoke test can be byte-identical to a retired oracle. That file alone is 18x cdcp_grade.
- Our own tick ledger convicts the campaign: of T1..T8, exactly TWO changed what a learner experiences (T1 unapproved items cannot reach a mock exam; T6 module-15 progress reaches the learner). Six were guards denying other guards. All eight were logged GREEN.
- The repo already wrote the doctrine it then violated: build_units.rs header says "a differential is not correctness"; FRANKEN-EXTRACT.md Doctrine #0 says "process work earns zero capability credit"; the flywheel charter says a gate that never denies scores ZERO. The standing P0 epic is to write seventeen more of them.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE METRIC, NOT THE ROADMAP. Every port bead currently passes when a Rust file exists that agrees byte-for-byte with a retired Python file. Nothing in that acceptance mentions the product, so the cheapest way to pass is to add lines to cdcp_gate. Change the acceptance to "cdcp_gate got SMALLER" and the same work routes into extraction instead of transcription.

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT: a roadmap v5, a new charter, or a rewrite. CHARTER.md and FEATURE_SURFACE.md are edited in place. No crate is created that does not remove more lines than it adds.

THE GATE CAMPAIGN WAS NOT WASTE, and the sequencing must not pretend it was. It found the single most learner-visible defect anyone has found here (learners SCORED on withdrawn questions, SRS-scheduled and mastery-weighted), the retired-items-in-units_index hole, the module-15 hub gap, and today an unclosed-banner hole that reopens the whole-file-substring fooling path. The by-catch is real. The net weighs more than the boat.

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EPIC:
- cdcp_gate line count is FALLING and mechanically cannot rise (child .1).
- No src/gates/*.rs compiles a product artifact; build_units, build_glossary and export_anki live in a product crate the gate CALLS.
